# Model-Facing Subagent Tools in 74 Agent Harnesses: Names, Descriptions, Schemas, and Semantics

Report type: informational / status. It records what each harness gives the model and makes no comparisons, rankings, or recommendations.

## Summary: 74 harnesses give the model 301 subagent tools

This catalog records every model-facing subagent tool found in 74 agent harnesses as of 2026-10-10. For each tool it gives the exact name, the description and parameter schema copied verbatim from the source, and two to five sentences on what a call does. Thirty-two harnesses are closed source and 42 are open source. Fifteen of the open-source entries are agent frameworks or SDKs, which count as harnesses here because they give the model subagent tools. Together the entries hold 301 tool subsections. A closing section names 53 more products and features in one sentence each: 35 with no model-facing subagent tool, and 18 with a delegation feature whose tool was not captured.

A subagent tool here is any tool that lets a model start another agent, delegate a task to one, hand control to one, or define one for later use. The companions count too: tools that read a subagent's output, wait for it, check its status, message it, list subagents, stop it, or let the subagent report back. Background-shell tools appear only where the same tool also manages subagents.

Entries are grouped into closed source and then open source, alphabetically within each part. Each entry opens with four metadata bullets: openness, the version or commit it describes, the target models, and its sources with a quality rating. One subsection per tool follows, in a fixed role order. The next section explains that layout and the conventions used inside verbatim text.

Every source was read or fetched on 2026-10-10. Open-source entries describe code at pinned commits; the oldest is Microsoft AutoGen's, dated 2026-04-06. Closed-source entries name the version, bundle, or capture date they describe, and several rest on extracted prompts from 2025. For 53 tools the description or the schema is partial or was not captured; the section on partial and missing captures lists them. Nothing is blocking: each gap is marked where it occurs.

## How each entry is laid out

**Metadata.** Each entry starts with the harness name as a heading and four bullets:

- Openness: open source or closed source, with the license where the sources give it.
- Version described: the release, version, commit and date, or capture date the entry describes.
- Target models: the model family or families, or "not stated in the sources".
- Sources: each source with its title, URL, quality rating, and date or version.

A short lead paragraph may follow. It names the tools the model sees, how they relate, and any gating such as feature flags, model ids, or versions.

**Tool headings.** Each tool subsection is headed by the exact name the model sees, with case, separators, and namespace as the source shows them, such as `Agent`, `collaboration.spawn_agent`, or `muse.subagent_spawn`. A tool whose name the framework generates per agent is written as a pattern with angle brackets, such as `transfer_to_<agent_name>` or `subagent_<name>`; its semantics give the naming rule. The tool's roles follow in parentheses. Where a harness has two live generations or surfaces, the generation follows a semicolon, as in `(spawn; V1)` and `(spawn; V2)`, and each generation's tools appear in role order, first generation first.

**Roles and their order.** Tools appear in this order within an entry, and a tool with several roles sits at the position of its first role:

- spawn: starts a subagent or delegates a task to one, including agent-as-tool designs where each child is its own tool.
- handoff: moves the conversation to another agent; control does not come back to the caller as a tool result.
- define: registers a reusable subagent for later spawning.
- output: reads a subagent's output or result.
- wait: blocks until one or more subagents finish or send something.
- status: reports whether a subagent is still running.
- message: sends a follow-up or steering message to a subagent.
- list: lists running subagents or the agent types available.
- cancel: stops or interrupts a subagent.
- return: a tool the subagent itself calls to report back to its parent.

One tool in Microsoft Agent Framework has the role "clear", because it removes a finished task from the list without stopping anything; it appears last in that entry.

**Description.** The description appears in a text block, copied verbatim. "Description (partial, verbatim)" marks a block where only part was captured, and a sentence after the block says what is missing. "Description: not captured." means no source gave it. For agent-as-tool designs whose description is the developer's own text, the entry says so, or shows the source expression that supplies the text, instead of quoting one.

**Parameters.** The schema appears in the source's own form: JSON Schema, a TypeScript type, a zod schema from a shipped bundle, a Python or pydantic model, a Rust type, or a protocol buffer message. The label names the form and the source. Where a source gives only parameter names and types, the entry renders them as a list labeled "names and types only". "Partial" and "not captured" work as they do for descriptions.

**Source lines.** A line after each block names the file or page, the commit or version, the quality rating, and the date. The quality ratings are:

- official doc, official changelog, official blog: the vendor's own documentation, changelog, or blog.
- source at commit: a file in a public repository at a pinned commit, including vendor cookbook and skill files.
- SDK type file: a vendor's TypeScript declaration file published on npm.
- shipped bundle: a vendor package unpacked and searched at a stated version.
- first-hand: observed directly on 2026-10-10, either a tool definition or tool result that a Cursor agent session received, or repository metadata (license, archive status, dates) read from GitHub.
- extracted prompt: a system prompt or tool list in a public collection of extracted prompts, at a pinned commit.
- third-party capture, third-party reverse engineering, third-party blog: an exported session or request capture, an analysis of a shipped binary, or an outside write-up.
- forum or issue: a forum post, GitHub issue, or pull request.
- search snippet: text seen only in a search result.

**Semantics.** Two to five sentences state facts from the sources: whether the call blocks or runs in the background and which is the default; what it returns and when; how ids work; how completion reaches the parent, with exact wording in quotation marks where captured; limits such as timeouts with their units; and rename history with dates. A fact from a source not named in that tool's source lines carries a short parenthetical cite that matches the entry's source list. Removed tools get no subsection; the semantics of the tool that replaced them give the removal and its date. Where sources disagree, the entry states both versions with their sources.

**Verbatim text.** Inside copied text, an em dash is rendered as " - ", an en dash as "-", and a double hyphen used as punctuation as " - ", and emoji are dropped. Command-line flags, code operators, identifiers, and placeholders such as `${...}` or `{available_models_description}` keep the source's spelling.

**Counting.** The tool count is the number of tool subsections. A tool shown in two generations, or in two language versions of one framework, counts once per subsection.

## Part 1: Closed-source harnesses (32 entries)

These 32 harnesses are closed source in the versions described. Most entries rest on official docs, shipped bundles, first-hand tool definitions, and extracted prompts, each rated in its source line. Three entries also draw on public material and say so in their Openness bullet: Warp (public client and protocol repositories), xAI Grok Build (CLI published under Apache-2.0), and Z.ai ZCode (an unverified report of an open-source release). The Claude Agent SDK gives the model the same tools as Claude Code and is described inside that entry.

### Amp

- Openness: closed source
- Version described: tool names from the shipped CLI bundle `@ampcode/cli-win32-x64@0.0.1791662459-g6be10b` (unpacked 2026-10-10); tool text from an `amp tools show` dump of 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10) and a 2025 extracted prompt; current schemas are assembled server-side and are not in the bundle
- Target models: GPT and Claude routes per mode ("each mode has its own system prompt and tool definitions"); GPT routes get `apply_patch`, Claude routes get `create_file`/`edit_file`, and all share `Task`; each subagent's model is chosen independently of the main agent's

Amp's docs list five specialist subagents, each exposed as its own tool: Search (`finder`), Oracle (`oracle`), Librarian (`librarian`), `Task`, and Read Thread (`read_thread`). Since 2026-07-17 the model can also start persistent child threads with `create_thread` and coordinate them with `list_agent_modes`, `get_thread_status`, `send_thread_message`, and `wait_for_threads`. All of these are assembled server-side, so the shipped bundle has their names but not their current schemas; plugins can also define a custom subagent and expose it as a tool (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10).

#### `Task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Perform a task (a sub-task of the user's overall task) using a sub-agent that has access to the following tools: Grep, glob, Read, Bash, edit_file, create_file, read_web_page, get_diagnostics, web_search, finder, skill, task_list.


When to use the Task tool:
- When you need to perform complex multi-step tasks
- When you need to run an operation that will produce a lot of output (tokens) that is not needed after the sub-agent's task completes
- When you are making changes across many layers of an application (frontend, backend, API layer, etc.), after you have first planned and spec'd out the changes so they can be implemented independently by multiple sub-agents
- When the user asks you to launch an "agent" or "subagent", because the user assumes that the agent will do a good job

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- When you are performing a single logical task, such as adding a new feature to a single part of an application.
- When you're reading a single file (use Read), performing a text search (use Grep), editing a single file (use edit_file)
- When you're not sure what changes you want to make. Use all tools available to you to determine the changes to make.

How to use the Task tool:
- Run multiple sub-agents concurrently if the tasks may be performed independently (e.g., if they do not involve editing the same parts of the same file), by including multiple tool uses in a single assistant message.
- You will not see the individual steps of the sub-agent's execution, and you can't communicate with it until it finishes, at which point you will receive a summary of its work.
- Include all necessary context from the user's message and prior assistant steps, as well as a detailed plan for the task, in the task description. Be specific about what the sub-agent should return when finished to summarize its work.
- Tell the sub-agent how to verify its work if possible (e.g., by mentioning the relevant test commands to run).
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
```

Source: amp-extractions-latest/agents/agent-tools.md (`amp tools show Task`), nghyane/ampcode-connector at b8e65c8 - third-party reverse engineering, 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The current server-side description is not captured.

Parameters (YAML tool definition from an extracted prompt, verbatim, indentation reduced):

```yaml
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    prompt:
      type: string
      description: >-
        The task for the agent to perform. Be specific about what needs
        to be done and include any relevant context.
    description:
      type: string
      description: >-
        A very short description of the task that can be displayed to
        the user.
  required:
    - prompt
    - description
```

Source: Amp/claude-4-sonnet.yaml, x1xhlol/system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools at 1e4203a - extracted prompt, added 2025-09-14 (same text in Amp/gpt-5.yaml); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The 2026-03-10 dump lists the same two fields, `prompt (string)` and `description (string)`, with the same descriptions.

Semantics. `Task` blocks until the subagent finishes, and parallelism comes from several `Task` calls in one message; the subagent's single final message is the tool result and is not shown to the user. Amp's docs say subagents "work in isolation, so they can't communicate with each other, you can't guide them mid-task [...] The main agent only receives their final summary" (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The current bundle's renderer reads a `mode` field ("Subagent (${mode})") and labels the tool "Subagent", but the plugin docs say "`Task` runs a scoped subagent instead and does not accept a per-call agent mode" (shipped bundle; official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The shipped bundle maps Claude Code-style calls with `Agent:{ampName:"Task",input:kst},Task:{ampName:"Task",input:kst}`, where `kst` takes `{description, prompt, subagent_type}` and turns `subagent_type` into Amp's `mode` (shipped bundle, 0.0.1791662459). Subagents have been tools since 2025-06-10 ("Subagents are tools, too") (official blog, 2025-06-10).

#### `finder` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Intelligently search your codebase: Use it for complex, multi-step search tasks where you need to find code based on functionality or concepts rather than exact matches. Anytime you want to chain multiple grep calls you should use this tool.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- You must locate code by behavior or concept
- You need to run multiple greps in sequence
- You must correlate or look for connection between several areas of the codebase.
- You must filter broad terms ("config", "logger", "cache") by context.
- You need answers to questions such as "Where do we validate JWT authentication headers?" or "Which module handles file-watcher retry logic"

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS TOOL:
- When you know the exact file path - use Read directly
- When looking for specific symbols or exact strings - use glob or Grep
- When you need to create, modify files, or run terminal commands

USAGE GUIDELINES:
1. Always spawn multiple search agents in parallel to maximise speed.
2. Formulate your query as a precise engineering request.
   ✓ "Find every place we build an HTTP error response."
   ✗ "error handling search"
3. Name concrete artifacts, patterns, or APIs to narrow scope (e.g., "Express middleware", "fs.watch debounce").
4. State explicit success criteria so the agent knows when to stop (e.g., "Return file paths and line numbers for all JWT verification calls").
5. Never issue vague or exploratory commands - be definitive and goal-oriented.
```

Parameters (names, types, and descriptions as printed by `amp tools show`; required flags not shown, verbatim):

- query (string): The search query describing to the agent what it should. Be specific and include technical terms, file types, or expected code patterns to help the agent find relevant code. Formulate the query in a way that makes it clear to the agent when it has found the right thing.

Source (description and parameters): amp-extractions-latest/agents/agent-tools.md (`amp tools show finder`), nghyane/ampcode-connector at b8e65c8 - third-party reverse engineering, 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The current server-side schema is not captured.

Semantics. Amp's docs list this tool as the Search subagent, which "retrieves relevant code quickly" (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The description tells the model to "spawn multiple search agents in parallel"; the result format is not in the sources. The 2025 extracted prompt names it `codebase_search_agent` in `Task`'s tool list, and the current bundle's tool-name enum has `e.CODEBASE_SEARCH="finder"` (extracted prompt, added 2025-09-14; shipped bundle, 0.0.1791662459). Plugin agent definitions can pin the model for "the other subagents spawned from threads running this agent (Task workers, finder, thread reader, librarian)" (SDK type file, 2026-09-29).

#### `oracle` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

````text
Consult the oracle - an AI advisor powered by OpenAI's GPT-5.4 reasoning model that can plan, review, and provide expert guidance.

The oracle has access to the following tools:
- Read
- Grep
- glob
- web_search
- read_web_page
- read_thread
- find_thread.

You should consult the oracle for:
- Code reviews and architecture feedback
- Finding difficult bugs in codepaths that flow across many files
- Planning complex implementations or refactors
- Answering complex technical questions that require deep technical reasoning
- Providing an alternative point of view when you are struggling to solve a problem

You should NOT consult the oracle for:
- File reads or simple keyword searches (use Read or Grep directly)
- Codebase searches (use finder)
- Web browsing and searching (use read_web_page or web_search)
- Basic code modifications and when you need to execute code changes (do it yourself or use Task)

Usage guidelines:
- Be specific about what you want the oracle to review, plan, or debug
- Provide relevant context about what you're trying to achieve. If you know that 3 files are involved, list them and they will be attached.

# Examples

Review the authentication system architecture and suggest improvements
```json
{"task":"Review the authentication architecture and suggest improvements","files":["src/auth/index.ts","src/auth/jwt.ts"]}
```

Plan the implementation of real-time collaboration features
```json
{"task":"Plan the implementation of real-time collaboration feature"}
```

Analyze the performance bottlenecks in the data processing pipeline
```json
{"task":"Analyze performance bottlenecks","context":"Users report slow response times when processing large datasets"}
```

Review this API design and suggest better patterns
```json
{"task":"Review API design","context":"This is a REST API for user management","files":["src/api/users.ts"]}
```

Debug failing tests after refactor
```json
{"task":"Help debug why tests are failing","context":"Tests fail with \"undefined is not a function\" after refactoring the auth module","files":["src/auth/auth.test.ts"]}
```
````

Parameters (names, types, and descriptions as printed by `amp tools show`; required flags not shown, verbatim):

- task (string): The task or question you want the oracle to help with. Be specific about what kind of guidance, review, or planning you need.
- context (string): Optional context about the current situation, what you've tried, or background information that would help the oracle provide better guidance.
- files (array of string): Optional list of specific file paths (text files, images) that the oracle should examine as part of its analysis. These files will be attached to the oracle input.

Source (description and parameters): amp-extractions-latest/agents/agent-tools.md (`amp tools show oracle`), nghyane/ampcode-connector at b8e65c8 - third-party reverse engineering, 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The current server-side schema is not captured.

Semantics. Amp's docs say the Oracle "handles difficult reasoning and planning questions" and runs its own model, shown on the Modes page (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10); the 2026-03 description names OpenAI's GPT-5.4. Files listed in `files` are attached to the oracle's input. Plugin agent definitions can pin the Oracle's model and reasoning effort with an `oracle` field (SDK type file, 2026-09-29). The result format is not in the sources.

#### `librarian` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
The Librarian - a specialized codebase understanding agent that helps answer questions about large, complex codebases.
The Librarian works by reading from GitHub - it can see the private repositories the user approved access to in addition to all public repositories on GitHub.
The Librarian also supports Bitbucket Enterprise (self-hosted) repositories when the user has connected their Bitbucket Enterprise instance.

The Librarian acts as your personal multi-repository codebase expert, providing thorough analysis and comprehensive explanations across repositories.

It's ideal for complex, multi-step analysis tasks where you need to understand code architecture, functionality, and patterns across multiple repositories.

WHEN TO USE THE LIBRARIAN:
- Understanding complex multi-repository codebases and how they work
- Exploring relationships between different repositories
- Analyzing architectural patterns across large open-source projects
- Finding specific implementations across multiple codebases
- Understanding code evolution and commit history
- Getting comprehensive explanations of how major features work
- Exploring how systems are designed end-to-end across repositories

WHEN NOT TO USE THE LIBRARIAN:
- Simple local file reading (use Read directly)
- Local codebase searches (use finder)
- Code modifications or implementations (use other tools)
- Questions not related to understanding existing repositories

USAGE GUIDELINES:
1. Be specific about what repositories or projects you want to understand
2. Provide context about what you're trying to achieve
3. The Librarian will explore thoroughly across repositories before providing comprehensive answers
4. Expect detailed, documentation-quality responses suitable for sharing
5. When getting an answer from the Librarian, show it to the user in full, do not summarize it.

EXAMPLES:
- "How does authentication work in the Kubernetes codebase?"
- "Explain the architecture of the React rendering system"
- "Find how database migrations are handled in Rails"
- "Understand the plugin system in the VSCode codebase"
- "Compare how different web frameworks handle routing"
- "What changed in commit abc123 in my private repository?"
- "Show me the diff for commit fb492e2 in github.com/mycompany/private-repo"
- "Read the README from the main API repo on our Bitbucket Enterprise instance"
```

Parameters (names, types, and descriptions as printed by `amp tools show`; required flags not shown, verbatim):

- query (string): Your question about the codebase. Be specific about what you want to understand or explore.
- context (string): Optional context about what you're trying to achieve or background information.

Source (description and parameters): amp-extractions-latest/agents/agent-tools.md (`amp tools show librarian`), nghyane/ampcode-connector at b8e65c8 - third-party reverse engineering, 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The current server-side schema is not captured.

Semantics. Amp's docs say the Librarian "researches external codebases and large bodies of source material" and runs its own model (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The description tells the model to show the Librarian's answer to the user in full. The result format is not in the sources.

#### `read_thread` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

````text
Read and extract relevant content from another Amp thread by its ID.

This tool fetches a thread (locally or from the server if synced), renders it as markdown, and uses AI to extract only the information relevant to your specific goal. This keeps context concise while preserving important details.

## When to use this tool

- When the user pastes or references an Amp thread URL (format: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx) in their message
- When the user references a thread ID (format: T-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx or @T-abc123)
- When the user asks to "apply the same approach from [thread URL]"
- When the user says "do what we did in [thread URL]"
- When the user says "implement the plan we devised in [thread URL]"
- When you need to extract specific information from a referenced thread

## When NOT to use this tool

- When no thread ID is mentioned
- When working within the current thread (context is already available)

## Parameters

- **threadID**: The thread identifier in format T-{uuid} (e.g., "T-a38f981d-52da-47b1-818c-fbaa9ab56e0c")
- **goal**: A clear description of what information you're looking for in that thread. Be specific about what you need to extract.

# Examples

User asks "Implement the plan we devised in https://ampcode.com/threads/T-3f1beb2b-bded-4fda-96cc-1af7192f24b6"
```json
{"threadID":"T-3f1beb2b-bded-4fda-96cc-1af7192f24b6","goal":"Extract the implementation plan, design decisions, architecture approach, and any code patterns or examples discussed"}
```

User asks: "Do what we did in https://ampcode.com/threads/T-f916b832-c070-4853-8ab3-5e7596953bec, but for the Oracle tool"
```json
{"threadID":"T-f916b832-c070-4853-8ab3-5e7596953bec","goal":"Extract the implementation approach, code patterns, techniques used, and any relevant code examples that can be adapted for the Oracle tool"}
```

User asks: "Take the SQL queries from https://ampcode.com/threads/T-95e73a95-f4fe-4f22-8d5c-6297467c97a5 and turn it into a reusable script"
```json
{"threadID":"T-95e73a95-f4fe-4f22-8d5c-6297467c97a5","goal":"Extract all SQL queries, their purpose, parameters, and any context needed to understand how to make them reusable"}
```

User asks: "Apply the same fix from @T-def456 to this issue"
```json
{"threadID":"T-def456","goal":"Extract the bug description, root cause, the fix/solution, and relevant code changes"}
```
````

Parameters (names, types, and descriptions as printed by `amp tools show`; required flags not shown, verbatim):

- threadID (string): The thread ID in format T-{uuid} (e.g., "T-a38f981d-52da-47b1-818c-fbaa9ab56e0c")
- goal (string): A clear description of what information you need from the thread. Be specific about what to extract.

Source (description and parameters): amp-extractions-latest/agents/agent-tools.md (`amp tools show read_thread`), nghyane/ampcode-connector at b8e65c8 - third-party reverse engineering, 0.0.1773129970 (2026-03-10); fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The current server-side schema is not captured.

Semantics. Amp's docs list Read Thread as a specialist subagent that "reads and summarizes other Amp threads" (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The description says the tool renders the thread as markdown and "uses AI to extract only the information relevant to your specific goal". The plugin type file calls this role the "thread reader" and lets agent definitions pin its model (SDK type file, 2026-09-29).

### Augment Code

- Openness: closed source
- Version described: Auggie CLI 0.36.0 (npm `@augmentcode/auggie@0.36.0`, `package/augment.mjs`, August 2026), unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog
- Target models: built-in subagents pin Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite preview; configured subagents can set their own `model`
- Sources:
  - Auggie CLI shipped bundle `@augmentcode/auggie@0.36.0`, package/augment.mjs, https://www.npmjs.com/package/@augmentcode/auggie/v/0.36.0 - shipped bundle, 0.36.0 (Aug 2026)
  - Augment changelog, New CLI subagents, https://www.augmentcode.com/changelog/new-cli-subagents - official changelog, 2026-01-09
  - Augment Code/claude-4-sonnet-tools.json in x1xhlol/system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools at 1e4203a, https://github.com/x1xhlol/system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools/blob/1e4203a7d88873c1b37ab2d1c07074fea498c274/Augment%20Code/claude-4-sonnet-tools.json - extracted prompt, 2025-08-18

Auggie's synchronous tool is `sub-agent` when no subagent configuration applies, or `sub-agent-<name>` for each configured subagent; the built-ins are `sub-agent-general-purpose`, `sub-agent-research`, `sub-agent-plan`, `sub-agent-code`, `sub-agent-validate`, and the hidden `sub-agent-context-gathering`. The same bundle defines webview-only tools, `subagent-webview[-<name>]` (synchronous) and `async-subagent-webview[-<name>]` (asynchronous), whose direct `call` in the CLI returns an error; whether the IDE exposes them is not in the sources. Subagents report back with `finish-subagent-task`, `finish-subagent-context-gathering`, or `report-to-parent`.

#### `sub-agent` (spawn, output)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Run a single synchronous sub-agent in the same workspace. Inputs: instruction (string), name (string). Returns the sub-agent's last message and minimal edit metadata. This tool only returns when the sub-agent completed its work.

**IMPORTANT: This tool can be run in parallel.** Multiple sub-agents can execute simultaneously with different names and instructions. Use parallel execution when you have multiple independent tasks that can be completed concurrently.

Available actions:
• **run** - Execute a sub-agent with the given instruction (waits for completion)
• **output** - Show the response and file changes (if any) made by a completed sub-agent
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `JSON.stringify` in the shipped bundle, shown with the default `instruction` description, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "run",
        "output"
      ],
      "description": "Action to perform:\n'run' - execute a sub-agent with the given instruction\n'output' - show the response and file changes (if any) made by a completed sub-agent"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Name of the sub-agent. Names must be unique and contain no spaces.\nFor 'run': provide a name for the new agent (required).\nFor 'output': provide the name of a completed agent to review (required)."
    },
    "instruction": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Detailed instruction for the sub-agent (required for 'run' action only).\nThe instruction should be clear and complete - the sub-agent will work independently to complete it."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): package/augment.mjs, sub-agent tool definition class (default description and `inputSchemaJson`), `@augmentcode/auggie` 0.36.0 - shipped bundle, Aug 2026; unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog, with the template literals evaluated in Node.

Semantics. `run` blocks until the subagent finishes and returns the runner's result text, or `Sub-agent ${l} failed:\n${f}` on failure; several `sub-agent` calls can run in parallel under different names. `output` returns a completed subagent's stored result followed by its diff, if any, and its errors include `Agent "${l}" not found. See the agent names from the run result.` and `No stored result found for agent ${l}. Agent may not have completed yet.`. The `name` is the only handle: it must be unique and contain no spaces (`Agent name "${l}" cannot contain spaces`, `Agent name "${l}" is already in use`), and the tool has no background, wait, or cancel action. When `action` is missing but `instruction` is present, the bundle treats the call as `run`. CLI subagents launched on 2026-01-09 (official changelog), and 2025 IDE tool dumps had no subagent tool (extracted prompt, 2025-08-18).

#### `sub-agent-<name>` (spawn, output)

Description (verbatim, as generated for a configured subagent; `<displayName or name>` and `<description>` stand for configured values, and the Description line appears only when a description is set):

```text
Run a single synchronous sub-agent in the same workspace. Inputs: instruction (string), name (string). Returns the sub-agent's last message and minimal edit metadata. This tool only returns when the sub-agent completed its work.

**IMPORTANT: This tool can be run in parallel.** Multiple sub-agents can execute simultaneously with different names and instructions. Use parallel execution when you have multiple independent tasks that can be completed concurrently.

Available actions:
• **run** - Execute a sub-agent with the given instruction (waits for completion)
• **output** - Show the response and file changes (if any) made by a completed sub-agent

**Configuration:**
- Name: <displayName or name>
- Description: <description>
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `JSON.stringify` in the shipped bundle, shown with the default `instruction` description, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "run",
        "output"
      ],
      "description": "Action to perform:\n'run' - execute a sub-agent with the given instruction\n'output' - show the response and file changes (if any) made by a completed sub-agent"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Name of the sub-agent. Names must be unique and contain no spaces.\nFor 'run': provide a name for the new agent (required).\nFor 'output': provide the name of a completed agent to review (required)."
    },
    "instruction": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Detailed instruction for the sub-agent (required for 'run' action only).\nThe instruction should be clear and complete - the sub-agent will work independently to complete it."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): package/augment.mjs, sub-agent tool definition class and tool-name function (`"sub-agent-"` prefix), `@augmentcode/auggie` 0.36.0 - shipped bundle, Aug 2026; unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog, with the template literals evaluated in Node.

Semantics. For each configured subagent the tool name is `sub-agent-` plus the configured name, normalized by trimming, turning whitespace runs and characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` into `-`, and collapsing repeated `-`; an empty result falls back to `sub-agent`. The schema shown is what the bundle generates for every configured subagent, and the description appends a `**Configuration:**` block with the display name (or name) and, when set, the configured description. A configured `toolDescription` replaces the whole description, and a configured `instructionDescription` replaces the `instruction` parameter's description. Behavior is the same as `sub-agent`, and a configuration can also set `model`, `color`, `tools` or `disabledTools`, and `finishTool`.

#### `subagent-webview` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Run a sub-agent in the same workspace. Returns the sub-agent's last message and edit metadata. This tool only returns when the sub-agent has completed its work.
Spawn a subagent to handle a discrete task. The subagent runs immediately and returns its result inline as a tool response - just like any other tool call. Use this as your DEFAULT delegation method.

**IMPORTANT: This tool can be run in parallel.** Multiple sub-agents can execute simultaneously with different instructions. Use parallel execution when you have multiple independent tasks that can be completed concurrently. For example, if you need to fix 5 files, spawn 5 sub-agents in parallel rather than fixing them one by one.
You should ALWAYS delegate to a subagent when a task:
- Does not require your ongoing reasoning or conversation history to complete
- Can be fully described in a single instruction
- Has a clear, verifiable output

Spawn subagents LIBERALLY. They are cheap and fast. Doing work yourself that a subagent could handle is wasteful - it burns your context window and slows you down.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `JSON.stringify` in the shipped bundle, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "instruction": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Detailed instruction for the sub-agent.\nThe instruction should be clear and complete - the sub-agent will work independently to complete it.\n\n### Subagent Example Prompt:\nYou are a focused subagent spawned to complete ONE specific task. You have no memory of prior conversation - everything you need is in this message.\n\n{task_description}\n\n## Context\n{relevant_context - files, code snippets, constraints}\n\n## Output Requirements\n{what_to_return - code, a file, a summary, etc.}\n"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "instruction"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): package/augment.mjs, webview sub-agent tool definition class, `@augmentcode/auggie` 0.36.0 - shipped bundle, Aug 2026; unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog, with the template literals evaluated in Node.

Semantics. The description says the subagent "returns its result inline as a tool response" and calls the tool the "DEFAULT delegation method". In the CLI bundle a direct `call` returns "Webview sub-agent tool is only supported in the webview context. Use the synchronous sub-agent tool instead." and logs that the call "should be handled by saga in webview context". Configured subagents get `subagent-webview-<name>` by the same normalization rule as `sub-agent-<name>`, with the same `**Configuration:**` block appended, and the schema shown is generated for each. Whether the IDE exposes this tool is not in the sources.

#### `async-subagent-webview` (spawn, output, wait, status, message)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn and manage asynchronous sub-agents that run in parallel with the parent conversation.

Unlike the synchronous sub-agent tool, this tool returns immediately after spawning a subagent,
allowing the parent to continue working while the subagent runs in the background.
Spawn a long-running subagent that works in the background. Unlike the synchronous subagent, this returns IMMEDIATELY with a task handle - the subagent continues working while you move on. Use this for tasks that are too large or complex for a synchronous call.

You check on async subagents later using 'check' action which returns:
- Status: running | completed | failed
- If completed: the subagent's output
- If running: a progress summary (if available)
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `JSON.stringify` in the shipped bundle, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "spawn",
        "check",
        "message",
        "await"
      ],
      "description": "Action to perform:\n- 'spawn': Start a new async subagent (returns immediately with conversationId)\n- 'check': Check status and latest output of an async subagent\n- 'message': Send a follow-up message to a running async subagent\n- 'await': Wait for an async subagent to complete and get its final result\nThe instruction should be clear and complete - the sub-agent will work independently to complete it.\n\n### Subagent Example Prompt:\nYou are a focused subagent spawned to complete ONE specific task. You have no memory of prior conversation - everything you need is in this message.\n\n{task_description}\n\n## Context\n{relevant_context - files, code snippets, constraints}\n\n## Output Requirements\n{what_to_return - code, a file, a summary, etc.}\n"
    },
    "instruction": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Detailed instruction for the subagent (required for 'spawn' action).\nThe instruction should be clear and complete - the subagent will work independently."
    },
    "subagentConversationId": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The conversation ID of an async subagent (required for 'check', 'message', and 'await' actions).\nThis is returned by the 'spawn' action."
    },
    "message": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Follow-up message to send to the subagent (required for 'message' action).\nUse this to provide additional context, clarify instructions, or redirect the subagent."
    },
    "timeoutSeconds": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Timeout in seconds for the 'await' action (default: 60).\nIf the subagent does not complete within this time, the await will return an error."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): package/augment.mjs, async webview sub-agent tool definition class, `@augmentcode/auggie` 0.36.0 - shipped bundle, Aug 2026; unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog, with the template literals evaluated in Node.

Semantics. `spawn` "returns immediately with conversationId", and later `check`, `message`, and `await` calls pass that value as `subagentConversationId`. `check` returns the status (`running | completed | failed`) and the output or a progress summary, and `await` waits up to `timeoutSeconds` seconds (default 60) and returns an error on timeout. Configured subagents get `async-subagent-webview-<name>` by the same normalization rule as `sub-agent-<name>`, with the `**Configuration:**` block appended, and the schema shown is generated for each. In the CLI bundle a direct `call` returns "Async sub-agent webview tool is only supported in the webview context. Use the synchronous sub-agent tool instead."; the spawn result text, any completion notice, and whether the IDE exposes the tool are not in the sources.

#### `finish-subagent-task` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Signal that this subagent has completed its assigned task and report the final result to the parent agent. Call this exactly once as your final action. After this tool succeeds, do not continue working unless the parent sends a follow-up instruction.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `JSON.stringify` in the shipped bundle, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "message": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Final result or findings to report to the parent agent."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "message"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): package/augment.mjs, finish-tool spec for `finish-subagent-task`, `@augmentcode/auggie` 0.36.0 - shipped bundle, Aug 2026; unpacked 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. A subagent calls it "exactly once as your final action"; the tool result is the trimmed `message`, and an empty message fails with "Invalid parameter `message`. It must not be empty.". Subagent configurations have a `finishTool` field, and the bundle registers two finish tools in one map: this one and `finish-subagent-context-gathering`. How the parent receives the message is not in the sources.

#### `finish-subagent-context-gathering` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Signal that this context-gathering subagent has finished and report results to the parent. Provide a concise free-form `summary`. Optionally include `scope` (what was and wasn't searched), `references` (a scannable exhaustive index of every relevant location, distinct from `snippets` which are the few locations expanded into full file contents for the parent to read in detail), `negativeFindings` (claims of "X does not exist" with the locations you actually inspected), and `openQuestions` (sub-questions you couldn't answer within budget). Your `grep-search` calls are auto-extracted from tool history into a Search Log section in the report - do not re-list them here. The runtime expands each `snippets` entry into the actual file contents on the way out, so do NOT paste code into `summary` or `note` - describe what is interesting at each location. Call this exactly once as your final action.
```

Semantics. The bundle validates each snippet (non-empty `path`, integer `startLine` of at least 1, `endLine` not before `startLine`) and skips malformed ones with warnings. How the parent sees the finished report is not in the sources.

The parent model sees `Agent` (named `Task` until 2.1.63) to spawn a subagent, `SendMessage` to message, continue, or resume one, `TaskStop` to stop one (the same tool stops background shells), and `ListAgents` to list message targets when cross-session messaging is on; a subagent spawned under auto mode can also get the child-side `SubagentHandback` to return its report. There is no wait, read, or status tool: "A background subagent's results reach Claude as a completion notification in a later turn." (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10). The Claude Agent SDK runs the same harness and gives the model the same tools; for SDK hosts, the `tools` array in the `SDKSystemMessage` init message "currently lists this tool as `Task` for backward compatibility", subagent types come from the `agents` option (each key becomes a `subagent_type` value), fork mode is off "in the Agent SDK unless you turn it on", and the host can stop a subagent with `stopTask(taskId)` in TypeScript or `stop_task(task_id)` in Python, after which "A `TaskNotificationMessage` with status `"stopped"` follows" (official docs, fetched 2026-10-10; source at commit `b6e9d12`).

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have - it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.${IS_WEB_FETCH_AGENT_AVAILABLE_FN()?` This does not cover the `${WEB_FETCH_AGENT_TYPE}` agent type where it is listed and you have no ${WEBFETCH_TOOL_NAME} tool of your own: it stands in for that tool, so calling it to read a page is ordinary tool use.`:""}

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative - "will I need this output again" - not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this - it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path - do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format - not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running - give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* - what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.

## Writing the prompt

${HAS_SUBAGENT_TYPE?"Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. ":""}Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room - it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question - prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

${HAS_SUBAGENT_TYPE?"For fresh agents, terse":"Terse"} command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this - it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
${AGENT_TOOL_NAME}({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list - done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn - the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn - notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit - that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent - it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
${AGENT_TOOL_NAME}({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes - I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

Parameters (TypeScript type from the SDK type file, verbatim):

```ts
export interface AgentInput {
  /**
   * A short (3-5 word) description of the task
   */
  description: string;
  /**
   * The task for the agent to perform
   */
  prompt: string;
  /**
   * The type of specialized agent to use for this task
   */
  subagent_type?: string;
  /**
   * Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" - forks always inherit the parent model.
   */
  model?: "sonnet" | "opus" | "haiku" | "fable";
  /**
   * Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.
   */
  effort?: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max";
  /**
   * Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs - otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.
   */
  run_in_background?: boolean;
  /**
   * Name for the spawned agent. Makes it addressable via SendMessage({to: name}) while running.
   */
  name?: string;
  /**
   * Deprecated; ignored. The session has a single implicit team.
   */
  team_name?: string;
  /**
   * Deprecated; ignored. Subagents inherit the parent session's permission mode; agent-definition frontmatter may override it.
   */
  mode?: "acceptEdits" | "auto" | "bypassPermissions" | "default" | "dontAsk" | "plan";
  /**
   * Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).
   */
  isolation?: "worktree" | "remote";
}
```

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.296 `sdk-tools.d.ts`, https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.296/sdk-tools.d.ts - SDK type file, 0.3.296 (bundles Claude Code 2.1.296), 2026-10-09, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog; the file says it is generated from the tools' JSON Schema. The 2.1.296 bundle assembles the model-facing schema conditionally: it defines a `cwd` parameter and then omits it, removes `run_in_background` when fork mode is on, drops `model` when `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` is set, and can swap `effort` for a variant that accepts `"lower"` and `"higher"` (shipped bundle, 2.1.296).

Semantics. Since 2.1.198 (2026-07-01) a call that omits `run_in_background` runs the subagent in the background ("Claude Code runs subagents in the background by default", official doc, fetched 2026-10-10), `subagent_type: "fork"` starts a fork that inherits the parent's full conversation context and always runs on the parent's model, an omitted `subagent_type` gets the general-purpose agent, and the list of agent types is not in the description: the bundle's `${AVAILABLE_AGENT_TYPES_NOTICE}` reads "Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation." (shipped bundle, 2.1.296). A background call returns at once with a result that begins "Async agent launched successfully.", gives `agentId: ${agentId}` with "Use SendMessage with to: '${agentId}', summary: '<5-10 word recap>' to continue this agent.", says "You will be notified automatically when it completes.", and ends with `output_file: ${outputFile}` and "Do NOT Read or tail this file via the shell tool - it is the full subagent JSONL transcript and reading it will overflow your context."; a foreground call returns the subagent's text blocks, then `agentId: <id> (use SendMessage with to: '<id>', summary: '<5-10 word recap>' to continue this agent)` and a `<usage>` block (shipped bundle, 2.1.296). Completion reaches the parent as a user-role `<task-notification>` message, prefixed inside `<system-reminder>` by a notice that opens "[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]", with summary variants `finished`, `failed: {error}`, `was stopped by Claude`, `was stopped by user`, and `stopped at its N-turn limit (partial result ...)`, in this shape (reconstructed from the 2.1.296 bundle code; optional elements marked; shipped bundle, 2.1.296):

```text
<task-notification>
<task-id>{agentId}</task-id>
<tool-use-id>{toolUseId}</tool-use-id>          (optional)
<output-file>{path}</output-file>               (optional)
<status>completed</status>
<summary>Agent "{description}" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>{agent's final text}</result>
<usage><subagent_tokens>N</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>N</tool_uses><duration_ms>N</duration_ms></usage>
</task-notification>
```

There is no wait or read tool: the 2.0.64 changelog entry (2025-12-10) reads "Unshipped AgentOutputTool and BashOutputTool, in favor of a new unified TaskOutputTool", the model-facing `TaskOutput` took `task_id`, `block` (default true), and `timeout` (milliseconds, 0 to 600000, default 30000) (shipped bundle, 2.0.65), 2.1.83 (2026-03-24) "Deprecated `TaskOutput` tool in favor of using `Read` on the background task's output file path", 2.1.277 (2026-09-18) "Removed the deprecated TaskOutput tool", and 2.1.7 (2026-01-13) "Added inline display of agent's final response in task notifications" (official changelog). The tool was `Task` until 2.1.63 (2026-02-28): "In version 2.1.63, the Task tool was renamed to Agent. Existing `Task(...)` references in settings and agent definitions still work as aliases." (official doc, fetched 2026-10-10; shipped bundles, 2.1.62 and 2.1.63); the 2.1.296 bundle still lists `Task` as an alias, but the docs confirm it only for settings and agent definitions, and the team tools `TeammateTool` (2.1.16) and its successors `TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` (2.1.33) were removed in 2.1.178 (2026-06-15) in favor of one implicit team addressed through `name`, which leaves `team_name` and `mode` "Deprecated; ignored" (extracted prompt changelog; official changelog).

#### `SendMessage` (message)

Description (verbatim):

````text
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
${IS_MESSAGING_BEYOND_OWN_AGENTS_DISABLED?'| `"researcher"` | An agent of this session, by its name |\n| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |\n\nNo one outside this session can be reached.':`| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |${CROSS_SESSION_RECIPIENT_TABLE_ROWS}`}

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents - to communicate, you MUST call this tool.${IS_MESSAGING_BEYOND_OWN_AGENTS_DISABLED?"":" Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox."} Refer to agents by name - names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original - it's already rendered to the user.${CROSS_SESSION_GUIDANCE_BLOCK}${SHOULD_INCLUDE_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_RESPONSES&&!IS_MESSAGING_BEYOND_OWN_AGENTS_DISABLED?'\n\n## Protocol responses (legacy)\n\nIf you receive a JSON message with `type: "shutdown_request"` or `type: "plan_approval_request"`, respond with the matching `_response` type - echo the `request_id`, set `approve` true/false:\n\n```json\n{"to": "team-lead", "message": {"type": "shutdown_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": true}}\n{"to": "researcher", "message": {"type": "plan_approval_response", "request_id": "...", "approve": false, "feedback": "add error handling"}}\n```\n\nApproving shutdown terminates your process. Rejecting plan sends the teammate back to revise. Don't originate `shutdown_request` unless asked. Don't send structured JSON status messages - report progress through your task tools if you have them, otherwise in plain prose.':""}

## Cross-session

Use `${LIST_AGENTS_TOOL_NAME}` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` - the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name - a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough - `${LIST_AGENTS_TOOL_NAME}` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins - use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `${LIST_AGENTS_TOOL_NAME}` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright - for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) - one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) - shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `${LIST_AGENTS_TOOL_NAME}` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block - a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` - subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` - only when a listing or an error shows one |
````

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64` 2.1.296 package, embedded JS of the native binary - shipped bundle, 2.1.296 (2026-10-09), fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. `Ps(!1)` builds the schema without cross-session messaging and `Ps(!0)` the schema with it (adding `notify_when_idle`), and `ke()` picks the variant; in the same chunk `bdt` is `200` and `xc` is `"ListAgents"`. Semantics. A send to a running subagent returns "Message queued for delivery to ${n.agentName} at its next tool round."; a send to a stopped subagent resumes it in the background from its transcript and returns "Resuming agent" plus its name; `to: "main"` from a background subagent returns "Message queued for the main conversation's next turn."; and a subagent the user stopped is not resumed ("Agent "${n.agentName}" was stopped by the user and was not resumed.") (shipped bundle, 2.1.296). The address is the `name` passed to `Agent` ("Makes it addressable via SendMessage({to: name}) while running.") or the `agentId` from the spawn result. Before 2.1.75 the tool was a union on `type` (`message` with `recipient`, `content`, and `summary`; `broadcast`; `shutdown_request`; and others) (shipped bundle, 2.1.63), and 2.1.77 (2026-03-16) made it the way to continue a subagent: "The Agent tool no longer accepts a `resume` parameter - use `SendMessage({to: agentId})` to continue a previously spawned agent" and "`SendMessage` now auto-resumes stopped agents in the background instead of returning an error" (official changelog), replacing `Agent`'s `resume` field, added in 2.0.28 (2025-10-27), whose text was "Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, the agent will continue from the previous execution transcript." (SDK type file, 0.1.28). When cross-session messaging is on, the same tool also reaches other Claude sessions that `ListAgents` shows, and `notify_when_idle` subscribes the main conversation to one idle notice from a session on the same machine.

#### `ListAgents` (list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Lists agents you can ${SEND_MESSAGE_TOOL_NAME} to - in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet - do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions - Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `${SEND_MESSAGE_TOOL_NAME}({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough - two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

Lists the agents and Claude sessions this session can see - in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions, each row labeled by kind - plus this session's own name, the one other sessions use to message it. This session has no ${SEND_MESSAGE_TOOL_NAME} tool, so it cannot message them with it; other sessions can still message this one. To reply, use your host application's own messaging tool if it provides one - otherwise a reply from here is not possible, and if one is needed, tell your user.
```

Source: Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts at commit `d1f0cb640f34dd2d2322a1f225060261ba913790`, `tool-description-listagents.md` (ccVersion 2.1.239) followed by `tool-description-listagents-no-sendmessage-tool.md` (ccVersion 2.1.284), where `${SEND_MESSAGE_TOOL_NAME}` is `SendMessage` - extracted prompt, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The block gives both variants: in the 2.1.296 bundle, `description()` and `prompt()` both return `Moo({canSendMessages:fv(t)})`, and the collection files the second text as the variant for sessions without a `SendMessage` tool (shipped bundle, 2.1.296, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from the shipped bundle, verbatim):

```js
d=p(()=>De({channel:o().max(256).optional().describe("Not available in this build; leave unset."),q:o().max(256).optional().describe("Not available in this build; leave unset.")}))
```

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64` 2.1.296 package, embedded JS of the native binary - shipped bundle, 2.1.296 (2026-10-09), fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. The 2.1.296 bundle enables the tool only when `xi()` is true; `xi()` returns false when the `messagingBeyondOwnAgentsDisabled` setting is on, and otherwise follows the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE` or, failing that, the feature flag `tengu_harbor_kite` (on Windows also `tengu_harbor_kite_win`), each with a fallback of true. The tool is read-only and concurrency-safe, and its tool result is the `listing` string ("Formatted list of reachable agents"), in which every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]`. It was `ListPeers` before: the bundle keeps `ListPeers` as an alias and maps it to `ListAgents`, and the extracted-prompt changelog first lists the `ListAgents` description at ccVersion 2.1.200 (extracted prompt changelog).

#### `TaskStop` (cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task
```

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64` 2.1.296 package, tool prompt in the embedded JS - shipped bundle, 2.1.296 (2026-10-09).

Parameters (TypeScript type from the SDK type file, verbatim):

```ts
export interface TaskStopInput {
  /**
   * The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.
   */
  task_id?: string;
  /**
   * Deprecated: use task_id instead
   */
  shell_id?: string;
}
```

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.296 `sdk-tools.d.ts`, https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.296/sdk-tools.d.ts - SDK type file, 0.3.296 (bundles Claude Code 2.1.296), 2026-10-09, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. One tool stops background shells, background subagents, and agent-team teammates, by ID or, for named subagents and teammates, by name; it returns `TaskStopOutput` with `message`, `task_id`, `task_type`, and an optional `command` (SDK type file, 0.3.296), and a stopped subagent's `<task-notification>` summary reads `Agent "<description>" was stopped by Claude` (shipped bundle, 2.1.296). `TaskStop` was added in 2.1.19 (2026-01-23) and replaced `KillShell` (`{shell_id}`, "Kills a running background bash shell by its ID"); the 2.1.296 bundle maps both `KillShell` and `KillBash` to `TaskStop`, and `shell_id` remains as "Deprecated: use task_id instead" (shipped bundles, 2.1.19 and 2.1.296). SDK hosts also have a host-side stop that is not a model tool, `stopTask(taskId)` in TypeScript and `stop_task(task_id)` in Python (official docs, fetched 2026-10-10).

#### `SubagentHandback` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call ${SUBAGENT_HANDBACK_TOOL_NAME}({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through ${SUBAGENT_HANDBACK_TOOL_NAME} reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.
```

Source: Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts at commit `d1f0cb640f34dd2d2322a1f225060261ba913790`, `tool-description-subagenthandback.md` (ccVersion 2.1.285) - extracted prompt, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The same text is the tool's `prompt()` in the 2.1.296 bundle, where `${SUBAGENT_HANDBACK_TOOL_NAME}` is `SubagentHandback` and `description()` returns the shorter "Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you: the only way it reaches them. The call ends your run, so make it your last." (shipped bundle, 2.1.296, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from the shipped bundle, verbatim):

```js
var L=p(()=>u({message:o().describe("Your full report for your caller")})),D=p(()=>u({success:M(),message:o()}));
```

Source: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64` 2.1.296 package, embedded JS of the native binary - shipped bundle, 2.1.296 (2026-10-09), fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog; `L` is the input schema and `D` the output schema.

Semantics. This is a child-side tool: the 2.1.296 bundle adds it to a subagent's tools only when the spawn meets several conditions, among them that the permission context's `mode` is `"auto"` and that a switch is on that reads the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_SENDMESSAGE_HANDBACK` and otherwise the flag `tengu_lively_waffle` (fallback true). The call ends the subagent's run and returns `{success, message}`: an empty `message` fails validation ("message must not be empty"), a subagent without the hand-back contract gets "Nothing was sent: SubagentHandback is not active for this agent. Write your report as plain text instead.", and a second call gets "Nothing was sent: your report was already delivered (SubagentHandback delivers one report)." If the subagent ends without calling it, the bundle prompts it with "Your report has not been delivered. Call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) now; the call ends your run." up to a bounce limit, and otherwise the parent is told "The subagent ended without delivering a report through SubagentHandback, so no report was delivered." A delivered report reaches the parent as a message from the subagent, and the parent is then told "This agent's report was delivered to you as a message from "<name>" (its SubagentHandback call). Read it there; it is not repeated here.", or that it came "under a SECURITY WARNING from auto mode" when auto mode's review flagged it (shipped bundle, 2.1.296). The extracted-prompt changelog first lists the tool at ccVersion 2.1.285 (extracted prompt changelog).

Anthropic's cookbook says the server gives the coordinator `create_agent`, `send_to_agent`, `wait_for_agents`, and `list_agents`, and gives workers `submit_result` and `send_to_parent`; Anthropic's skill file at commit dbd4588 names two coordinator tools (`list_agents`, `send_to_agent`). The difference is unresolved, so each named tool has its own subsection with its sources; the Multiagent orchestration doc mentions only `list_agents` and `send_to_agent`. The tools come from the agent's `multiagent` block (the `coordinator` type, or the newer `multiagent_20261001` type, which also allows inline agents and dynamic workflows), and the cookbook says "You never define any of those tools."

#### `create_agent` (spawn)

Description: not captured.

Parameters: not captured.

Source (tool name): Claude Managed Agents cookbook "Plan big, execute small", https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/managed-agents-cma-plan-big-execute-small, and its notebook at commit 813fbee - official doc and source at commit, published 2026-07-02.

Semantics. The cookbook names `create_agent` among the four tools the server "automatically gives" a coordinator and says "Its `create_agent` tool takes a bare agent name and task string." It adds that "the coordinator can't see anything about its roster agents - not their prompts, not their names, not their descriptions" and "(With a single-agent roster, any requested name resolves to the one worker; with several worker types, name them explicitly in the coordinator's prompt.)" The cookbook's coordinator system prompt says to "delegate each to a worker via create_agent" and to "Run several workers in parallel on independent sub-questions". The skill file does not name `create_agent`; it says "Spawning returns immediately; the subagent's report arrives in a later coordinator turn." and sets limits of one level of delegation and "at most 25 child threads per session, idle ones included" (source at commit, dbd4588).

Description: not captured.

Parameters: not captured.

Semantics. The skill file says "The coordinator's thread receives delegation tools for working the roster: `list_agents` (see the roster) and `send_to_agent` (task or message a member)." The Multiagent orchestration doc calls it "`send_to_agent`, which sends a subagent a follow-up message", and the cookbook's coordinator prompt says to "send a follow-up with send_to_agent". Threads persist, so "the coordinator can send a follow-up to a subagent it called earlier and that subagent retains its prior turns" (skill file). On the primary stream the coordinator's message appears as an `agent.thread_message_sent` event with `to_session_thread_id`, `to_agent_name`, and `content`, described as "the coordinator sent a task or follow-up to an agent" (skill file). Both the skill file and the doc say `send_to_agent` cannot reach the advisor.

Semantics. Of the sources here, only the cookbook names `wait_for_agents`, as one of the coordinator's four server-provided tools. The cookbook's coordinator system prompt says "ALWAYS call wait_for_agents after spawning before drawing any conclusion" and "If a worker returns an infrastructure error (rate limit, timeout) instead of findings, re-assign the same sub-question to a fresh worker." Whether the tool takes a timeout, and in what unit, is not in the sources. The skill file names no wait tool and says the subagent's report "arrives in a later coordinator turn" (source at commit, dbd4588).

A roster holds 1-20 entries, at most one of them `self`, and "each rostered agent can be spawned many times" (skill file).

Anthropic's cookbook prompts give the lead agent `run_blocking_subagent` to start a research subagent, and give both the lead and each subagent `complete_task` to submit a report. The engineering post says "See the open-source prompts in our Cookbook for example prompts from our system."

The lead prompt says "Use the `run_blocking_subagent` tool to create a research subagent, with very clear and specific instructions in the `prompt` parameter of this tool to describe the subagent's task." The engineering post says "Currently, our lead agents execute subagents synchronously, waiting for each set of subagents to complete before proceeding." (official blog, 2025-06-13). The subagent prompt says "As soon as the task is done, immediately use the `complete_task` tool to finish and provide your detailed, condensed, complete, accurate report to the lead researcher."
