The bundle's tool-name enum gives the subagent tools below: `Agent`, `Workflow`, `TaskOutput`, `SendMessage`, `ListAgents`, `InterruptAgent`, and `TaskStop`. Each tool class except `Agent` sets a short inline `description`; the package's `product.json` also ships longer description templates (`tool-agent-description`, `tool-taskoutput-description`, `tool-taskstop-description`, `tool-sendmessage-description`, `workflow-tool-description`), which the JavaScript bundle never references by name, so which text reaches the model when both exist was not traced. The same enum names team tools (`TeamCreate`, `TeamDelete`), colleague and channel tools (`MessageColleague`, `CreateColleague`, `ListColleagues`, `SpeakInChannel`, `ChannelTasks`, `CreateChannel`), `InspectSelf`, and A2A client tools (`A2AGetAgentCard`, `A2ASendMessage`, `A2AGetTask`, `A2ACancelTask`); their definitions were not extracted for this catalog. CodeBuddy's docs still say "Task tool" in places (official doc, undated).

#### `Agent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Agent tool launches specialized agents (subprocesses) that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types and the tools they have access to:
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
{%- if agents and agents.length > 0 -%}
{%- for agent in agents -%}
{%- if agent.asTool %}
- {{agent.name}}{%- if agent.truncatedDescription == undefined -%}: {{agent.description}}{%- elif agent.truncatedDescription %}: {{agent.truncatedDescription}}{%- endif -%} (Tools: {%- if agent.tools and agent.tools.length > 0 -%}{{agent.tools.join(',')}}{%- endif -%})
{%- endif -%}
{%- endfor -%}
{%- if agentsOverview and agentsOverview.omittedCount > 0 %}
[Registered agents exceed the maximum limit. Please go to `.codebuddy/agents/` and `.codebuddy/plugins/` to find remaining agents.]
{%- endif %}
{%- endif %}

When using the Agent tool, you can specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, it defaults to "general-purpose" which runs with an independent context.

{%- if not forkSubagentDisabled %}
**Fork mode (subagent_type="fork")**: When you explicitly set subagent_type to "fork", the agent inherits your full context (system prompt, tools, conversation history). This is ideal for:
- Tasks that require the same tools and context as the current conversation
- Tasks where the agent needs to understand the full conversation history to proceed

Only use fork mode when inheriting context is essential. For most tasks (code review, exploration, research, generation), prefer specifying a concrete agent type or omitting subagent_type to get an independent agent.
{%- endif %}

When NOT to use the Agent tool:
- If you want to read a specific file path, use the Read tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the Bash tool (`grep -rn` / `rg`) instead, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the Read tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly
- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do
- When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- You can optionally run agents in the background using the `run_in_background` parameter. When an agent runs in the background, you will be automatically notified when it completes - do NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress. Continue with other work or respond to the user instead.
- **Foreground vs background**: Use foreground (default) when you need the agent's results before you can proceed - e.g., research agents whose findings inform your next steps. Use background when you have genuinely independent work to do in parallel.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's name as the `recipient` field - that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs, so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent.
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.

## Writing the prompt

Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room - it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question - prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

Terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

{%- if teamEnabled %}
## Spawning Teammates

When a team is active (created via TeamCreate), you can spawn teammates by providing the `name` and optionally `team_name` parameters:

- `name`: Name for the spawned agent. Makes it addressable via SendMessage({to: name}) while running.
- `subagent_type`: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.
- `team_name`: Team name for spawning. Uses current team context if omitted.
- `mode`: Permission mode for the spawned teammate (e.g., "plan" to require plan approval)
- `max_turns`: Maximum number of agentic turns (API round-trips) before the agent stops

## Choosing Agent Types for Teammates

When spawning teammates via the Agent tool, choose the `subagent_type` based on what tools the agent needs for its task. Each agent type has a different set of available tools - match the agent to the work:
- **Read-only agents** (e.g., Explore, Plan) cannot edit or write files. Only assign them research, search, or planning tasks. Never assign them implementation work.
- **Full-capability agents** (e.g., general-purpose) have access to all tools including file editing, writing, and bash. Use these for tasks that require making changes.
- **Custom agents** defined in `.codebuddy/agents/` may have their own tool restrictions. Check their descriptions to understand what they can and cannot do.
Always review the agent type descriptions and their available tools listed in the Agent tool prompt before selecting a `subagent_type` for a teammate.

Teammates always run in the background in detached mode. They communicate via the SendMessage tool and coordinate through the shared task list.
{%- endif %}

Example usage:

<example_agent_descriptions>
"code-reviewer": use this agent after you are done writing a significant piece of code
"greeting-responder": use this agent to respond to user greetings with a friendly joke
</example_agent_descriptions>

<example>
user: "Please write a function that checks if a number is prime"
assistant: I'm going to use the Write tool to write the following code:
<code>
function isPrime(n) {
  if (n <= 1) return false
  for (let i = 2; i * i <= n; i++) {
    if (n % i === 0) return false
  }
  return true
}
</code>
<commentary>
Since a significant piece of code was written and the task was completed, now use the code-reviewer agent to run the tests
</commentary>
assistant: Uses the Agent tool to launch the code-reviewer agent
</example>

<example>
user: "Hello"
<commentary>
Since the user is greeting, use the greeting-responder agent to respond with a friendly joke
</commentary>
assistant: "I'm going to use the Agent tool to launch the greeting-responder agent"
</example>
```

Source: @tencent-ai/codebuddy-code 2.164.0, `product.json`, prompt `tool-agent-description` - shipped bundle, 2.164.0 (2026-10-09).

Source (description and parameters): @tencent-ai/codebuddy-code 2.164.0, `dist/codebuddy.js`, `SendMessage` tool class - shipped bundle, 2.164.0 (2026-10-09).

Semantics. The `Agent` description says to continue a previously spawned agent with "SendMessage with the agent's name as the `recipient` field - that resumes it with full context", while the `Agent` schema's `name` description writes the call as `SendMessage({to: name})`. Outside a team the tool answers "Not in a team. SendMessage is only available when you are in a team or have background agents running." The `product.json` template `tool-sendmessage-description` is a longer text that begins "# SendMessageTool".

Semantics. The tool takes no arguments. In a multitask-coordinator session it returns the live workers; otherwise it returns a JSON list of the registered agent types (name, optional display name, and description) that the `Agent` tool accepts as `subagent_type`.

#### `InterruptAgent` (cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Stop a running background sub-agent spawned from the current session (cancels the task like TaskStop). Cannot target the current session or tasks belonging to another conversation.
```

Source (description and parameters): @tencent-ai/codebuddy-code 2.164.0, `dist/codebuddy.js`, `InterruptAgent` tool class - shipped bundle, 2.164.0 (2026-10-09).

Semantics. The target is a background subagent's task id or its session id. A call naming the current session returns "Refusing to interrupt the current session. Pass the id of a background sub-agent instead.", an unknown id returns a message pointing to `TaskList`, and a task from another conversation is refused.

Description (verbatim):

```text
Stop a running background worker or shell by ID. The agent_id returned by Agent() is the task_id (same string). Prefer InterruptAgent for workers. Do not use this to wait for completion.
```

```js
ul=oL.z.object({task_id:oL.z.string().optional().describe("The ID of the background task to stop. For workers spawned by Agent(), this is the agent_id returned by that call (same string)."),shell_id:oL.z.string().optional().describe("Deprecated: use task_id instead")}).refine(eA=>eA.task_id||eA.shell_id,{message:"Either task_id or shell_id is required"})
```

Source (description and parameters): @tencent-ai/codebuddy-code 2.164.0, `dist/codebuddy.js`, `TaskStop` tool class - shipped bundle, 2.164.0 (2026-10-09).

Semantics. This is a shared stop tool for background shells and background subagents, keyed by the `agent_id` that `Agent` returns; one of `task_id` or the deprecated `shell_id` is required. The tool class lists the aliases `taskstop`, `task-stop`, `KillShell`, and `kill-shell`, and the docs give "`TaskStop` | `KillShell`" as a permission alias pair (official doc, undated). The `product.json` template `tool-taskstop-description` instead begins "- Stops a running background task by its ID".

#### `SearchRepo` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launches a new agent that searches and explores the codebase using multiple search strategies (grep, file listing, content reading). 

Returns relevant files and contextual information to answer queries about code structure, functionality, and content.

**Core capabilities:**
- File discovery and content analysis across the entire repository
- Pattern matching with regex search for specific code constructs
- Directory exploration and project structure understanding
- Intelligent file selection and content extraction with chunking for large files
- Contextual answers combining search results with code analysis

**When to use:**
- **Architecture exploration** - Understanding project structure, dependencies, and patterns
- **Refactoring preparation** - Finding all instances of functions, components, or patterns
- Delegate to subagents when the task clearly benefits from a separate agent with a new context window
```

The tool names below are field names of the `ToolCall` oneof in Warp's public protocol buffer definitions: `run_agents` (field 35), `send_message_to_agent` (field 30), and `wait_for_events` (field 36). The model-facing JSON schemas and descriptions are built on Warp's server and are not captured, so each parameter block below is the protocol buffer message, not the schema the model sees; client text that tells the model to "send any follow-up with send_message_to_agent" and a client spec that says "The model calls the server-handled `wait_for_events` tool" show the model uses these names. The same oneof also has a `subagent` variant (field 19) whose message holds `task_id`, `payload`, and metadata kinds `cli`, `research`, `advice`, `computer_use`, `summarization`, `conversation_search`, and `warp_documentation_search`; the sources do not show whether the model calls it, and a 2025 extracted Warp prompt has no subagent tool.

#### `run_agents` (spawn)

Description: not captured.

Parameters (protocol buffer message `RunAgents` from source at commit e6b8fe9, verbatim):

```protobuf
// A client tool call to start a batch of child agents that share run-wide
// configuration (model, harness, execution mode).
message RunAgents {
  message Local {}
  message Remote {
    string environment_id = 1;
    string worker_host = 2;
    // LLM-set per call based on whether the children need computer use
    // (browser automation, visual inspection, etc.). Not a user preference.
    bool computer_use_enabled = 3;
    // Optional UID of the runner (OS and resource configuration) for the
    // remote children.
    string runner_id = 4;
  }

  message ExecutionMode {
    oneof mode {
      Local local = 1;
      Remote remote = 2;
    }
  }

  // Configuration for a single child agent in the batch.
  message AgentRunConfig {
    // Display name for the child agent. Required: must be non-empty and
    // unique across the entries in a single RunAgents call. The server
    // rejects violations with
    // RunAgentsResult.Failure { error: "agent names must be non-empty and
    // unique" }.
    string name = 1 [ (sensitive) = true ];
    string prompt = 2 [ (sensitive) = true ];
    // Title for the spawned agent's task.
    string title = 3 [ (sensitive) = true ];
    // Optional UID of the named agent (service account) the child run should
    // execute as. Only valid for factory agents dispatching sibling factory
    // agents; enforced server-side at dispatch time.
    string agent_identity_uid = 4;

    // Optional, per-agent overrides.
    string model_id = 5;
    Harness harness = 6;
    ExecutionMode execution_mode = 7;
  }

  string summary = 1 [ (sensitive) = true ];
  string base_prompt = 2 [ (sensitive) = true ];
  repeated SkillRef skills = 3;
  string model_id = 4;
  Harness harness = 5;
  oneof execution_mode {
    Local local = 6;
    Remote remote = 7;
  }
  repeated AgentRunConfig agent_run_configs = 8;
  // Optional plan ID. When set and matches an OrchestrationConfigSnapshot's
  // plan_id, run-wide fields inherit from that config.
  string plan_id = 9;
}
```

Source: warp-proto-apis `apis/multi_agent/v1/task.proto`, commit `e6b8fe90b000e264a2849a1888fa8b522d1fa98f` - source at commit, 2026-10-09, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. `Harness` and `SkillRef` are defined elsewhere in the same file. The model-facing JSON schema is built on Warp's server and is not captured.

Semantics. The result is `RunAgentsResult`, whose `Launched` variant lists one `AgentOutcome` per child with its `name` and either `launched { agent_id }` or `failed { error }`, beside `Denied { reason }` and `Failure { error }` variants; the children keep running, and the parent "observes these events to decide what to do next (keep waiting, send a follow-up, spawn a replacement, finish) without polling any child" (official doc). Children emit lifecycle events "routed to lead agents" (`in_progress`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `errored`, `blocked`, `cancelled`; `started`, `idle`, and `restarted` are deprecated), and a child in a terminal state "is still addressable by its agent ID and will wake up to handle follow-up instructions when the parent sends a new message" (official doc); how these events are rendered to the model is server-side and not captured, and no model-facing cancel tool was found. A repeated launch is refused with "Requested agent(s) have already been launched: {duplicate_list}. Do not start duplicate child agents; send any follow-up with send_message_to_agent using the existing agent id(s): {addresses}." (source at commit, `run_agents.rs`). The earlier `StartAgent` (added 2026-02-25) and `StartAgentV2` variants were removed on 2026-07-22 and are now `reserved 29, 33; // Removed: StartAgent, StartAgentV2`; `RunAgents` was added on 2026-05-02 (source at commit, pull requests #299, #315, #344).

#### `wait_for_events` (wait)

Description: not captured.

Parameters (protocol buffer message `WaitForEvents` from source at commit e6b8fe9, verbatim):

```protobuf
    // A tool call indicating the agent has yielded and is waiting for inbound
    // events (a user message, an inbound message from another agent, or a
    // lifecycle event). The wait ends when either (a) a new inbound input
    // supersedes the call or (b) `idle_timeout_seconds` elapses without any
    // inbound input arriving.
    message WaitForEvents {
      // Upper bound on how long the client should wait. Unset means the client
      // should fall back to its default waiting policy.
      int32 idle_timeout_seconds = 1;
    }
```

Source: warp-proto-apis `apis/multi_agent/v1/task.proto`, commit `e6b8fe90b000e264a2849a1888fa8b522d1fa98f` - source at commit, 2026-10-09, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The model-facing JSON schema is built on Warp's server and is not captured.

Semantics. The client spec says "The model calls the server-handled `wait_for_events` tool" (source at commit, TECH.md). The result message `WaitForEventsResult {}` has no fields, and the wait ends when "a new inbound input supersedes the call" or the timeout elapses; how the inbound events are rendered to the model is server-side and not captured. The timeout is in seconds; in the client, "If `idle_timeout_seconds <= 0` (prost's "unset" sentinel), fall back to `DEFAULT_ORCHESTRATED_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30 min`", then a 30 s safety margin is subtracted and the result is floored at 5 s (source at commit, TECH.md). The `WaitForEvents` client variant was added on 2026-06-05 (source at commit, pull requests #299, #315, #344).

#### `send_message_to_agent` (message)

Description: not captured.

Parameters (protocol buffer message `SendMessageToAgent` from source at commit e6b8fe9, verbatim):

```protobuf
// A client tool call to send a message to one or more agents.
message SendMessageToAgent {
  // The agent IDs of the recipients.
  repeated string addresses = 1;
  // The subject line of the message.
  string subject = 2 [ (sensitive) = true ];
  // The body of the message.
  string message = 3 [ (sensitive) = true ];
}
```

Source: warp-proto-apis `apis/multi_agent/v1/task.proto`, commit `e6b8fe90b000e264a2849a1888fa8b522d1fa98f` - source at commit, 2026-10-09, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The model-facing JSON schema is built on Warp's server and is not captured.

Semantics. The parent addresses one or more agents by the agent IDs that `run_agents` returned. The result `SendMessageToAgentResult` is either `Success { message_id }`, where the proto calls `message_id` "The client-generated message ID", or `Error { message }`. A message to a finished child wakes it to handle the follow-up (official doc).

Grok Bot is an xAI desktop assistant whose prompt gives the model `Task` to spawn subagents and `CheckSubagent`, `MessageSubagent`, and `StopSubagent` to inspect, steer, and abort them by the Agent ID that each `Task` result returns, plus a `CloudAgent` tool for Cursor cloud agents that the same prompt says the team admin has disabled. #### `Task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Task tool launches specialized subagents (subprocesses) that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each subagent_type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

When using the Task tool, you must specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use.

VERY IMPORTANT: When broadly exploring the codebase to gather context for a large task, it is recommended that you use the Task tool with subagent_type="explore" instead of running search commands directly.

If the query is a narrow or specific question, you should NOT use the Task and instead address the query directly using the other tools available to you.

Examples:
- user: "Where is the ClientError class defined?" assistant: [Uses Grep directly - this is a needle query for a specific class]
- user: "Run this query using my database API" assistant: [Calls the MCP directly - this is not a broad exploration task]
- user: "What is the codebase structure?" assistant: [Uses the Task tool with subagent_type="explore"]

If it is possible to explore different areas of the codebase in parallel, you should launch multiple agents concurrently.

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- Simple, single or few-step tasks that can be performed by a single agent (using parallel or sequential tool calls) - just call the tools directly instead.
- For example:
  - If you want to read a specific file path, use the Read or Glob tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
  - If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the Read tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
  - If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the Glob tool instead, to find the match more quickly

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do
- Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. Specify exactly what information the agent should return back in its final response to you. Background subagent completion messages already include a user-visible summary portion; do not summarize or restate a single background subagent's result by default. Respond only when the user asks, multiple background subagents need synthesis, or the background subagent reports a blocker requiring parent action outside of the user-visible high level summary.
- Agents can be resumed using the `resume` parameter by passing the agent ID from a previous invocation. This sends a follow-up message after the agent has completed, preserving existing context. If the agent is still running, the request fails unless `interrupt` is true. Set `interrupt` to true only when the user explicitly wants to interrupt the running agent. You can also set `resume` to "self" to fork the current parent agent into a new child subagent. When NOT resuming, each invocation starts fresh and you should provide a detailed task description with all necessary context.
- In user-facing responses, you may link to agents and subagents with markdown chat links in the `[label](id)` format, using the agent ID as the link target. Do not print raw agent IDs separately.
- When using the Task tool, the subagent invocation does not have access to the user's message or prior assistant steps. Therefore, you should provide a highly detailed task description with all necessary context for the agent to perform its task autonomously.
- The subagent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the subagent which tasks you want it to perform, since it is not aware of the user's intent or your prior assistant steps (tool calls, thinking, or messages).
- If the subagent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run subagents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Task tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a code-reviewer subagent and a test-runner subagent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- Avoid delegating the full query to the Task tool and returning the result. In these cases, you should address the query using the other tools available to you.

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- computerUse: Perform manual testing of built applications and code. This subagent has access to the computer and browser to test the application. This subagent_type is stateful; if a computerUse subagent already exists, the previously created subagent will be resumed if you reuse the Task tool with subagent_type set to computerUse.
- debug: Debug specialist that uses hypothesis-driven investigation with instrumentation logs. Use when investigating reproducible bugs with non-obvious root causes. The subagent will instrument code and provide reproduction steps. After reproduction, it will analyze logs, and repeat until the root cause is found and fixed. This subagent is stateful and auto-resumes from previous context.
- videoReview: Analyze videos with an expert visual video model. Pass file paths via the `file_attachments` parameter. Use this to verify your understanding of video artifacts before referencing them in your response. For videos, always use the demo version (recording_demo.mp4), not raw. Your prompt should include: (1) what you believe is in the video, (2) questions to verify.
- vmSetupHelper: Codebase analysis helper for VM environment setup. Use this to explore the codebase structure, find setup scripts, discover dependencies, and analyze configuration. Ideal for parallel discovery tasks.
- watchVideo: Describe or analyze videos with an expert video description and analysis model. Use this subagent type to generate a description of user-provided videos, or to ask specific questions about said videos. Pass file paths via the `file_attachments` parameter. ALWAYS start by asking for a video description by asking "Describe what is happening in the attached video, in detail". You may resume the same subagent to ask more specific, detailed follow-up questions. When using, include relevant context about the video, e.g. details from the conversation about what the video may contain and why it is relevant (do not make assumptions, just share what you know). When resuming, you need not re-attach the videos.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- shell: Command execution specialist for running bash commands. Use this for git operations, command execution, and other terminal tasks.
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.

No alternative models are available. Subagents will inherit the parent model.

When an agent runs in the background, you will be automatically notified when it completes after you end your own turn - do NOT AwaitShell, poll, or proactively check on its progress. Continue with other work or end your turn instead.
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok Bot system prompt, xAI/grok-bot.md, section "3.2 Task", asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks commit 181ebcd7 - extracted prompt, added 2026-08-21; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. The system prompt says "Subagents always run in the background, so the moment you dispatch one you keep control instead of blocking on it.", while the schema keeps `run_in_background` with no stated default and the text "If this is false, you will be blocked until the agent completes." Each `Task` result gives the subagent's Agent ID, and a finished background subagent revives the parent with its result as a "hidden self-initiated wake", through a notification that "includes a user-visible summary portion"; the wording of the `Task` result and of the wake is not captured. `resume` follows up with a finished subagent and fails on a running one unless `interrupt` is true, `resume: "self"` forks the parent, and the system prompt also says that resuming an executor does not keep its context and tells the model to "re-include what matters". The `AwaitShell` tool takes a `task_id` described as "Optional shell or subagent id to poll." and its `pattern` description says "Not supported for awaiting subagents: you MUST leave this argument unset.", but the `Task` description says "do NOT AwaitShell, poll, or proactively check on its progress" and `run_in_background` says "A background subagent cannot be polled or awaited". The `subagent_type` enum lists seven values, the description's list names nine types, including `videoReview`, `cursor-guide`, and `shell` but not `mediaReview`, and the system prompt also tells the model to call `Task` with `subagent_type` "executor" for heavy work.
#### `CloudAgent` (spawn, output, status, message, list, cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Manage Cursor cloud agents - background coding agents that run on a Cursor-managed VM or self-hosted worker, edit a GitHub repo on a branch, and open a pull request. Use this to spawn coding agents that make code changes, and to enumerate, inspect, follow up on, or clean up cloud agents.

Actions:
- launch: start a new cloud agent. Requires prompt + repo_url (a GitHub repo the user has connected to Cursor); repo_url is optional when launching into a saved environment (see Environment below), which supplies its own repos. Optional starting_ref, model, model_params, title (used verbatim as the agent's title instead of the auto-generated prompt summary), and environment (where it runs - see Environment below). Returns the agent id and its cursor.com URL. You're revived automatically when the run finishes - don't poll it - and the completion message includes the path to its full transcript (auto-dumped to a file on your box), so you can inspect it with Shell or Read without calling dump.
- list: enumerate cloud agents. scope defaults to "launched" (agents started via this tool this session); pass scope: "all" to see every cloud agent on the account.
- models: list the model ids you can launch with and, per model, the params each accepts with allowed values. Use only to resolve a model or settings the user explicitly requested; do not browse the catalog to choose a model yourself.
- get: status of one agent (agent_id) - state, branch, PR, change stats. For a one-off status check; for being notified on completion, use watch instead of polling get. To read the actual code changes, use the branch from here over the GitHub API, never a local clone: `gh pr diff` for runs with a PR, or `gh api` against the branch for runs without one.
- dump: write the agent's FULL conversation transcript (agent_id) to a file on your box (under cloud-agent-transcripts/ in your working directory - the result gives the exact path), then use Shell to grep it or Read to read it. Limited to agents you manage this session (launched, watched, or replied to) - for others, 'watch' it first. Returns the path + size, not the contents. JSONL, one message per line with full detail (text, reasoning, tool calls with args, tool results). The final assistant report is the last line - `tail -n 1` it for just the final output. Works while running (partial) and when finished. Use this for mid-run inspection or to re-dump; a finished run you launched/watched is auto-dumped to the same path already (its completion message has the path). Use this instead of sending a 'reply' that asks the agent to summarize.
- watch: register to be revived automatically when an existing agent (agent_id) finishes - use this for agents you didn't launch this session (launch already watches its own). You keep working and are revived with the result; never poll get in a loop.
- reply: send a follow-up prompt to an existing agent (agent_id + prompt). By default the follow-up is queued and processed only after the agent's current turn finishes; pass interrupt: true to interrupt the in-flight turn and have the agent start working on your message immediately (no-op if it isn't currently running - it just sends normally). Like launch, you're revived automatically when the follow-up run finishes - don't poll it.
- rename: retitle an existing agent (agent_id + title). Works on a running agent, so use it when taking ownership of an in-flight run (e.g. prefixing a title) rather than relaunching. The title is used verbatim and shows on cursor.com, in the IDE sidebar, and on mobile.
- cancel / archive / unarchive: manage lifecycle (agent_id). These run immediately - no confirmation needed. Archiving keeps the agent's pull request open.
- delete: permanently delete an agent. Confirm with the user (e.g. a SendMessage widget) first, then call with confirm: true.
- list_artifacts: list files the agent saved under its workspace artifacts.

Environment (worker pools / private workers): set where the agent runs with the environment param on launch.
- Omit environment, or pass {"type":"cloud"}, for a Cursor-managed Linux VM (the default).
- Pass {"type":"pool"} to run on any eligible self-hosted pool for the repo ("shared pool" / self-hosted pool).
- Pass {"type":"pool","name":"`<pool-name>`"} for a specific named pool the user or task names (examples: "mobile-ios-mac", "mobile-ios-mac-legacy"). Use this when the work needs Mac/iOS simulators, a team's shared workers, or any runtime the default cloud VM cannot provide.
- Pass {"type":"machine","name":"`<worker-name>`"} for one specific private worker ("My Machine").
- Pass {"type":"environment","name":"`<environment-name>`"} (or "id" with its public id) to launch into a saved Cloud Agents environment from the user's cursor.com dashboard - the run gets that environment's custom env vars, egress rules, install commands, and (for multi-repo environments) all configured repos, on a Cursor VM. repo_url is then optional and defaults to the environment's primary repo. Use this when the user names a saved environment or the task needs specific environment variables or egress settings.
- For pool and machine, a single active team is selected automatically; set team_id only when the user belongs to multiple active teams.
- If the user asks to launch on a pool / self-hosted workers / a named pool / a saved environment, pass environment on that same launch call.

Model configuration: only pass model (id) and model_params (structured params like thinking/effort/context/fast) when the user explicitly requests that model or those settings for this cloud agent. model_params requires model because parameter schemas are model-specific. Never select a model based on the task, catalog order, availability, or your own preference. For a user-requested override, discover valid ids and per-model params/values with the 'models' action first; params are validated against the catalog. Otherwise omit both: a launch uses the user's saved/team/global cloud-agent default, while a reply keeps the cloud agent's current model. Never encode params into the model id string - keep model a clean id and put settings in model_params.

Attaching images: on launch and reply, pass images: [{"url":"`file:///workspace/shot.png`"}] to show the cloud agent a screenshot, mock, chart, or repro. The agent actually sees them, so never paste an image as a markdown ![](...) in the prompt. Use absolute `file://` URLs - a path in your own box (`file:///workspace/…`) or a host attachment path; `https://` is rejected, so download such an image to a file first. There is no caption field: say what each image shows in the prompt text.

Cloud agents run remotely and do not edit the user's local files - results come back as a branch/PR. Authentication is handled for the signed-in user; never ask for an API key.
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok Bot system prompt, xAI/grok-bot.md, section "3.28 CloudAgent", asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks commit 181ebcd7 - extracted prompt, added 2026-08-21; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. One tool with an `action` enum covers launch, list, models, get, dump, watch, reply, rename, cancel, archive, unarchive, delete, and list_artifacts; `launch` "Returns the agent id and its cursor.com URL", and the parent is "revived automatically when the run finishes" with a completion message that "includes the path to its full transcript". `reply` queues a follow-up by default and interrupts the running turn when `interrupt` is true, `watch` registers revival for agents not launched in the session, `cancel` stops the active run, and `list` defaults to scope "launched" and a limit of 20. Agent ids follow the form shown in the `agent_id` description, "The agent id (bc-…).", and the wording of the completion message is not captured. The same prompt says "Your team's admin has disabled Cursor cloud agents in Grok Bot, so the CloudAgent tool is not available to you here" and "Never claim you can launch or manage a cloud agent.", so in this capture the definition is present but the model is told the tool is unavailable.

#### `CheckSubagent` (status, list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Check how a background subagent you dispatched (via Task) is doing without waiting for it to finish. Returns its status, how long it has been running, the tool calls it has made recently, and a path to its live transcript you can Read for the full play-by-play. Pass the subagent's Agent ID (from the Task result), or omit it to list every running subagent. Use this when a subagent - especially a computerUse one driving the box desktop - is taking a long time or might be stuck or looping, so you can decide whether to MessageSubagent it or StopSubagent it. This is read-only; it's not polling for completion (you're revived automatically when a subagent finishes).
```

Parameters (JSON Schema as given in the extracted prompt, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "subagent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The Agent ID of the subagent to inspect (from the Task tool result that dispatched it). Omit to list every subagent currently running."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
}
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok Bot system prompt, xAI/grok-bot.md, section "3.49 CheckSubagent", asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks commit 181ebcd7 - extracted prompt, added 2026-08-21; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. The call is read-only: with a `subagent_id` it returns that subagent's status, running time, recent tool calls, and a path to its live transcript, and without one it lists every running subagent; the result format is not captured. The system prompt tells the model to "Proactively CheckSubagent on it (periodically, and always before you tell the user it's "still working")" and to "Use it to spot trouble, not to poll for completion", and the description says completion still arrives by revival: "you're revived automatically when a subagent finishes".

#### `MessageSubagent` (message)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Force a message into a running background subagent to course-correct it without aborting it. The subagent interrupts its current step, reads your message, and continues from where it was (its context is preserved - it does not start over). Use this to unstick or redirect a subagent that is looping, stuck, or heading the wrong way - for example to tell a computerUse subagent to try a different element, that the user just signed in so it can proceed, or to wrap up and report what it has. Pass the subagent's Agent ID (from the Task result). You're still revived with its result when it finishes; to follow up AFTER a subagent has already finished, use Task with the resume parameter instead.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema as given in the extracted prompt, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "subagent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The Agent ID of the running subagent to message (from the Task tool result that dispatched it)."
    },
    "message": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The instruction to inject. The subagent interrupts what it is doing, reads this, and continues from where it was with its context intact."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "subagent_id",
    "message"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
}
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok Bot system prompt, xAI/grok-bot.md, section "3.50 MessageSubagent", asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks commit 181ebcd7 - extracted prompt, added 2026-08-21; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. The subagent "interrupts its current step, reads your message, and continues from where it was" with its context kept, and the parent is "still revived with its result when it finishes"; the tool's result text is not captured. A follow-up to a finished subagent goes through `Task` with `resume` instead, and the system prompt says "A follow-up or correction to work already running is NOT a new executor: steer it into the running one with MessageSubagent (its context is kept)." Both `subagent_id` and `message` are required and must be non-empty (`minLength` 1).

#### `StopSubagent` (cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Abort a running background subagent you dispatched (via Task). Use this to kill a subagent that is wedged, looping with no progress, or no longer needed - for example a computerUse subagent stuck on the box desktop. This tears the subagent down and frees its box desktop window; it does not come back, and you are not separately revived for it (this tool's result is the confirmation). If you instead want it to change course and keep going, use MessageSubagent. Pass the subagent's Agent ID (from the Task result).
```

Parameters (JSON Schema as given in the extracted prompt, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "subagent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The Agent ID of the running subagent to abort (from the Task tool result that dispatched it)."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "subagent_id"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
}
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok Bot system prompt, xAI/grok-bot.md, section "3.51 StopSubagent", asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks commit 181ebcd7 - extracted prompt, added 2026-08-21; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. The call "tears the subagent down and frees its box desktop window"; the subagent "does not come back", and the parent is "not separately revived for it (this tool's result is the confirmation)". The confirmation text is not captured. The system prompt pairs it with `MessageSubagent` and says StopSubagent "aborts one for good when it's wedged or no longer needed".

#### `task` (spawn; web app)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Start a subagent that works on a task independently and reports back.
Agent types:
- **general-purpose**: General purpose agent for multi-step tasks. Has access to: run_terminal_cmd, read_file, search_replace, list_dir, grep, web_search, and todo_write.
- **explore**: Fast, read-only agent specialized for codebase exploration. Read-only - has access to: read_file, list_dir, grep.
- **plan**: Software architect for planning implementation strategies. Read-only - has access to: read_file, list_dir, grep, web_search, and todo_write. File editing and command execution are not available.
```

Semantics. `run_in_background` defaults to `true`, and a background call returns "Subagent started in background." followed by `subagent_id: {subagent_id}` and `description: {description}` lines and "When you need its result, use {task_output_tool} with {task_ids_param}=["{subagent_id}"] and a positive {timeout_ms_param}.", whose placeholders default to `get_task_output`, `task_ids`, and `timeout_ms` (source at commit, task.rs). A finished subagent's result is its output text followed by `<subagent_meta>id={subagent_id}, tool_calls={tool_calls}, turns={turns}, duration_ms={duration_ms}</subagent_meta>` and a `<subagent_result>` block holding `subagent_id: {subagent_id}` and "To continue this subagent's conversation, use resume_from="{subagent_id}"." (source at commit, task.rs). A foreground call that outlasts its budget returns "Subagent took longer than the foreground budget and was moved to the background to keep the conversation responsive. It is still running - you will be notified when it completes.", where the clause after "running" appears only for clients that deliver system reminders; the wake text the model receives on completion is not captured (source at commit, task.rs). #### `spawn_subagent` (spawn; CLI)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Start a subagent that works on a task independently and reports back.

## Usage notes
- When the agent is done, it returns a single message with its agent ID. Use that ID to resume the agent later for follow-up work.
- background: Returns immediately with a subagent_id. Use get_command_or_subagent_output to retrieve results. This is set to true by default.
- Subagents receive a compacted version of project instructions (AGENTS.md). If the task requires detailed conventions (e.g., build rules, testing patterns), include the relevant rules directly in the prompt.
- When launching independent subagents, you MUST incorporate the results into the task based on requirements BEFORE concluding.

Resuming a previous agent (resume_from):
- Use resume_from to continue a previously completed subagent's conversation. Pass the subagent_id returned by a prior spawn_subagent call. A resumed agent keeps its full transcript and tool state, so you only need to describe what changed since the last run - don't re-explain the original task.

Isolation mode:
- Use isolation to control the child's execution environment. With "worktree", the child runs in an isolated git worktree whose edits don't affect the parent workspace; the worktree is preserved after completion and its path is returned in the output.
```

Semantics. `background` defaults to `true`; the user guide at commit 2bdd1d6 lists the same parameter as `run_in_background`, and the source's description builder takes that parameter's name from the host (`run_in_background_param`) (source at commit, user guide and task.rs). The started, auto-backgrounded, and completion texts, including the `<subagent_meta>` and `<subagent_result>` tags, come from the same source format strings described under `task` (source at commit, task.rs). The capture has no `subagent_type` or `model`; the user guide says "`spawn_subagent` has an optional `subagent_type` enum when plugin, project, or user agents exist" and "Built-in names and xAI-bundled agents are not listed" (source at commit, user guide). The default nesting limit is `MAX_SUBAGENT_DEPTH: u32 = 1` ("Default max nesting depth when [`MaxSubagentDepth`] is not injected") (source at commit, task/mod.rs). Subagents are on by default and are turned off with `grok --no-subagents`, `GROK_SUBAGENTS=0`, or `[subagents] enabled = false` (source at commit, user guide).

Source (description and parameters): Grok Build web app system prompt, `xAI/grok-build.md` in asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks at commit `181ebcd703f377a71fd87e21ca6839b54ccfae67`, section "get_task_output" - extracted prompt, self-dated April 2026, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. A positive `timeout_ms` (milliseconds) blocks until every listed task completes or the wait ends; omitting it or passing 0 returns a non-blocking status snapshot. In the source at commit 2bdd1d6, the wait ceiling is per session and defaults to `3_600_000` ms ("One hour"), which hosts can lower with `GROK_MAX_WAIT_BLOCK_MS`; one call takes at most 20 ids (`MAX_MULTI_WAIT_IDS`); and `task_ids` also accepts a singular `task_id` key on the wire, because "Models frequently mirror `kill_task`'s singular `task_id` here" (source at commit, task.rs). When this tool returns a finished subagent, the `<subagent_result>` resume footer is rendered "e.g. in the `get_task_output` path" (source at commit, task.rs), and the web prompt warns that "consuming a task's output suppresses its completion notification". The source builds this tool's description with added "Usage notes:" lines, the form the CLI capture shows for `get_command_or_subagent_output` (source at commit, task.rs).

#### `get_command_or_subagent_output` (output, wait, status; CLI)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Get output and status from a background task, monitor, or subagent.

Usage notes:
- Pass task_ids with one or more ids from background=true commands or subagents (a monitor's task_id is returned by monitor); for a single task use a one-element array. Multiple ids with a positive timeout_ms wait until all complete
- Omit timeout_ms or pass 0 for a non-blocking status snapshot; set a positive timeout_ms to wait up to that many milliseconds, capped at 3600000 (~1 h)
- Returns current output, status, and exit code if completed
- If output is large, use read_file on the output_file path
```

#### `send_subagent_message` (message; CLI)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Send a message to a subagent that this session owns. An eligible completed subagent resumes with the same identity. Use this tool to add a fact or correct a wrong target. Do not use this tool to tell a subagent to stop, send its result now, or stop reading and start writing. There is no time limit, whatever the subagent shows. Trust the subagent and let it run to completion, unless it needs guidance or more information.
```

Parameters (Rust input types from source at commit 2bdd1d6, verbatim):

```rust
/// How the message reaches an active subagent. An inactive subagent always
/// wakes and runs the text as its next turn.
#[derive(
    Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema,
)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SendSubagentMessageDelivery {
    /// Join the current turn at its next safe point (default).
    Steer,
    /// Wait as a later turn.
    Queue,
    /// Arrives before a pending steer. It interrupts a subagent waiting on background work.
    Interject,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct SendSubagentMessageInput {
    /// The durable agent ID of the target subagent.
    pub subagent_id: String,
    /// Text to send to the subagent.
    pub text: String,
    /// Delivery operation; omitted means `steer`.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub delivery: Option<SendSubagentMessageDelivery>,
    /// Legacy `queue: true`; accepted on the wire, hidden from the schema,
    /// ignored when `delivery` is present.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(skip)]
    pub queue: bool,
}
```

Source (description and parameters): grok-build `crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools/src/implementations/grok_build/send_subagent_message.rs`, commit `2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8` - source at commit, 2026-09-29, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description is the tool's `description_template` string with its Rust line continuations joined; the types derive `schemars::JsonSchema`, and the generated JSON is not captured.

Semantics. "The `send_subagent_message` tool is off by default. Enable it with `GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES` or `[features] active_agent_messages`", and when it is on, a granted child can target its parent with `subagent_id: "parent"` (source at commit, user guide "Subagents and Personas"). An inactive subagent wakes with the message as its next turn; for an active one, `steer` (the default) joins the current turn at its next safe point, `queue` waits as a later turn, and `interject` is delivered ahead of pending steers and interrupts a subagent blocked on background work (source at commit, user guide). "Child senders are bounded: 4 in-flight messages per sender-target pair, and 32 outbound messages per sender attempt. A send over the limit returns `QuotaExceeded`." (source at commit, user guide). The result text includes "Message accepted (message_id: {message_id})." and "Subagent not found or not owned by this session.". The tool does not appear in the CLI capture.

#### `kill_task` (cancel; web app)

Description (verbatim):


The capture sorts tools into groups: `Agent`, `TaskOutput`, `TaskStop`, and `SendMessage` are in "activeReceiptVerified"; the child-side `RespondToCoordinator` is in "inactiveProviderContracts", so it was not active in the captured parent session; and a `Task` alias sits in "inactiveRegistryAliases" with `"providerVisible": false`. That alias's description begins "Claude Code-compatible alias for the Agent tool. Use this when plugin instructions ask for the Task tool." and then repeats the `Agent` description.

#### `Agent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types and the tools they have access to:
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches - when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files - delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself - wait for the result.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user - relay what matters.
- A new Agent call starts fresh, so the prompt must be self-contained.
- `run_in_background: true` runs the agent asynchronously; you'll be notified when it completes.
- When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
```

Semantics. A foreground call blocks and returns the subagent's final message as the tool result; `run_in_background: true` runs it asynchronously, and the schema has no default for that flag. Background completion is injected as a block that opens with "[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]" and "This is an automated task event, NOT a message from the user.", followed by a `<task-notification>` element with fields including `task-id`, `tool-use-id`, `task-type`, `agent-id`, `subagent-type`, `output-file`, `status`, `summary`, `result`, `error`, and `usage` (extracted prompt, repository HEAD 2026-09-22). An omitted `subagent_type` selects `general-purpose`, and a completed subagent is resumed through `SendMessage` with its `agentId`.

#### `TaskOutput` (output, wait)

Description (verbatim):

```text
DEPRECATED: Background tasks return their output file path in the tool result, and you receive a <task-notification> with the same path when the task completes.
- For bash tasks: prefer using the Read tool on that output file path - it contains stdout/stderr.
- For local_agent tasks: use the Agent tool result directly. Do NOT Read the .output file - it is a symlink to the full subagent conversation transcript (JSONL) and will overflow your context window.
- For remote_agent tasks: prefer using the Read tool on the output file path - it contains the streamed remote session output (same as bash).

- Retrieves output from a running or completed task (background shell, agent, or remote session)
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task
- Returns the task output along with status information
- Use block=true (default) to wait for task completion
- Use block=false for non-blocking check of current status
- Task IDs can be found using the /tasks command
- Works with all task types: background shells, async agents, and remote sessions
```

```text
Usage:
```

## Part 2: Open-source harnesses and frameworks (42 entries)

These 42 entries describe code at the pinned commit named in each entry. Fifteen are agent frameworks or SDKs: Agno, AWS Strands Agents harness, AWS Strands Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK, Hugging Face smolagents, LangGraph Supervisor, LangGraph Swarm, Letta V1 server, LlamaIndex AgentWorkflow, Mastra, Microsoft Agent Framework, Microsoft AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI Harness. They count as harnesses here because they give the model subagent tools. LangChain Deep Agents ships a library and a coding agent built on it with the same model-facing tools, so it has one entry. Letta's retired V1 server and its current Letta Code agent give the model different tools, so each has its own entry.

A `Team` leader gets delegation tools by mode (`TeamMode`, `mode.py`): `coordinate` (the default) and `route` give `delegate_task_to_member`, `broadcast` gives `delegate_task_to_members`, and `tasks` gives `execute_task` and `execute_tasks_parallel` together with task-list tools (`create_task`, `update_task_status`, `list_tasks`, `add_task_note`, `mark_all_complete`) that record tasks, assignees, notes, and status without running a member (`_init.py:216-231`, `team/_tools.py:263-333`, `_task_tools.py:179-313`, `:1258-1272`). An optional `get_member_information` tool lists the members outside `tasks` mode. Agno builds each tool description from the docstring's short and long description and each parameter description from its `Args:` entry, prefixed with the declared type in parentheses, such as "(str) ..." (`function.py:363-382`, `:1529-1542`).

#### `delegate_task_to_member` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Use this function to delegate a task to the selected team member.
```

Parameters (Python function signature and docstring, verbatim; Agno builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
    def delegate_task_to_member(member_id: str, task: str) -> Iterator[Union[RunOutputEvent, TeamRunOutputEvent, str]]:
        """Use this function to delegate a task to the selected team member.

        Args:
            member_id (str): The ID of the member to delegate the task to, exactly as it appears in <team_members>.
            task (str): A clear and concise description of the task the member should achieve, including what a good result looks like.
        Returns:
            str: The result of the delegated task.
        """
```

Source (description and parameters): Agno `libs/agno/agno/team/_default_tools.py:694-702` (sync) and `:872-882` (async variant, same docstring), commit `24bc39f` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is the docstring's short description as `get_entrypoint_docstring` extracts it (`function.py:363-382`).

Semantics. The tool is registered with `Function.from_callable(delegate_function, name="delegate_task_to_member")` (`_default_tools.py:1517`); the call blocks, runs the member on `task` (or on the user's input when `determine_input_for_members` is `False`), and returns the member's result as the tool result, streaming member events when streaming is on. An unknown id returns `f"Member with ID {member_id} not found in the team or any subteams. Please choose the correct member from the list of members:\n\n{team.get_members_system_message_content(indent=0, run_context=run_context)}"` (`:704-708`). In `route` mode (`respond_directly=True`) the tool gets `stop_after_tool_call = True` and `show_result = True`, so the team run stops after the call and the member's response is shown as the answer (`:1519-1521`). In Agno v1.7.0 the coordinate-mode tool was `transfer_task_to_member(member_id: str, task_description: str, expected_output: Optional[str] = None)` and the route-mode tool was `forward_task_to_member(member_id: str, expected_output: Optional[str] = None)` (`team.py` at tag v1.7.0); Agno renamed `transfer_` to `delegate_` and `task_description` to `task`, and the rename date is not in the sources.

Semantics. The tool is registered with `Function.from_callable(delegate_function, name="delegate_task_to_members")` when `delegate_to_all_members` is set, which `broadcast` mode does (`_default_tools.py:1504-1510`, `_init.py:219-221`). The call blocks and yields each member's result; "``arun`` runs the members concurrently; ``run`` runs them in sequence." (`mode.py:18-21`), and in the concurrent path a failing member yields `f"Agent {member_name_fallback}: Error - {raw!s}"` (`_default_tools.py:1483-1499`). #### `execute_task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Execute a task by delegating it to a team member. The member will receive the task

```

Parameters (Python function signature and docstring, verbatim; Agno builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
    def execute_task(task_id: str, member_id: str) -> Iterator[Union[RunOutputEvent, TeamRunOutputEvent, str]]:
        """Execute a task by delegating it to a team member. The member will receive the task
        description and return a result.

        Args:
            task_id (str): The ID of the task to execute.

        Returns:
```

Source (description and parameters): Agno `libs/agno/agno/team/_task_tools.py:482-491` (sync) and `:663-674` (async variant, same docstring), commit `24bc39f` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description joins the docstring's short and long description with a newline (`function.py:363-382`).

Semantics. In `tasks` mode the leader first records tasks with `create_task` (title, description, assignee, `depends_on`); `execute_task` marks the task `in_progress`, sets its assignee to `member_id`, runs the member on the task's description (or its title), and returns the member's result as the tool result (`_task_tools.py:492-530`). The call blocks. A missing or finished task returns `f"Task with ID '{task_id}' not found."` or `f"Task [{task_id}] is {task.status.value} and cannot be executed."`, and an unknown member returns a "Member with ID {member_id} not found. Available members:" message (`:492-504`).

#### `execute_tasks_parallel` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Execute multiple independent tasks in parallel by delegating each to its assigned member.
All tasks must be pending with no unresolved dependencies.
```

Parameters (Python function signature and docstring, verbatim; Agno builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
    def execute_tasks_parallel(task_ids: List[str]) -> Iterator[Union[RunOutputEvent, TeamRunOutputEvent, str]]:
        """Execute multiple independent tasks in parallel by delegating each to its assigned member.
        All tasks must be pending with no unresolved dependencies.

        Args:
            task_ids (list): List of task IDs to execute concurrently.
        Returns:
            str: Aggregated results from all task executions.
        """
```

Source (description and parameters): Agno `libs/agno/agno/team/_task_tools.py:855-863` (sync) and `:1059-1069` (async variant, same docstring), commit `24bc39f` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description joins the docstring's short and long description with a newline (`function.py:363-382`).

Semantics. The call checks that every task exists, is `pending` or `in_progress`, and has an assignee (otherwise `f"Task [{tid}] has no assignee. Assign a member_id first."`), marks them `in_progress`, runs the assigned members concurrently in a thread pool with one worker per task (`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(tasks_to_run))`), and returns the aggregated results joined by newlines (`_task_tools.py:865-895`, `:945`, `:1054`). The call blocks until all members finish; there is no task-level cancel tool.

The registered `Team.get_member_information` method has no docstring at this commit; the module function it calls has the docstring "Get information about the members of the team, including their IDs, names, and roles." (`team/_tools.py:513-515`). `Function.from_callable` drops `run_context` from the schema (`function.py:1505-1506`).

Semantics. The tool is added only when `get_member_information_tool=True` (default `False`) and the team is not in `tasks` mode (`team.py:245`, `team/_tools.py:291-333`). It returns `team.get_members_system_message_content(indent=0, run_context=run_context)` (`team.py:1574-1575`, `team/_tools.py:513-515`). The call is synchronous and takes no model arguments.

#### `delegate` (spawn, status, list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch and manage asynchronous agent processes. This tool allows you to delegate tasks to agents that run independently in the background.

Operations:
- launch: Start a new task with an agent (requires task parameter, agent is optional)
- status: Check agent status and get full output if completed. Agent is optional - defaults to 'all' if not specified

If no agent is specified for launch, uses 'default_agent'. Only one task can run per agent at a time. Files are stored in ~/.aws/amazonq/.subagents/

IMPORTANT: If a specific agent is requested but not found, DO NOT automatically retry with 'default_agent' or any other agent. Simply report the error and available agents to the user.

Example usage:
1. Launch with agent: {"operation": "launch", "agent": "rust-agent", "task": "Create a snake game"}
2. Launch without agent: {"operation": "launch", "task": "Write a Python script"}
3. Check specific agent: {"operation": "status", "agent": "rust-agent"}
4. Check all agents: {"operation": "status", "agent": "all"}
5. Check all agents (shorthand): {"operation": "status"}
```

Parameters (JSON Schema `input_schema` from source at commit 15cc8f3c, verbatim):

```json
    "input_schema": {
      "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "operation": {
            "description": "Operation to perform: launch, status, or list",
            "$ref": "#/$defs/Operation"
          },
          "agent": {
            "description": "Agent name to use (optional - uses \"q_cli_default\" if not specified)",
            "type": [
              "string",
              "null"
            ],
            "default": null
          },
          "task": {
            "description": "Task description (required for launch operation). This process is supposed to be async. DO NOT query immediately after launching a task.",
            "type": [
              "string",
              "null"
            ],
            "default": null
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "operation"
        ],
        "$defs": {
          "Operation": {
            "oneOf": [
              {
                "description": "Launch a new agent with a specified task",
                "type": "string",
                "const": "launch"
              },
              {
                "description": "Check the status of a specific agent or all agents if None is provided",
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "status": {
                    "type": [
                      "string",
                      "null"
                    ]
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "status"
                ],
                "additionalProperties": false
              },
              {
                "description": "List all available agents",
                "type": "string",
                "const": "list"
              }
            ]
          }
        },
        "required": ["operation"]
    }
```

Source (description and parameters): Amazon Q Developer CLI source, `crates/chat-cli/src/cli/chat/tools/tool_index.json` (the `delegate` entry; the description is the decoded JSON string, and the schema keeps the file's indentation and its two `required` keys), commit `15cc8f3c` - source at commit, 2026-04-23 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. `launch` starts a subagent in the background and the call returns without waiting; the launch result format is not in the sources. `status` reads a subagent's state and, per the experiments doc, "Reading specific agents automatically reads the full std output from disk of the run."; `list` shows the agents available for delegation, and only one task can run per agent at a time. The experiments doc says "When a background task completes, you'll see a notification at your next prompt" with the task status (SUCCESS/FAILED), completion time, task description, and an AI-generated summary, and "The summary is automatically added to your conversation context" (`docs/experiments.md`, source at commit). The fallback agent is named 'default_agent' in the description and "q_cli_default" in the `agent` parameter; the description stores files in `~/.aws/amazonq/.subagents/`, while the experiments doc says `.amazonq/.subagents/` "in your current directory". Per the experiments doc, tasks with a named agent require explicit approval, and tasks without an agent "run with trust-all permissions and show a warning".
