`create_harness` enables `subagent` by default (the default built-in set is `["shell", "read", "write", "edit", "web_fetch", "web_search", "programmatic_tool_caller", "subagent"]`, `agent.py:302-303`); the harness also turns on SDK Background Tasks by default and always runs `subagent` as a background task, so the model also sees the SDK's `strands_manage_background_task` (`agent.py:210-235`, `:328-332`). Developers can replace the default with a tool built by `make_subagent` (custom roles, model tiers, fixed prompts), whose schema follows the configured axis modes (`agent.py:318-327`).

#### `subagent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent that runs in its own context and returns a final report. Reach for this when a subtask would otherwise flood your context with intermediate work and you only need its conclusion. Do not poll for progress or redo its work.

Available subagents (agent_type):
- generalist: a general-purpose agent for a focused subtask that runs in its own context
```

Source: Strands harness `harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/subagent.py:635-643` (base text), `:161-165` (role list), `:121-132` and `:760` (the `generalist` preset), commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The second paragraph is generated from the preset map; the default harness tool has the single preset `generalist`, and a tool built with no presets has only the first paragraph.

Parameters (Python functions that build the JSON Schema, verbatim):

```python
def _choice_prop(choice: Choice, base: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
    """A ``string`` enum prop (an array-of-enum when ``choice.multiple``); per-option descriptions
    render into the prop's ``description`` so each value guides the model (JSON Schema has no
    per-enum-value doc)."""
    options = choice.normalized()
    values = [o.name for o in options]
    lines = [f"- {o.name}: {o.description}" for o in options if o.description]
    desc = base
    if lines:
        block = "Options:\n" + "\n".join(lines)
        desc = f"{base}\n{block}" if base else block
    prop: dict[str, Any] = (
        {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "enum": values}}
        if choice.multiple
        else {"type": "string", "enum": values}
    )
    if desc:
        prop["description"] = desc
    return prop


def _build_schema(
    *,
    presets: Mapping[str, Preset],
    instructions: Any,
    tools: Any,
    mcp_servers: Any,
    model: Any,
    context: Any,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Derive the input schema from the axis modes: each axis adds zero or one parameter."""
    props: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The self-contained task, including all context the subagent needs. It "
            "starts from a blank conversation and cannot ask follow-up questions.",
        }
    }
    required = ["task"]

    if presets:
        props["agent_type"] = {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": list(presets),
            "description": "Which subagent role to use. Omit to use the default.",
        }

    if isinstance(instructions, Open):
        props["instructions"] = {"type": "string", "description": "A system prompt defining the subagent's role."}
    elif isinstance(instructions, Choice):
        props["instructions"] = _choice_prop(instructions, "A system prompt defining the subagent's role.")

    if isinstance(tools, Choice):
        props["tools"] = _choice_prop(
            tools, "Subset of tools to grant the subagent. Fewer is safer; it cannot exceed your own."
        )

    if isinstance(mcp_servers, Choice):
        props["mcp_servers"] = _choice_prop(
            mcp_servers,
            "Subset of MCP servers whose tools to grant the subagent. Fewer is safer; it cannot "
            "exceed your own. Omit to grant all of them.",
        )

    if isinstance(model, Choice):
        props["model"] = _choice_prop(model, "Which model the subagent runs on.")

    if isinstance(context, Choice):
        props["context"] = _choice_prop(
            context,
            "How much of this conversation the subagent sees: 'none' (fresh start), 'all' (full "
            "history including tool calls and their results - can be large), 'no_tools' (text turns "
            "only - tool calls and their results removed). More context costs more tokens.",
        )
        if any(str(o.value) != "none" for o in context.normalized()):
            props["last_messages"] = {
                "type": "integer",
                "description": "Optional: limit the shared context to the last N messages. Omit to "
                "share all of the selected context.",
            }

    return {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required}
```

Source: Strands harness `harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/subagent.py:168-249`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). In the default harness tool, `task`, `agent_type` (enum `["generalist"]`), `instructions`, `tools` (array of enum over the parent's enabled built-in tools other than `web_search`, plus its named consumer tools), `context` (enum `none`, `all`, `no_tools`), and `last_messages` are present, `mcp_servers` appears only when the parent has named MCP clients, and `model` is absent (`subagent.py:599-620`, `:755-766`).

Semantics. The harness puts `subagent` in the SDK Background Tasks `always` policy (`_ALWAYS_BACKGROUND_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({"subagent"})`, `agent.py:69-71`, `:210-235`), so every call returns the SDK's "Background task dispatched." acknowledgement at once and the subagent's final text arrives later as a synthetic `strands_manage_background_task` "get" call; by default "The invocation waits for completion and continues with the result." (`agent.py:328-332`). Each call builds a fresh child through the same `create_harness` factory: the child inherits the parent's model, built-in tools, plugins, skills, and hooks, may be granted a subset of tools and MCP servers but never more, and searches the parent's memory read-only (`agent.py:318-324`, `subagent.py:687-766`). `context` sets how much of the parent conversation the child sees: `none` (the `generalist` default), `all` (the parent's messages, forked), or `no_tools` (text turns rendered into a `<parent_context>` block) (`subagent.py:346-458`). Depth is bounded by `max_depth`, default `DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_MAX_DEPTH = 2` (`defaults.py:33`), and at the limit the tool returns "Delegation depth limit reached ({self._max_depth} levels); you cannot delegate further. Complete this task yourself instead of calling subagent again." (`subagent.py:513-529`). Other error results are "Subagent produced no result.", "Subagent was cancelled.", and "Subagent error: {exc}" (`subagent.py:550-573`).

#### `strands_manage_background_task` (output, status, list, cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
List, get, or cancel background tasks. Results are delivered automatically as synthetic 'get' calls. Do not poll for results.
```

Parameters (Python method signature and docstring, verbatim; the `@tool` decorator builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
    async def _manage_background_task(
        self, mode: Literal["list", "get", "cancel"], task_id: str | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Manage tracked background tasks.

        Args:
            mode: Whether to list, inspect, or cancel background tasks.
            task_id: The background task ID returned when the task was dispatched. Required for get and cancel.
        """
```

Source (description and parameters): Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/background_tasks/_background_tasks.py:124-139`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The tool comes from the SDK's Background Tasks plugin, which the harness turns on by default (`agent.py:210-235`).

Semantics. A `subagent` call returns "Background task dispatched.\n\nTask ID: {task['task_id']}\nTool: {task['tool_name']}\nStatus: {task['status']}\n\nThe task is running in the background. Continue without waiting or polling.\nThe final result will be delivered automatically when the task completes." (`_background_tasks.py:210-222`). When the subagent finishes, the SDK appends a synthetic assistant `toolUse` of this tool with `{"mode": "get", "task_id": ...}` and the matching `toolResult` (task metadata as JSON plus the result content) before the next model call (`:365-415`, `:518-520`). Mode `list` returns each task's `task_id`, `tool_name`, and `status`, and mode `cancel` stops a running task and returns its `task_id` and `status` (`:140-158`). For other tools, the harness default policy lets the model choose background execution through the `_background_execution` flag ("by default, the model may choose background execution for any other compatible tool", `agent.py:328-330`).

The Python SDK gives the model agents as tools through `Agent.as_tool()` (one tool per child, named after the agent), the swarm handoff tool `handoff_to_agent`, and, when Background Tasks are configured on an agent, the management tool `strands_manage_background_task` plus a per-call `_background_execution` flag on eligible tools. The community package strands-agents/tools adds `use_agent` and `swarm`, which build and run nested agents with the SDK. The repository is a monorepo (`strands-py`, `strands-ts`, `harness-py`, `harness-ts`); tool names in the TypeScript packages are not in the sources.

#### `<agent_name>` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
description or agent.description or f"Use the {name} agent as a tool by providing a natural language input"
```

Source: Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/agent/_agent_as_tool.py:98-102`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is the `description` argument to `as_tool()`, else the agent's own description, else the default string shown; with `delegate=True` the SDK appends " Calling this tool will return its response directly to the user as the final answer. It should be the only tool called in the turn." (`:31-34`).

Parameters (Python `tool_spec` property returning the JSON Schema, verbatim):

```python
    @property
    def tool_spec(self) -> ToolSpec:
        """Get the tool specification."""
        return {
            "name": self._tool_name,
            "description": self._description,
            "inputSchema": {
                "json": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "input": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "The input to send to the agent tool.",
                        },
                    },
                    "required": ["input"],
                }
            },
        }
```

Source: Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/agent/_agent_as_tool.py:139-157`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The tool name is the `name` argument to `as_tool()`, which "Defaults to the agent's name" and "Must match the pattern ``[a-zA-Z0-9_\\-]{1,64}``" (`agent.py:1135-1136`, `:1167-1168`), and the schema shown is what the SDK generates for every child. The call blocks: the wrapped agent runs on `input` and the tool result is its text response; with the default `preserve_context=False`, the agent's messages and state reset to their construction-time values before each call (`_agent_as_tool.py:81-85`). A second call while the same agent tool is busy returns the error "Agent '{self._tool_name}' is already processing a request" (`:212`), and cancelling the parent's tool call cancels the sub-agent (`:229-238`). When Background Tasks are configured, an agent tool can take `_background_execution` and run in the background, except an agent tool made with `delegate=True`, which never runs in the background (`_background_tasks.py:434-443`).

#### `use_agent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Start a new AI event loop with a specified prompt and optionally different model.

This function creates a new Strands Agent instance with the provided system prompt,
optionally using a different model provider than the parent agent, runs it with the
specified prompt, and returns the response with performance metrics.

How It Works:
------------
1. Determines which model to use (parent's model, specified provider, or environment)
2. Creates a new Agent instance with the model and system prompt
3. The agent processes the given prompt in its own isolated context
4. The response and metrics are captured and returned in a structured format
5. The new agent instance exists only for the duration of this function call

Model Selection Process:
----------------------
1. If model_provider is None: Uses parent agent's model (original behavior)
2. If model_provider is "env": Uses environment variables (STRANDS_PROVIDER, etc.)
3. If model_provider is specified: Uses that provider with optional custom config
4. Model utilities handle all provider-specific configuration automatically

Common Use Cases:
---------------
- Multi-model workflows: Use different models for different tasks
- Model comparison: Compare responses from different providers
- Cost optimization: Use cheaper models for simple tasks
- Specialized models: Use domain-specific models (code, math, creative)
- Fallback strategies: Switch to alternative models if primary fails

        Examples: ["calculator", "file_read", "retrieve"]
        If not provided, inherits all tools from the parent agent.
    model_provider: Model provider to use for the nested agent.
        Options: "bedrock", "anthropic", "litellm", "llamaapi", "ollama", "openai", "github"
        Special values:
        - None: Use parent agent's model (default, preserves original behavior)
        - "env": Use environment variables to determine provider
        Examples: "bedrock", anthropic", "litellm", "env"
    model_settings: Optional custom configuration for the model.
        If not provided, uses default configuration for the provider.
        Example: {"model_id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "params": {"temperature": 1}}
    agent: The parent agent (automatically passed by Strands framework).

Returns:
    Dict containing status and response content in the format:
    {
        "status": "success|error",
        "content": [
            {"text": "Response: The response text from the agent"},
            {"text": "Model: Information about the model used"},
            {"text": "Metrics: Performance metrics information"}
        ]
    }

    Success case: Returns the agent response with model info and performance metrics
    Error case: Returns information about what went wrong during processing

Environment Variables for Model Switching:
----------------------------------------
When model_provider="env", these variables are used:
- STRANDS_PROVIDER: Model provider name
- STRANDS_MODEL_ID: Specific model identifier, example;
    "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0" for bedrock provider
- STRANDS_MAX_TOKENS: Maximum tokens to generate
- STRANDS_TEMPERATURE: Sampling temperature
- Provider-specific keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.)

Examples:
--------
# Use Bedrock for creative tasks
result = agent.tool.use_agent(
    prompt="Write a poem about AI",
    system_prompt="You are a creative poet.",
    model_provider="bedrock"
)

# Use Ollama for local processing
result = agent.tool.use_agent(
    prompt="Summarize this text",
    system_prompt="You are a summarization assistant.",
    model_provider="ollama",
    model_settings={"host": "http://localhost:11434", "model_id": "qwen3:4b"}
)

# Use environment configuration
os.environ["STRANDS_PROVIDER"] = "litellm"
os.environ["STRANDS_MODEL_ID"] = "openai/gpt-4o"
result = agent.tool.use_agent(
    prompt="Analyze this data",
    system_prompt="You are a data analyst.",
    model_provider="env"
)

Notes:
    - Model switching requires the appropriate dependencies (bedrock, anthropic, ollama, llamaapi, litellm, etc.)
    - When model_provider is None, behavior is identical to the original implementation
    - Custom model_settings overrides default environment-based configuration
    - Performance metrics include token usage for the specific model used
    - Model information is included in the response for transparency
```

Source: strands-agents/tools `src/strands_tools/use_agent.py:80-183` (docstring), commit `1dd0465` - source at commit, 2026-09-30, with the description rule in Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/tools/decorator.py:235-283`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (both fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The `@tool` decorator sends the docstring with lines dropped from `Args:` until the next line that starts with a section word such as `Examples:` or `Returns:`; here the indented line `Examples: ["calculator", "file_read", "retrieve"]` ends that skip, so the later `Args:` lines stay in the description shown.

Parameters (Python signature and docstring `Args:` section, verbatim; the decorator builds the JSON Schema from them and leaves out the framework-injected `agent` parameter):

```python
@tool
def use_agent(
    prompt: str,
    system_prompt: str,
    tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    model_provider: Optional[str] = None,
    model_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    agent: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
```

```python
    Args:
        prompt: The prompt to process with the new agent instance.
        system_prompt: Custom system prompt for the agent.
        tools: List of tool names to make available to the nested agent.
            Tool names must exist in the parent agent's tool registry.
            Examples: ["calculator", "file_read", "retrieve"]
            If not provided, inherits all tools from the parent agent.
        model_provider: Model provider to use for the nested agent.
            Options: "bedrock", "anthropic", "litellm", "llamaapi", "ollama", "openai", "github"
            Special values:
            - None: Use parent agent's model (default, preserves original behavior)
            - "env": Use environment variables to determine provider
            Examples: "bedrock", anthropic", "litellm", "env"
        model_settings: Optional custom configuration for the model.
            If not provided, uses default configuration for the provider.
            Example: {"model_id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "params": {"temperature": 1}}
        agent: The parent agent (automatically passed by Strands framework).
```

Source: strands-agents/tools `src/strands_tools/use_agent.py:71-79` and `:109-125`, commit `1dd0465` - source at commit, 2026-09-30, with the injected-parameter rule (`special_params = {"self", "cls", "agent"}`) in Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/tools/decorator.py:448`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The call blocks: it creates a new `Agent` with the given system prompt, empty messages, the parent's tools (or the named subset), and the parent's model unless `model_provider` selects another, runs it on `prompt`, and returns content items `f"Response: {assistant_response}"`, `f"Model: {model_info}"`, and `f"Metrics: {metrics_text}"` (`use_agent.py:184-281`). The nested agent exists only for the call, so there is no ID and no companion tool. Errors return `f"Error in use_agent tool: {str(e)}"` (`:283-288`).

#### `swarm` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

````text
Create and coordinate a custom team of AI agents for collaborative task solving.

This function leverages the Strands SDK's Swarm multi-agent pattern to create custom teams
of specialized AI agents with individual configurations. Each agent can have its own system
prompt, tools, model provider, and settings, enabling precise control over team composition.

How It Works:
------------
1. Custom Agent Creation:
   • Each agent is created with individual specifications
   • Unique system prompts define each agent's role and expertise
   • Per-agent tool access controls what each agent can do
   • Individual model providers and settings for optimization

2. Autonomous Coordination:
   • Agents automatically receive coordination tools (handoff_to_agent, complete_swarm_task)
   • Shared working memory maintains context across all handoffs
   • Agents decide when to collaborate based on task requirements
   • Self-organizing collaboration without central control

3. Flexible Team Composition:
   • Mix different model providers for diverse capabilities
   • Assign specialized tools to relevant agents only
   • Custom temperature and model settings per agent
   • Support for any number of agents with unique roles

4. Safety and Control:
   • Comprehensive timeout mechanisms prevent infinite loops
   • Handoff limits ensure efficient resource usage
   • Repetitive behavior detection prevents endless agent exchanges
   • Rich execution metrics for performance insights

Returns:
    Dict containing status and response content in the format:
    {
        "status": "success|error",
        "content": [{"text": "Comprehensive results from agent team collaboration"}]
    }

    Success case: Returns detailed results from swarm execution with agent contributions
    Error case: Returns information about what went wrong during processing

Example Usage:
-------------
```python
# Research and development team
result = agent.tool.swarm(
    task="Research and design a sustainable energy solution for rural communities",
    agents=[
        {
            "name": "researcher",
            "system_prompt": "You are a renewable energy specialist. Focus on feasibility and impact.",
            "tools": ["retrieve", "calculator"],
            "model_provider": "bedrock",
            "model_settings": {"model_id": "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0"}
        },
        {
            "name": "engineer",
            "system_prompt": "You are an engineering specialist. Focus on implementation and costs.",
            "tools": ["calculator", "file_write"],
            "model_provider": "anthropic",
            "model_settings": {"model_id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"}
        },
        {
            "name": "community_expert",
            "system_prompt": "You are a community specialist. Focus on social impact and adoption.",
            "tools": ["retrieve", "file_write"],
            "model_provider": "openai",
            "model_settings": {"model_id": "o4-mini"}
        }
    ]
)

# Creative content team
result = agent.tool.swarm(
    task="Create a comprehensive brand identity and marketing campaign",
    agents=[
        {
            "name": "brand_strategist",
            "system_prompt": "You are a brand strategist. Focus on positioning and messaging.",
            "tools": ["retrieve", "file_write"]
        },
        {
            "name": "creative_director",
            "system_prompt": "You are a creative director. Focus on visual concepts and campaigns.",
            "tools": ["generate_image", "file_write"],
            "model_settings": {"params": {"temperature": 0.8}}
        },
        {
            "name": "copywriter",
            "system_prompt": "You are a copywriter. Focus on messaging and marketing copy.",
            "tools": ["file_write"],
            "model_settings": {"params": {"temperature": 0.7}}
        }
    ],
    execution_timeout=1200  # Extended timeout for creative work
)

# Minimal team with inheritance
result = agent.tool.swarm(
    task="Analyze quarterly financial performance",
    agents=[
        {
            "system_prompt": "You are a financial analyst specializing in performance metrics and trend analysis.",
            "tools": ["calculator", "file_write"],
            "inherit_parent_prompt": True
        },
        {
            "system_prompt": "You are a business strategist focusing on insights and recommendations.",
            "tools": ["file_write"],
            "inherit_parent_prompt": True
        }
    ]
)

# Custom repetitive handoff detection
result = agent.tool.swarm(
    task="Complex multi-step analysis requiring tight collaboration",
    agents=[...],
    repetitive_handoff_detection_window=12,  # Look at more recent handoffs
    repetitive_handoff_min_unique_agents=4,  # Require more variety in agent participation
)
```

Notes:
    - Built on Strands SDK's native Swarm multi-agent pattern
    - Each agent can use different models and tools for optimal performance
    - Agents coordinate autonomously through injected coordination tools
    - Shared context enables true collective intelligence
    - Safety mechanisms prevent infinite loops and resource exhaustion
    - Rich execution metrics provide insights into team collaboration
    - Supports complex multi-modal tasks and diverse expertise areas
    - Tool filtering ensures agents only get tools that exist in parent registry
````

Source: strands-agents/tools `src/strands_tools/swarm.py:244-395` (docstring), commit `1dd0465` - source at commit, 2026-09-30, with the description rule in Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/tools/decorator.py:235-283`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (both fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The text shown is the docstring without its `Args:` section, which is what the `@tool` decorator sends.

Parameters (Python signature and docstring `Args:` section, verbatim; the decorator builds the JSON Schema from them and leaves out the framework-injected `agent` parameter):

```python
@tool
def swarm(
    task: str,
    agents: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    max_handoffs: int = 20,
    max_iterations: int = 20,
    execution_timeout: float = 900.0,
    node_timeout: float = 300.0,
    repetitive_handoff_detection_window: int = 8,
    repetitive_handoff_min_unique_agents: int = 3,
    agent: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
```

```python
    Args:
        task: The main task to be processed by the agent team.
        agents: List of agent specification dictionaries. Each dictionary can contain:
            - name (str): Agent name/identifier (optional, auto-generated if not provided)
            - system_prompt (str): Agent's system prompt defining its role and expertise
            - tools (List[str]): List of tool names available to this agent (optional)
            - model_provider (str): Model provider for this agent (optional, inherits from parent)
            - model_settings (Dict): Model configuration for this agent (optional)
            - inherit_parent_prompt (bool): Whether to append parent agent's system prompt (optional)
        max_handoffs: Maximum number of handoffs between agents (default: 20).
        max_iterations: Maximum total iterations across all agents (default: 20).
        execution_timeout: Maximum total execution time in seconds (default: 900).
        node_timeout: Maximum time per agent in seconds (default: 300).
        repetitive_handoff_detection_window: Number of recent handoffs to analyze for repetitive behavior (default: 8).
        repetitive_handoff_min_unique_agents: Minimum number of unique agents required in the
            detection window (default: 3).
        agent: The parent agent (automatically passed by Strands framework).
```

Source: strands-agents/tools `src/strands_tools/swarm.py:232-243` and `:276-292`, commit `1dd0465` - source at commit, 2026-09-30 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The call blocks: it builds one agent per entry in `agents`, runs them as an SDK `Swarm` with the given limits (`execution_timeout` and `node_timeout` in seconds), and returns the swarm's results; it requires at least one agent spec and logs a warning above 10 agents (`swarm.py:400-423`). The agents inside the swarm receive the SDK's `handoff_to_agent` tool. The docstring also names `complete_swarm_task`, but the SDK's `swarm.py` at commit `38afb96` injects only `handoff_to_agent` (`multiagent/swarm.py:578-600`); when `complete_swarm_task` was removed is not in the sources.

#### `handoff_to_agent` (handoff)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Transfer control to another agent in the swarm for specialized help.

Returns:
    Confirmation of handoff initiation
```

Parameters (Python function signature and docstring, verbatim; the `@tool` decorator builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
        @tool
        def handoff_to_agent(agent_name: str, message: str, context: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
            """Transfer control to another agent in the swarm for specialized help.

            Args:
                agent_name: Name of the agent to hand off to
                message: Message explaining what needs to be done and why you're handing off
                context: Additional context to share with the next agent

            Returns:
                Confirmation of handoff initiation
            """
```

Source (description and parameters): Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/multiagent/swarm.py:612-623`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is the docstring without its `Args:` section, which is what the `@tool` decorator sends (`tools/decorator.py:235-283`).

Semantics. `Swarm` injects this one tool into every swarm agent and raises an error if an agent already has a tool with that name (`swarm.py:578-600`). A call records the target and message, adds `context` to the swarm's shared context, and returns the tool result "Handing off to {agent_name}: {message}" to the caller, or "Error: Agent '{agent_name}' not found in swarm" (`:624-637`, `:641-659`). Control then moves to the target: when the calling agent's turn ends, the swarm loop makes the target the current node and gives it an input built from the handoff message, the user request, the previous agents, and the shared context, so the target's work does not come back to the caller as a tool result (`:679-751`, `:890-911`). Each node's input ends "You have access to swarm coordination tools if you need help from other agents. If you don't hand off to another agent, the swarm will consider the task complete." (`:746-749`), and `max_handoffs` defaults to 20 (`:274`).

#### `strands_manage_background_task` (output, status, list, cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
List, get, or cancel background tasks. Results are delivered automatically as synthetic 'get' calls. Do not poll for results.
```

Parameters (Python method signature and docstring, verbatim; the `@tool` decorator builds the JSON Schema from them):

```python
    async def _manage_background_task(
        self, mode: Literal["list", "get", "cancel"], task_id: str | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Manage tracked background tasks.

        Args:
            mode: Whether to list, inspect, or cancel background tasks.
            task_id: The background task ID returned when the task was dispatched. Required for get and cancel.
        """
```

Source (description and parameters): Strands SDK `strands-py/src/strands/background_tasks/_background_tasks.py:124-139`, commit `38afb96` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The tool is declared with `@tool(name=_MANAGE_TOOL_NAME, description=(...))`, so the explicit description replaces the docstring.

Semantics. Background Tasks were added on 2026-09-08 ("feat(python): add backgroundTasks to Agent", PR #4226, forum or issue); when they are configured, eligible tools get a boolean `_background_execution` property described "Run this tool in the background and continue without waiting for its result.", and the default policy offers it on every eligible tool (`agentic` for `"*"`) unless a wildcard is set under `always` or `never` (`_background_tasks.py:464-511`). A background call returns "Background task dispatched.\n\nTask ID: {task['task_id']}\nTool: {task['tool_name']}\nStatus: {task['status']}\n\nThe task is running in the background. Continue without waiting or polling.\nThe final result will be delivered automatically when the task completes." (`:210-222`). When a task is terminal, the SDK appends a synthetic assistant `toolUse` of `strands_manage_background_task` with `{"mode": "get", "task_id": ...}` and the matching `toolResult` (task metadata as JSON plus the result content), and by default (`wait_for_completion`) the agent waits for pending tasks at the end of an invocation and continues with their results (`:328-415`, `:518-520`). Mode `list` returns each task's `task_id`, `tool_name`, and `status`; mode `cancel` returns the task's `task_id` and `status`; `get` and `cancel` without `task_id` raise "Task ID is required for mode '{mode}'" (`:140-158`).

#### `agent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a new agent that has access to the following tools: glob, grep, ls, view. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match on the first try, use the agent tool to perform the search for you.
```

Source: Crush source, `internal/agent/templates/agent_tool.md` (embedded as `agentToolDescription`), commit `df5b024a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (Go struct with JSON and description tags from source at commit df5b024a, verbatim):

```go
type AgentParams struct {
	Prompt string `json:"prompt" description:"The task for the agent to perform"`
}
```

Source: Crush source, `internal/agent/agent_tool.go`, commit `df5b024a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The JSON Schema that the `fantasy` library renders from these struct tags is not in the sources.

Semantics. `agent` is synchronous: the call returns when the subagent finishes, and several `agent` calls in one turn run concurrently because the tool is built with `fantasy.NewParallelAgentTool`. The subagent is Crush's configured task agent, run in a new child session titled "New Agent Session"; its final text comes back as a plain-text tool result with no envelope, and failures return "Failed to generate response: %s" or "Sub-agent completed but produced no text output." (Crush `internal/agent/coordinator.go`, source at commit). There is no tool to stop, message, or wait on a subagent; background mode exists only for `bash`, whose companions `job_output {shell_id, wait}` and `job_kill {shell_id}` (added 2025-11-07) manage background shells only (Crush `bash.go`, `job_output.go`, `job_kill.go`, and commit `4401d5b37f03`, source at commit). The name `agent` is unchanged since the opencode-ai Go ancestor, whose description named the tools GlobTool, GrepTool, LS, and View and said "Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report." (opencode-ai `agent-tool.go`, source at commit). Crush sent the full markdown description until 2026-04-11, sent only its first line from that date, and cut the `.md` file itself to one line on 2026-05-12 (Crush commits `f78baed0f06e` and `efb3b03390d4`, source at commit).

#### `agentic_fetch` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Fetch a URL or search the web using an AI sub-agent that can extract, summarize, and answer questions. Slower and costlier than fetch; use fetch for raw content or API responses.
```

Source: Crush source, `internal/agent/templates/agentic_fetch.md` (embedded as `agenticFetchToolDescription`), commit `df5b024a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (Go struct with JSON and description tags from source at commit df5b024a, verbatim):

```go
type AgenticFetchParams struct {
	URL    string `json:"url,omitempty" description:"The URL to fetch content from (optional - if not provided, the agent will search the web)"`
	Prompt string `json:"prompt" description:"The prompt describing what information to find or extract"`
}
```

Source: Crush source, `internal/agent/tools/fetch_types.go`, commit `df5b024a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The JSON Schema that the `fantasy` library renders from these struct tags is not in the sources.

Semantics. `agentic_fetch` is synchronous and parallel like `agent` (`fantasy.NewParallelAgentTool`); it first asks the user for permission with action "fetch", then runs a subagent on the small model with the tools `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `glob`, `grep`, `sourcegraph`, and `view` in a temporary directory, in a child session titled "Fetch Analysis" whose own tool calls are auto-approved (Crush `internal/agent/agentic_fetch_tool.go`, source at commit). With `url`, Crush fetches the page first and either inlines it in `<webpage_content>` tags or, when it is longer than `LargeContentThreshold` (50000, commented "50KB"), saves it to a file and tells the subagent "Use the view and grep tools to analyze this file and extract the requested information."; without `url`, the subagent is told "Use the web_search tool to find relevant information." The result is the subagent's final text as a plain-text tool result, with the same error strings as `agent` (Crush `internal/agent/coordinator.go`, source at commit). The tool was added on 2025-11-05 in #1315 (Crush commit `51a2144e7724`, source at commit).

Since v4.1.0 (2026-07-31) one VSIX loads either the legacy bundle (`use_subagents`, `use_subagent_<name>`, `new_task`) or the SDK bundle (`spawn_agent`, `subagent_<name>`, and 18 `team_*` tools); the 4.1.0 changelog says most users still get the legacy bundle and "a small percentage (starting at 1%)" get the SDK bundle. In the SDK bundle the VS Code host disables both `spawn_agent` and the team tools, while the CLI enables both unless it runs in yolo mode, and the docs say "Subagents are available in the Cline CLI and Cline Desktop. The VS Code and JetBrains extensions don't use them."

#### `spawn_agent` (spawn; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn a sub-agent with custom instructions for a specialized task. Waits for the sub-agent to finish and returns its result before your next step.
```

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
export const SpawnAgentInputSchema = z.object({
	systemPrompt: z
		.string()
		.describe("System prompt defining the sub-agent's behavior"),
	task: z.string().describe("Task for the sub-agent to complete"),
});
```

Source (description and parameters): Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/spawn-agent-tool.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. `spawn_agent` blocks until the subagent finishes, with `timeoutMs: 300000` (milliseconds) and `retryable: false`; it has `executionMode: "parallel"`, so several calls in one turn run concurrently, which started with PR #14197 on 2026-09-17 (Cline commit `721d18548554`, source at commit). The tool returns `{text, iterations, finishReason, usage: {inputTokens, outputTokens}}`, which the message codec serializes to JSON text (Cline SDK `persisted-tool-result-content.ts`, source at commit). The docs say the subagent has Cline's built-in tools for the current mode but no MCP tools, that "A subagent can start subagents of its own.", and that "Approving the `spawn_agent` call approves everything the subagent then does: its own tool calls don't ask for approval." (Cline docs page `docs/features/subagents.mdx`, source at commit). Users turn subagents off by disabling the `spawn_agent` tool in the CLI or Desktop tool settings (same docs page).

#### `subagent_<name>` (spawn; SDK)

Description (verbatim template, filled for each configured agent):

```text
Use the "${config.name}" subagent: ${config.description}
```

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
const ConfiguredAgentInputSchema = z.object({
	prompt: z.string().trim().min(1).describe("Task for the subagent to perform"),
});
```

Source (description and parameters): Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/configured-agent-tool.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. Cline makes one tool per configured agent, named `subagent_` plus the agent name lowercased, with every run of characters outside `a-z` and `0-9` (underscores included) turned into one underscore and leading or trailing underscores dropped, or `agent` if nothing is left. Names are capped at 64 characters: a longer name keeps a truncated body plus `_` and the first six characters of a base-36 hash of the original name, and collisions get `_2`, `_3`, and so on; the schema shown is what the code generates for every configured agent. Each call blocks, runs in parallel with other calls in the same turn, has `timeoutMs: 300000` (milliseconds), and returns the same `{text, iterations, finishReason, usage}` object as `spawn_agent`, while the subagent runs with the agent's `systemPrompt` and its own `providerId`, `modelId`, and `maxIterations` when set. A code comment says "The parent approves delegation; child tools run autonomously". Configured agents became `subagent_<name>` tools on 2026-06-10 (Cline pull request #11368, forum or issue).

#### `team_spawn_teammate` (spawn; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn a teammate with a required agentId and rolePrompt.
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
export const TeamSpawnTeammateInputSchema = z
	.object({
		agentId: z.string().min(1).describe("Teammate identifier"),
		rolePrompt: z
			.string()
			.min(1)
			.describe("System prompt describing teammate role"),
	})
	.strict();
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. Only the lead can call it (otherwise "Only the lead agent can manage teammates."); it creates a teammate agent whose prompt is `rolePrompt`, gives it the base tools plus the team tools without `team_spawn_teammate`, and returns `{agentId, status: "spawned"}` without running any task. Work reaches a teammate through `team_run_task`, and the CLI runtime builder bootstraps the team with `includeLeadSpawnTool: true` and `includeLeadManagementTools: true` (Cline SDK `runtime-builder.ts`, source at commit). The other eight of the 18 team tools manage shared team records rather than subagent runs: `team_task` (shared task list), `team_mission_log`, `team_cleanup` ("Clean up the team runtime. Fails if teammates are still running."), `team_create_outcome`, `team_attach_outcome_fragment`, `team_review_outcome_fragment`, `team_finalize_outcome`, and `team_list_outcomes`.

#### `team_run_task` (spawn; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Route a delegated task to a teammate. Choose sync (wait) or async (run in background).
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
function nullableOptional<T extends z.ZodTypeAny>(schema: T) {
	return z.preprocess(
		(value) => (value === null ? undefined : value),
		schema.optional(),
	);
}

export const TeamRunTaskInputSchema = z.object({
	agentId: z.string().describe("Teammate agent ID"),
	task: z.string().min(1).describe("Task instructions for the teammate"),
	taskId: nullableOptional(z.string()).describe("Optional shared task list ID"),
	runMode: nullableOptional(z.enum(["sync", "async"])).describe(
		"Execution mode: 'sync' blocks until the teammate finishes and returns the result (default if omitted); 'async' queues the run and returns a runId immediately - use team_await_runs to collect results later.",
	),
	continueConversation: nullableOptional(z.boolean()).describe(
		"If true, continue the teammate conversation; otherwise start fresh",
	),
});
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The `nullableOptional` helper and the schema are two separate excerpts from the same file.

Semantics. `runMode` defaults to sync: the call blocks until the teammate finishes and returns `{agentId, mode: "sync", status: "running", dispatched: true, message, text, iterations}` with the message "Task dispatched to ${validatedInput.agentId} and completed in sync mode." In async mode it returns at once with `status: "queued"`, a `runId`, and the message "Task dispatched to ${validatedInput.agentId} and queued as ${run.id}.", and the lead collects the result with `team_await_runs` or `team_list_runs`. A duplicate sync call for the same teammate in one tool batch joins the first run and reports "Task for ${validatedInput.agentId} was already dispatched in this tool batch; joined the existing in-flight run." When the lead tries to stop while tasks are unfinished or runs are active, the completion guard returns "[SYSTEM] You still have team obligations. ${parts.join(". ")}. Use team_run_task to delegate work, or team_task with action=complete to mark tasks done, or team_await_runs to wait for active runs. Do NOT stop until all tasks are completed." (Cline SDK `runtime-builder.ts`, source at commit).

#### `team_await_runs` (output, wait; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Wait for async teammate runs. Provide runId to wait for one run, or omit it to wait for all active async runs. Uses a long timeout for legitimate teammate work.
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
export const TeamAwaitRunsInputSchema = z
	.object({
		runId: nullableOptional(z.string().min(1)).describe(
			"Optional async run ID to await. Omit to wait for all active async runs.",
		),
	})
	.strict();
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). `nullableOptional` is a helper in the same file that maps `null` to `undefined` and makes the field optional.

Semantics. The tool timeout is `TEAM_AWAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000` (milliseconds), and the runtime polls run status every 250 ms (Cline SDK `multi-agent.ts`, source at commit). With `runId` it returns one run summary; without it, it waits until no run is queued or running and returns summaries of all runs. Each summary has the run `id`, `agentId`, `status`, timing and progress fields, and a `resultSummary` whose `textPreview` is the teammate's result text with whitespace collapsed and cut to `TEAM_RUN_TEXT_PREVIEW_LIMIT = 400` characters. A failed, cancelled, or interrupted run makes the call throw, for example `` Run "${run.id}" failed${run.error ? `: ${run.error}` : ""} `` or "One or more runs did not complete successfully: ${details}". The earlier tools `team_await_run` and `team_await_all_runs` were merged into this tool between 2026-04-15 and 2026-04-17 (Cline team tools commit history, source at commit).

#### `team_status` (status; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Return a snapshot of team members, task counts, mailbox, and mission log stats.
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The tool returns `{teamId, teamName, members, taskCounts, unreadMessages, missionLogEntries, activeRuns, queuedRuns, outcomeCounts}`, where each member is `{agentId, role: "lead" | "teammate", description?, status: "idle" | "running" | "stopped"}`. It does not block. Teammates receive this tool and the other team management tools too; only `team_spawn_teammate` is withheld from them.

#### `team_send_message` (message; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Send a mailbox message to a specific teammate.
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
export const TeamSendMessageInputSchema = z.object({
	toAgentId: z.string().min(1).describe("Recipient agent ID"),
	subject: z.string().min(1).describe("Message subject"),
	body: z.string().min(1).describe("Message body"),
	taskId: nullableOptional(z.string().min(1)).describe(
		"Optional task ID context",
	),
});
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). `nullableOptional` is a helper in the same file that maps `null` to `undefined` and makes the field optional.

Semantics. The call stores the message in the team mailbox and returns `{id, toAgentId}`, with ids of the form `msg_${String(++this.messageCounter).padStart(5, "0")}`. When the recipient is a teammate with a run in progress, the runtime sets a pending steer message on it: `[MAILBOX] You got a message from ${fromAgentId}. Subject: "${subject}". Use the team_read_mailbox tool to read it at your convenience.` (Cline SDK `multi-agent.ts`, source at commit). The recipient reads the body with `team_read_mailbox`; any team member, lead or teammate, can send, and the lead can be the recipient.

Description (verbatim):

```text
Broadcast a message to all teammates.
```

Semantics. The runtime sends one mailbox message to every member except the sender and the lead, through the same path as `team_send_message`, so running teammates get the same "[MAILBOX] ..." steer message (Cline SDK `multi-agent.ts`, source at commit). The tool returns `{delivered: <count>}`.

Read the current agent mailbox.

The call does not block and returns an array of run summaries in the same shape `team_await_runs` returns, including `status`, a `messagePreview` cut to `TEAM_RUN_MESSAGE_PREVIEW_LIMIT = 240` characters, `lastProgressMessage`, `currentActivity`, `error`, and `resultSummary.textPreview` cut to 400 characters. #### `team_cancel_run` (cancel; SDK)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Cancel one async teammate run.
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit c3a40572, converted with `zodToJsonSchema`, verbatim):

```js
export const TeamCancelRunInputSchema = z.object({
	runId: z.string().min(1).describe("Run ID"),
	reason: nullableOptional(z.string().min(1)).describe(
		"Optional cancellation reason",
	),
});
```

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). `nullableOptional` is a helper in the same file that maps `null` to `undefined` and makes the field optional.

Semantics. The runtime's `cancelRun` marks the run record `cancelled`, stores the reason as its error, removes it from the run queue, and returns `{runId, status}`; a run that already finished is returned unchanged. `cancelRun` does not call `abort()` on the teammate agent, so it updates the record without stopping a teammate that is already working (Cline SDK `multi-agent.ts`, source at commit). Stopping the teammate itself is done with `team_shutdown_teammate`.

Source: Cline SDK source, `sdk/packages/shared/src/team/schema.ts`, commit `c3a40572` - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). `nullableOptional` is a helper in the same file that maps `null` to `undefined` and makes the field optional.

Semantics. Only the lead can call it (otherwise "Only the lead agent can manage teammates."). The runtime calls `abort()` on the teammate agent, sets the member status to `stopped`, emits a teammate-shutdown event with the reason, and the tool returns `{agentId, status: "stopped"}` (Cline SDK `multi-agent.ts`, source at commit).

#### `use_subagents` (spawn; legacy extension)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Run up to five focused in-process subagents in parallel. Each subagent gets its own prompt and returns a comprehensive research result with tool and token stats. Use this for broad exploration when reading many files would consume the main agent's context window. You do not need to launch multiple subagents every time; using one subagent is valid when it avoids unnecessary context usage for light discovery work.
```

Parameters (`ClineToolSpec` parameter list in TypeScript from source at commit 77613702, verbatim):

```ts
	parameters: [
		{
			name: "prompt_1",
			required: true,
			instruction: "First subagent prompt.",
		},
		{
			name: "prompt_2",
			required: false,
			instruction: "Optional second subagent prompt.",
		},
		{
			name: "prompt_3",
			required: false,
			instruction: "Optional third subagent prompt.",
		},
		{
			name: "prompt_4",
			required: false,
			instruction: "Optional fourth subagent prompt.",
		},
		{
			name: "prompt_5",
			required: false,
			instruction: "Optional fifth subagent prompt.",
		},
	],
```

Source (description and parameters): Cline legacy extension source, `apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/tools/subagent.ts`, `legacy-extension` commit `77613702` - source at commit, 2026-08-18 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The call blocks while every non-empty prompt among `prompt_1` through `prompt_5` runs as a separate in-process subagent in parallel, and it returns once all of them settle (Cline legacy `SubagentToolHandler.ts`, source at commit). The result is one text block that starts "Subagent results:" with lines for total, succeeded, failed, tool calls, and peak context usage, then a header `[${entry.index}] ${entry.status.toUpperCase()} - ${entry.prompt}` for each subagent followed by its result or error cut to 1200 characters. Each subagent runs with a research-mode system suffix and, by default, the tools `FILE_READ`, `LIST_FILES`, `SEARCH`, `LIST_CODE_DEF`, `BASH`, `USE_SKILL`, and `ATTEMPT`, and it returns through `attempt_completion`: "The attempt_completion result field is sent directly to the main agent, so put your full final findings there." (Cline legacy `SubagentBuilder.ts`, source at commit); a subagent that never calls it fails with "Subagent did not call attempt_completion." (Cline legacy `SubagentRunner.ts`, source at commit). The tool is offered only when the `subagentsEnabled` setting is on and the current run is not itself a subagent, is listed in all 12 legacy prompt variants, and is removed from the tool list whenever a `use_subagent_<name>` tool exists (Cline legacy `ClineToolSet.ts` and prompt variant configs, source at commit). It was added on 2026-02-11 in PR #9208 and v3.58.0, and before that, from v3.33.0 (2025-10-16), the system prompt told the model to run `cline "prompt"` through `execute_command` with no subagent tool (Cline pull request #9208, forum or issue; Cline `CHANGELOG.md`, official changelog).

#### `use_subagent_<name>` (spawn; legacy extension)

Description (verbatim template, filled for each configured agent):

```text
Use the "${config.name}" subagent: ${config.description}
```

Parameters (`ClineToolSpec` parameter list in TypeScript from source at commit 77613702, verbatim):

```ts
			parameters: [
				{
					name: "prompt",
					required: true,
					instruction: "Helpful instruction for the task that the subagent will perform.",
				},
			],
```

Source (description and parameters): Cline legacy extension source, `apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/registry/ClineToolSet.ts` (`getDynamicSubagentToolSpecs`), `legacy-extension` commit `77613702` - source at commit, 2026-08-18 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. Cline makes one tool per agent config file, named `use_subagent_` plus the agent name trimmed and lowercased, with every run of characters outside `a-z`, `0-9`, and `_` replaced by one underscore, repeated underscores collapsed, and leading or trailing underscores removed, or `agent` if nothing is left (Cline legacy `SubagentToolName.ts`, source at commit). Names over 64 characters keep a truncated body plus `_` and the first six characters of a base-36 hash of the original name, and collisions get `_2`, `_3`, and so on; the schema shown is what the code generates for every configured agent (Cline legacy `AgentConfigLoader.ts`, source at commit). Each agent comes from a file whose YAML frontmatter gives `name` and `description` and whose body is the subagent's system prompt, and when at least one such tool exists the generic `use_subagents` tool is removed from the list. The call goes through the same handler as `use_subagents`: one blocking subagent run, the same "Subagent results:" text with one entry, and the same `attempt_completion` return path (Cline legacy `SubagentToolHandler.ts`, source at commit). File-based agents became these tools on 2026-02-23 (Cline pull request #9245, forum or issue).

#### `new_task` (handoff; legacy extension)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Request to create a new task with preloaded context covering the conversation with the user up to this point and key information for continuing with the new task. With this tool, you will create a detailed summary of the conversation so far, paying close attention to the user's explicit requests and your previous actions, with a focus on the most relevant information required for the new task.
Among other important areas of focus, this summary should be thorough in capturing technical details, code patterns, and architectural decisions that would be essential for continuing with the new task. The user will be presented with a preview of your generated context and can choose to create a new task or keep chatting in the current conversation. The user may choose to start a new task at any point.
```

Parameters (`ClineToolSpec` parameter list in TypeScript from source at commit 77613702, verbatim):

```ts
	parameters: [
		{
			name: "context",
			required: true,
			instruction: `The context to preload the new task with. If applicable based on the current task, this should include:
  1. Current Work: Describe in detail what was being worked on prior to this request to create a new task. Pay special attention to the more recent messages / conversation.
  2. Key Technical Concepts: List all important technical concepts, technologies, coding conventions, and frameworks discussed, which might be relevant for the new task.
  3. Relevant Files and Code: If applicable, enumerate specific files and code sections examined, modified, or created for the task continuation. Pay special attention to the most recent messages and changes.
  4. Problem Solving: Document problems solved thus far and any ongoing troubleshooting efforts.
  5. Pending Tasks and Next Steps: Outline all pending tasks that you have explicitly been asked to work on, as well as list the next steps you will take for all outstanding work, if applicable. Include code snippets where they add clarity. For any next steps, include direct quotes from the most recent conversation showing exactly what task you were working on and where you left off. This should be verbatim to ensure there's no information loss in context between tasks. It's important to be detailed here.`,
			usage: "context to preload new task with",
		},
	],
```

Source (description and parameters): Cline legacy extension source, `apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/tools/new_task.ts`, `legacy-extension` commit `77613702` - source at commit, 2026-08-18 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The handler shows the user the generated context and waits; the "Start New Task with Context" button sends that context to `newTask`, whose `initTask` calls `clearTask()` before it starts a new task with the context as its first message, so control moves to the new task and does not come back to the calling task as a tool result (Cline legacy `NewTaskHandler.ts`, `useMessageHandlers.ts`, `buttonConfig.ts`, `controller/task/newTask.ts`, and `controller/index.ts`, source at commit). If the user types a reply instead, the tool result is "The user provided feedback instead of creating a new task:\n<feedback>\n${text}\n</feedback>"; the handler also has a branch, for a user response with no text, that returns "The user has created a new task with the provided context." The tool is offered only outside yolo mode (`!context.yoloModeToggled`) and only in the gemini-3, hermes, and native-gpt-5-1 prompt variants (Cline legacy prompt variant configs, source at commit). It was added on 2025-04-09 in v3.10.1 and dropped from most prompt variants on 2025-11-18 in v3.38.0 (Cline `CHANGELOG.md`, official changelog).

#### `spawn_agents` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Use this tool to spawn agents to help you complete the user request. Each agent has specific requirements for prompt and params based on their tools schema.

The prompt field is a simple string, while params is a JSON object that gets validated against the agent's schema.

Each agent available is already defined as another tool, or, dynamically defined later in the conversation.

**IMPORTANT**: `agent_type` must be an actual agent name (e.g., `basher`, `code-searcher`, `opus-agent`), NOT a tool name like `read_files`, `str_replace`, `code_search`, etc. If you need to call a tool, use it directly as a tool call instead of wrapping it in spawn_agents.

You can call agents either as direct tool calls (using the listed tool name, e.g. `example_agent`) or use `spawn_agents` with the canonical agent name in `agent_type` (e.g. `example-agent`). Both formats work, but **prefer using spawn_agents** because it allows you to spawn multiple agents in parallel for better performance. Both use the same schema with nested `prompt` and `params` fields.

**IMPORTANT**: Many agents have REQUIRED fields in their params schema. Check the agent's schema before spawning - if params has required fields, you MUST include them in the params object. For example, code-searcher requires `searchQueries`, basher requires `command`.

Example:
<spawn_agents_params_example>
{
  "agents": [
    {
      "agent_type": "basher",
      "prompt": "Check if tests pass",
      "params": {
        "command": "npm test"
      }
    },
    {
      "agent_type": "code-searcher",
      "params": {
        "searchQueries": [
          {
            "pattern": "authenticate",
            "flags": "-g *.ts"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
</spawn_agents_params_example>
```

Source: Codebuff `spawn_agents` tool definition, `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts` lines 122-158, commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The example block is the output of the `$getNativeToolCallExampleString` helper (`common/src/tools/params/utils.ts` lines 109-121), which wraps `JSON.stringify(input, null, 2)` in `<spawn_agents_params_example>` tags; it is rendered here from that helper and the example input in source, not from a live capture.

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit d418a51, verbatim):

```js
export const MAX_SPAWN_AGENTS_PER_CALL = 6

const toolName = 'spawn_agents'
const endsAgentStep = true
const inputSchema = z
  .object({
    agents: z.preprocess(
      coerceToArray,
      z
        .object({
          agent_type: z.string().describe('Agent to spawn'),
          prompt: z.string().optional().describe('Prompt to send to the agent'),
          params: z
            .preprocess(
              coerceToObject,
              z
                .object({
                  // Common agent fields (all optional hints - each agent validates its own required fields)
                  command: z
                    .string()
                    .optional()
                    .describe('Terminal command to run (basher, tmux-cli)'),
                  what_to_summarize: z
                    .string()
                    .optional()
                    .describe(
                      'What information from the command output is desired (basher)',
                    ),
                  timeout_seconds: z
                    .number()
                    .optional()
                    .describe(
                      'Timeout for command. Set to -1 for no timeout. Default 30 (basher)',
                    ),
                  searchQueries: z
                    .array(
                      z.object({
                        pattern: z
                          .string()
                          .describe('The pattern to search for'),
                        flags: z
                          .string()
                          .optional()
                          .describe(
                            'Optional ripgrep flags (e.g., "-i", "-g *.ts")',
                          ),
                        cwd: z
                          .string()
                          .optional()
                          .describe(
                            'Optional working directory relative to project root',
                          ),
                        maxResults: z
                          .number()
                          .optional()
                          .describe('Max results per file. Default 15'),
                      }),
                    )
                    .optional()
                    .describe('Array of code search queries (code-searcher)'),
                  filePaths: z
                    .array(z.string())
                    .optional()
                    .describe(
                      'Relevant file paths to read (opus-agent, gpt-5-agent)',
                    ),
                  directories: z
                    .array(z.string())
                    .optional()
                    .describe('Directories to search within (file-picker)'),
                  url: z
                    .string()
                    .optional()
                    .describe('Starting URL to navigate to (browser-use)'),
                  prompts: z
                    .array(z.string())
                    .optional()
                    .describe(
                      'Array of strategy prompts (editor-multi-prompt, code-reviewer-multi-prompt)',
                    ),
                })
                .catchall(z.any()),
            )
            .optional()
            .describe('Parameters object for the agent'),
        })
        .array()
        // One swarm at a time, and never a big one: a free-mode root once
        // fanned out to 21 subagents in a single call (2026-10-10). The
        // runtime handler enforces the same ceiling, so a caller that
        // bypasses the schema still cannot.
        .max(
          MAX_SPAWN_AGENTS_PER_CALL,
          `Spawn at most ${MAX_SPAWN_AGENTS_PER_CALL} agents in one call. For more, spawn again after these return.`,
        ),
    ),
  })
  .describe(
    `Spawn multiple agents and send a prompt and/or parameters to each of them. These agents will run in parallel. Note that that means they will run independently. If you need to run agents sequentially, use spawn_agents with one agent at a time instead. At most 6 agents per call.`,
  )
```

Source: Codebuff `spawn_agents` tool definition, `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts` lines 22-121, commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The output schema is `jsonToolResultSchema(spawnAgentsOutputSchema)`, an array of objects with `agentType` plus any JSON fields (lines 13-18 and 165).

Semantics. The call ends the parent's step (`endsAgentStep = true`), runs the listed agents in parallel, and waits for all of them with `Promise.allSettled` before returning one JSON result, an array of `{agentName, agentType, value}`, where a failed spawn's `value` is ``{ errorMessage: `Error spawning agent: ${result.reason}` }`` (source at commit, `spawn_agents` handler). The cap of 6 agents per call arrived on 2026-10-10 (`18e14e87252c`), and the handler refuses a larger batch with ``Refusing to spawn ${agents.length} agents at once: at most ${MAX_SPAWN_AGENTS_PER_CALL} per spawn_agents call. Split the fan-out into smaller batches.`` (source at commit, `spawn_agents` handler). Before the call streams, the runtime drops entries without `agent_type` and entries that name a tool, answering the latter with ``"${agentTypeStr}" is a tool, not an agent. Call it directly as a tool instead of wrapping it in spawn_agents.`` (source at commit, `tool-executor.ts`). Spawned children report back through `set_output`. The asynchronous `spawn_agents_async`, which took the same entries, returned `[{agentType, success, agentId}]`, and queued "Agent ${agentType} completed with output:\n\n..." to the parent, was removed on 2025-10-06 (`7b7a1af5be96`, "Remove spawn_agents_async tool (we'll bring it back with a different impl later!)"), and `send_agent_message {target_agent_id, prompt, params?}`, where `"PARENT_ID"` addressed the parent, was removed on 2025-08-10 (`d774a1190033`) (source at commit, removal commits).

#### `spawn_agent_inline` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn a single agent that runs within the current message history. 
The spawned agent sees all previous messages and any messages it adds 
are preserved when control returns to you.

You should prefer to use the spawn_agents tool unless instructed otherwise. This tool is only for special cases.

This is useful for:
- Delegating specific tasks while maintaining context
- Having specialized agents process information inline
- Managing message history (e.g., summarization)
The agent will run until it calls end_turn, then control returns to you. There is no tool result for this tool.
Example:
<spawn_agent_inline_params_example>
{
  "agent_type": "file-picker",
  "prompt": "Find files related to authentication",
  "params": {
    "paths": [
      "src/auth.ts",
      "src/user.ts"
    ]
  }
}
</spawn_agent_inline_params_example>
```

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit d418a51, verbatim):

```js
const toolName = 'spawn_agent_inline'
const endsAgentStep = true
const inputSchema = z
  .object({
    agent_type: z.string().describe('Agent to spawn'),
    prompt: z.string().optional().describe('Prompt to send to the agent'),
    params: z
      .preprocess(coerceToObject, z.record(z.string(), z.any()))
      .optional()
      .describe('Parameters object for the agent (if any)'),
  })
  .describe(
    `Spawn a single agent that runs within the current message history.`,
  )
```

Source (description and parameters): Codebuff `spawn_agent_inline` tool definition, `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts` lines 11-48, commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The example block is rendered from the `$getNativeToolCallExampleString` helper and the example input in source, not from a live capture.

Semantics. The child runs inside the parent's own message history, sees all earlier messages, and its messages stay in that history when control returns. The call ends the parent's step, and per the description the child runs until it calls `end_turn` and there is no tool result; the declared output schema is `textToolResultSchema()`, a single `{type: 'json', value: {message}}` entry (source at commit, `utils.ts` lines 141-150).

#### `<agent_name>` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn the ${agentTemplate.displayName} agent
```

Source: Codebuff agent tool builder, `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/prompts.ts` lines 113-118 (`buildAgentToolSet`), commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. This is the fallback; when the agent template sets `spawnerPrompt`, that text is the description instead.

Parameters (zod schema built per agent, from source at commit d418a51, verbatim):

```js
function ensureJsonSchemaCompatible(schema: z.ZodType): z.ZodType {
  try {
    z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input' })
    return schema
  } catch {
    const fallback = z.object({}).passthrough()
    return schema.description ? fallback.describe(schema.description) : fallback
  }
}

/**
 * Gets the short agent name from a fully qualified agent ID.
 * E.g., 'codebuff/file-picker@1.0.0' -> 'file-picker'
 */
export function getAgentShortName(agentType: AgentTemplateType): string {
  const withoutVersion = agentType.split('@')[0]
  const parts = withoutVersion.split('/')
  return parts[parts.length - 1]
}

/**
 * Converts an agent ID into the provider-facing tool name used for direct
 * subagent calls. Agent IDs remain hyphenated; tool names use underscores.
 */
export function getAgentToolName(agentType: AgentTemplateType): string {
  return getAgentShortName(agentType).replace(/-/g, '_')
}

/**
 * Builds an input schema for an agent tool with prompt and params as top-level fields.
 * This matches the spawn_agents schema structure: { prompt?: string, params?: object }
 */
export function buildAgentToolInputSchema(
  agentTemplate: AgentTemplate,
): z.ZodType {
  const { inputSchema } = agentTemplate

  // Build schema with prompt and params as top-level fields (consistent with spawn_agents)
  // Preserve the original optionality from the inputSchema
  let schemaFields: Record<string, z.ZodType> = {}

  if (inputSchema?.prompt) {
    schemaFields.prompt = inputSchema.prompt
  }

  if (inputSchema?.params) {
    schemaFields.params = inputSchema.params
  }

  return z
    .object(schemaFields)
    .describe(
      agentTemplate.spawnerPrompt ||
        `Spawn the ${agentTemplate.displayName} agent`,
    )
}
```

Source: Codebuff agent tool builder, `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/prompts.ts` lines 13-68, commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

Semantics. Naming rule: the tool name is the agent's short name (the id with any `publisher/` prefix and `@version` suffix removed) with hyphens replaced by underscores, so `codebuff/file-picker@1.0.0` becomes `file_picker`, and the runtime also accepts the hyphenated short name (source at commit, `tool-executor.ts`). The schema shown is what the runtime generates for each spawnable agent: `prompt` and `params` copied from that agent's own `inputSchema` with their original optionality, or a passthrough object when that cannot be converted to JSON Schema. The runtime rewrites a direct call into a `spawn_agents` call with one entry whose `agent_type` is the full agent id, so it runs and returns as `spawn_agents` does (source at commit, `tool-executor.ts`). Agents are offered this way only by a parent whose `toolNames` include `spawn_agents`, and the underscored names date from 2026-04-29 (`537da7262e41`, "[codex] Use underscored direct subagent tool names (#565)") (source at commit, `537da7262e41`).

#### `set_output` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Subagents must use this tool as it is the only way to report any findings. Nothing else you write will be visible to the user/parent agent.

Note that the output schema is provided dynamically in a user prompt further down in the conversation. Be sure to follow what the latest output schema is when using this tool.

Please set the output with all the information and analysis you want to pass on. If you just want to send a simple message, use an object with the key "message" and value of the message you want to send.
Example:
<set_output_params_example>
{
  "message": "I found a bug in the code!"
}
</set_output_params_example>
```

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit d418a51, verbatim):

```js
const toolName = 'set_output'
const endsAgentStep = false

// WHY `data` EXISTS IN THE INPUT SCHEMA:
// Subagents inherit their parent's tool definitions, and because of prompt caching
// we cannot modify or add tools mid-conversation. OpenAI models enforce the tool's
// input schema strictly, so we need a permissive shape that any model can call.
// An empty schema or `z.object({}).passthrough()` would be rejected by OpenAI's
// strict schema enforcement. The `data: z.record(...)` field is a deliberately
// vague shape that satisfies OpenAI while allowing us to inject the real
// outputSchema later in the conversation (in the instructions prompt).
//
// At runtime, the handler (`packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/set-output.ts`)
// tries parsing against the real outputSchema in two ways:
//   1. Parse the raw output (agent passed fields at top level)
//   2. Fallback: parse `output.data` (agent wrapped fields in `data`)
// This means both `{ results: [...] }` and `{ data: { results: [...] } }` are accepted.
const inputSchema = z
  .looseObject({
    data: z.record(z.string(), z.any()).optional(),
  })
  .describe(
    'JSON object to set as the agent output. The shape of the parameters are specified dynamically further down in the conversation. This completely replaces any previous output. If the agent was spawned, this value will be passed back to its parent. If the agent has an outputSchema defined, the output will be validated against it.',
  )
```

Source (description and parameters): Codebuff `set_output` tool definition, `common/src/tools/params/tool/set-output.ts` lines 7-46, commit `d418a51` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The example block is rendered from the `$getNativeToolCallExampleString` helper and the example input in source, not from a live capture.

Semantics. The child calls the tool to set its output, which "completely replaces any previous output" and, for a spawned agent, "will be passed back to its parent". The call does not end the child's step (`endsAgentStep = false`), and it returns `[{type: 'json', value: {message}}]`. The real output schema reaches the child later in the conversation, and the handler accepts fields either at the top level or inside `data`.
