#### `Subagent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim template, as generated at runtime):

```text
Launch a specialized subagent to handle a specific task.

Here are the available subagents:
${agentList}
```

Source: Continue CLI source, `extensions/cli/src/subagent/get-agents.ts` (`generateSubagentToolDescription`), commit `5522c6f4` - source at commit, 2026-07-21 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). Each `${agentList}` line is `  - ${subagentModel.model.name}: ${subagentModel.model.chatOptions?.baseSystemMessage}`, and this runtime text replaces the static description "Use a subagent to handle a specialized task." in `SUBAGENT_TOOL_META`.

Parameters (JSON Schema inside a TypeScript tool object from source at commit 5522c6f4, verbatim):

```ts
export const SUBAGENT_TOOL_META: Tool = {
  name: "Subagent",
  displayName: "Subagent",
  description: "Use a subagent to handle a specialized task.",
  readonly: false,
  isBuiltIn: true,
  parameters: {
    type: "object",
    required: ["description", "prompt", "subagent_name"],
    properties: {
      description: {
        type: "string",
        description: "A short description of the task",
      },
      prompt: {
        type: "string",
        description: "The task for the agent to perform",
      },
      subagent_name: {
        type: "string",
        description: "The type of specialized agent to use for this task.",
      },
    },
  },
  run: async () => "",
};
```

Source: Continue CLI source, `extensions/cli/src/subagent/index.ts`, commit `5522c6f4` - source at commit, 2026-07-21 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The call blocks with no background mode: it runs the named subagent model with `prompt` under the parent session, streams interim output into the pending tool result, and returns `result.response` followed by the lines `<task_metadata>`, `status: completed` or `status: failed`, and `</task_metadata>` (Continue CLI `extensions/cli/src/tools/subagent.ts`, source at commit). At runtime the `subagent_name` description becomes "The type of specialized agent to use for this task. Available agents: " followed by the comma-separated agent names, the available agents are the models `ModelService.getSubagentModels` returns, and an unknown name fails with "Unknown agent type: ${subagent_name}. Available agents: " followed by the same names (same file). Before the run, the tool preview shows "Spawning ${agent.model.name} to: ${description}" (Continue CLI `extensions/cli/src/tools/subagent.ts`, source at commit). There is no cancel, wait, or status tool for subagents, and the tool is registered only when `isBetaSubagentToolEnabled()` is true (Continue CLI `extensions/cli/src/tools/index.tsx`, source at commit). The tool arrived with PR #9128, "feat: subagents", merged on 2026-01-15 (Continue pull request #9128, forum or issue).

#### `delegate_work_to_coworker` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a specific task to one of the following coworkers: {coworkers}
The input to this tool should be the coworker, the task you want them to do, and ALL necessary context to execute the task, they know nothing about the task, so share absolutely everything you know, don't reference things but instead explain them.
```

Source: CrewAI source at commit 6b93fa0, `lib/crewai/src/crewai/translations/en.json:58` (key `delegate_work`, where `\n` is a newline), filled in by `tools/agent_tools/agent_tools.py:24-29`, which replaces `{coworkers}` with the roles of the available agents joined by ", " - source at commit, 2026-10-09.

Parameters (Python pydantic model and tool class from source at commit 6b93fa0, verbatim):

```python
class DelegateWorkToolSchema(BaseModel):
    task: str = Field(..., description="The task to delegate")
    context: str = Field(..., description="The context for the task")
    coworker: str = Field(
        ..., description="The role/name of the coworker to delegate to"
    )


class DelegateWorkTool(BaseAgentTool):
    """Tool for delegating work to coworkers"""

    name: str = "Delegate work to coworker"
    args_schema: type[BaseModel] = DelegateWorkToolSchema
```

Source: CrewAI source at commit 6b93fa0, `lib/crewai/src/crewai/tools/agent_tools/delegate_work_tool.py:8-20` - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). For native function calling, CrewAI turns this model into JSON Schema with `generate_model_description(tool.args_schema, strip_null_types=False)`, removes the `title` and `description` keys, and sends it with `"strict": True` (`utilities/agent_utils.py:253-288`); the resulting JSON text is not in the sources.

Semantics. The declared name has spaces, but the model sees `delegate_work_to_coworker`: native function calling passes every name through `sanitize_tool_name` (NFKD to ASCII, camelCase split, lowercase, quotes removed, characters outside `[a-z0-9_]` turned into underscores, repeats collapsed, 64-character cap with a hash suffix) at `utilities/agent_utils.py:271`, and the ReAct text prompt prints the same sanitized name both in its tool-name list (`get_tool_names`, `agent_utils.py:189-198`) and in each tool block, which has the form "Tool Name: ...\nTool Arguments: ...\nTool Description: ..." (`tools/structured_tool.py:178-182`). The call is blocking: CrewAI builds a `Task` whose description is `task`, runs `selected_agent.execute_task(task_with_assigned_agent, context)`, and returns that text as the tool result (`base_agent_tools.py:110-120`). The coworker is matched against agent roles ignoring case, extra whitespace, and quotes; the tool also accepts `co_worker` as an alias for `coworker`, and a value like "[a,b]" uses the first entry (`base_agent_tools.py:20-44`). An unknown coworker returns "\nError executing tool. coworker mentioned not found, it must be one of the following options:\n{coworkers}\n" and a failure inside the coworker returns "Error executing task with agent '{agent_role}'. Error: {error}" (`en.json:48`, `:54`). CrewAI adds both coworker tools for an agent with `allow_delegation` set, listing the other agents in the crew, and gives them to the manager agent in the hierarchical process (`crew.py:1531-1555`, `:1658-1673`, `:1833-1843`, `:1866-1876`).

- Target models: not stated in the catalog; the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model card says the model was "evaluated with the Minimal mode of DeepSeek Harness" (official doc, 2026-09-10)
- Sources:
  - DeepSeek Harness Tool Schema Catalog, https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/reference/tool-catalog - official doc, undated developer preview (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog)
  - docs/tool-catalog.md at tag dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1, https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/5badb15009ae1756c3afe0ae0cef1faafc290ccc/docs/tool-catalog.md - source at commit, 2026-10-03 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog)
  - docs/tool-catalog.md at tag dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2, https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/d743267388641bc76f17c45ce8b4c231aed1d32c/docs/tool-catalog.md - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog)
  - docs/tool-catalog.md at tag dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2, https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84/docs/tool-catalog.md - source at commit, 2026-09-29 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog)
  - deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness repository (MIT License), https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness - source at commit, `master` at `d743267` (2026-10-09)
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model card, https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash - official doc, created 2026-09-10

The catalog is generated by booting each tool plugin with its default config and reading `ctx.tools.schemas()`. The delegation tool's registered name is "the load-time `toolName` config (default `subagent`)", with shipped aliases `subagent` and `subagent_fork`, and `list_subagent_models` is a companion for picking a provider and model when model selection is enabled. In the published docs and at `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1`, a background subagent is a job that the shared `job_output`, `job_list`, and `job_kill` tools read, list, and kill alongside background shell commands; at `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2` the `subagent` tool always returns a child id at once, drops `run_in_background`, adds `cwd`, and the jobs package note no longer lists subagents. An experimental package, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-agent-team`, adds nine team tools (`interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, `send_message`, `spawn_teammate`, `team_task_create`, `team_task_get`, `team_task_list`, `team_task_update`, `wait_agent`); "The shipped dsh-base bundle keeps the package disabled".

#### `subagent` (spawn; 0.2.1-alpha.1)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work - research, a scoped implementation, an analysis - so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema from the generated catalog, verbatim):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display."
    },
    "prompt": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs."
    },
    "run_in_background": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Run as a background job and return its id (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). Defaults to false."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "description",
    "prompt"
  ]
}
```

Source (description and parameters): `docs/tool-catalog.md`, section `subagent` (generated from `packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts`), tag `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1`, commit `5badb15` - source at commit, 2026-10-03; the published Tool Schema Catalog page fetched 2026-10-10 has the same text.

Semantics. The call blocks by default and returns the subagent's result; with `run_in_background: true` it returns a job id at once, and the result is collected with `job_output` and the run stopped with `job_kill`. Background completion is announced by a notice the jobs package injects ("user/message via agent.inject() for background completion notices"); whether that notice includes the subagent's result was not verified. Each instance "independently controls whether it reads model-selection settings and its background behavior through `modelSelectionSettings`, `backgroundMode`, and `enableRunInBackground`", and the registered name comes from the load-time `toolName` config.

#### `subagent` (spawn; 0.2.1-alpha.2)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work - research, a scoped implementation, an analysis - so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.
```

```json
    },
```

Semantics. At this tag the call never blocks: it "starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id", and "The runtime notifies you when it finishes." The child reports its results to the parent with `send_message`, which the parent also uses to steer the child or continue it later. The package note says "Every delegation returns a child id promptly; local children accept follow-ups, while external backends report their single execution automatically." `run_in_background` is gone, and `cwd` sets the child's initial working directory.

#### `ralph` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.
```

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "objective": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round."
    },
    "maxRounds": {
      "type": "number",

    }
```

Semantics. The call runs in the foreground: each round starts one fresh child with no parent conversation, and the call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or when the round cap is reached. The model chooses only the objective and an optional `maxRounds`, which the deployment ceiling bounds. At `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2` the text is unchanged and the catalog lists the source under `packages/experimental/tool-ralph`.

#### `workflow` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces - an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings - where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` - run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` - run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` - run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` - start a progress phase; `log(message)` - narrate progress; `args` - the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.
```

A sub-agent's `mode` decides which tool the parent sees: "chat: Standard chat agent reachable via transfer_to_agent. task: Task agent that chats with the user to accomplish a task. single_turn: Agents that complete a task without chatting with the user." and "Default value is chat as a sub-agent, single_turn as a node in a workflow." (llm_agent.py lines 419-428). Chat-mode targets share one `transfer_to_agent` tool, each `single_turn` or `task` sub-agent becomes its own tool named after the agent, and a task-mode agent gets `finish_task` to report back (llm_agent.py lines 1333-1356). A developer can also wrap an agent with `AgentTool`, whose declaration `single_turn` sub-agents reuse, and its docstring says "Direct usage of ``AgentTool`` is discouraged." (agent_tool.py lines 118-128).

#### `<agent_name>` (spawn; `single_turn` sub-agent or `AgentTool`)

Description: no framework text. The description is the agent's own `description` field (`description=self.agent.description`).

Parameters (Python `FunctionDeclaration` with a JSON Schema dict, from source at commit bcac35a, verbatim):

```python
        result = types.FunctionDeclaration(
            name=self.name,
            description=self.agent.description,
            parameters_json_schema={
                'type': 'object',
                'properties': {
                    'request': {'type': 'string'},
                },
                'required': ['request'],
            },
        )
```

Source (description and parameters): adk-python source, `src/google/adk/tools/agent_tool.py` lines 152 and 174-185, commit `bcac35a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. When the `JSON_SCHEMA_FOR_FUNC_DECL` feature is off, the same shape is built as a `types.Schema` (lines 186-199); when the agent defines an `input_schema`, the declaration is built from that schema instead, still with the agent's description (lines 167-172).

Semantics. The tool name is the agent's `name` unchanged (`super().__init__(name=agent.name, description=agent.description)` and `result.name = self.name`, agent_tool.py lines 152, 217), and the schema shown is what ADK generates for each child that has no `input_schema`. A chat-mode `LlmAgent` wraps each `mode='single_turn'` sub-agent in `_SingleTurnAgentTool`, which passes `args.get('request')` to `tool_context.run_node(...)`, returns the subagent's result as the tool result, and returns "Error running sub-agent: {e}" on failure (agent_tool.py lines 419-457; llm_agent.py lines 1353-1354). A directly used `AgentTool` runs the agent in its own `Runner` with an in-memory session, forwards state deltas to the parent, and returns the last event's text, validated against the agent's output schema if it has one, as the tool result (agent_tool.py lines 220-385). The `AgentTool` docstring says "To expose an agent as an inline tool of a parent ``LlmAgent``, prefer setting ``mode='single_turn'`` on the sub-agent and attaching it via ``sub_agents=[...]`` instead of wrapping it with ``AgentTool``." (agent_tool.py lines 118-122). ADK exposes no background, status, wait, or cancel tool for subagents; `LongRunningFunctionTool` (long_running_tool.py line 27) is a generic long-operation tool.

#### `<agent_name>` (spawn; `task` mode)

```text
{agent.description}
IMPORTANT: This tool delegates execution to a specialized agent. Do NOT call this tool in parallel with any other tools.
```

```python
class _DefaultTaskInput(BaseModel):
```

Source (description and parameters): adk-python source, `src/google/adk/tools/agent_tool.py` lines 460-463 and 489-508, commit `bcac35a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description is `f'{base_desc}{suffix}'.strip()`, where `base_desc` is `self.agent.description or ''` and the suffix starts with a newline; `_DefaultTaskInput` is used when the agent has no `input_schema` and is converted with `build_function_declaration_with_json_schema` (lines 493-501).

Semantics. The tool name is the agent's `name` (`result.name = self.name`, agent_tool.py line 508), and the schema shown is what ADK generates for each `mode='task'` sub-agent that has no `input_schema` (llm_agent.py lines 1355-1356). The class docstring calls `_TaskAgentTool` "a framework delegation marker" and says "The wrapper intercepts calls to this tool to drive task sub-agent execution via ctx.run_node."; the tool sets `self._defers_response = True`, and its own `run_async` returns `None` with the comment "Framework handles task delegation dispatch directly via the wrapper." (agent_tool.py lines 466-527). The `mode` docstring describes a task agent as one "that chats with the user to accomplish a task" (llm_agent.py line 424), and the task agent ends by calling `finish_task`; how the task result is then shown to the parent model is not in the sources beyond the `finish_task` code comment quoted in that tool's semantics. Task-mode and `single_turn` sub-agents are not `transfer_to_agent` targets, because both modes are in `DELEGATED_TASK_MODES`, documented as "Agent modes that execute as tool-delegated tasks rather than LLM transfers." (_agent_transfer.py lines 252-258; _agent_mode.py lines 62-66).

#### `transfer_to_agent` (handoff)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Transfer the query to another agent.

Use this tool to hand off control to another agent that is more suitable to
answer the user's query according to the agent's description.

Args:
  agent_name: the agent name to transfer to.
```

Parameters (Python function signature from source at commit bcac35a, verbatim):

```python
def transfer_to_agent(
    agent_name: str,
    tool_context: ToolContext,
    *,
    transfer_reason: str = '',

```

Source (description and parameters): adk-python source, `src/google/adk/tools/transfer_to_agent_tool.py` lines 27-42, 49-54, and 81-133, commit `bcac35a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description is `inspect.cleandoc` of the `_transfer_to_agent_without_reason` docstring, which `TransferToAgentTool` uses unless `include_transfer_reason=True`; `_get_declaration` sets `enum` on `agent_name` to the list of valid target names and deletes `transfer_reason` unless that flag is set, and `_build_transfer_tool` builds the tool without it (_agent_transfer.py lines 282-295), so the model sees only `agent_name`; `tool_context` is the context parameter that `FunctionTool` drops from declarations (function_tool.py lines 103-121).

Semantics. ADK gives one `transfer_to_agent` tool for all targets: chat-mode sub-agents, the parent unless `disallow_transfer_to_parent` is set, and peers unless `disallow_transfer_to_peers` is set (_agent_transfer.py lines 233-279). The function sets `tool_context.actions.transfer_to_agent = agent_name` and returns `None` (transfer_to_agent_tool.py lines 64-65), and the LLM flow is documented as "A basic flow that calls the LLM in a loop until a final response is generated." and "This flow ends when it transfers to another agent." (base_llm_flow.py lines 93-96), so control moves to the named agent and no result comes back to the caller as a tool result. ADK injects an instruction that lists each target's name and description and says "call `{tool_name}` function to transfer the question to that agent. When transferring, do not generate any text other than the function call." and "**NOTE**: the only available agents for `{tool_name}` function are {formatted_agent_names}." (_agent_transfer.py lines 151-200). A sub-agent with a parent also gets "If neither you nor the other agents are best for the question, transfer to your parent agent {agent.parent_agent.name}." (_agent_transfer.py lines 226-229). Agents in delegated task modes still receive the tool when they have targets but get no transfer instruction (_agent_transfer.py lines 73-90, 221-222).

#### `finish_task` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Signal that this agent has completed its delegated task. Call this when you have finished your delegated task.
```

Parameters (Python Pydantic model from source at commit bcac35a, verbatim):

```python
class _DefaultTaskOutput(BaseModel):
  """Default output schema when no custom output_schema is provided.

  Used by FinishTaskTool to generate the function declaration when the
  task agent does not define an explicit output_schema.
  """

  model_config = ConfigDict(
      extra='forbid',
      alias_generator=alias_generators.to_camel,
      populate_by_name=True,
  )

  result: str
  """A brief summary of what the agent accomplished."""
```

Source (description and parameters): adk-python source, `src/google/adk/agents/llm/task/_finish_task_tool.py` lines 40 and 102-112, and `src/google/adk/agents/llm/task/_task_models.py` lines 83-97, commit `bcac35a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. When the task agent has an `output_schema`, " Pass the required output data in the parameters." is appended to the description and that schema replaces the default; a non-object schema is wrapped in an object with one required `result` property (_finish_task_tool.py lines 52-67, 106-107, 114-136).

Semantics. ADK adds `finish_task` to the tools of every `mode='task'` agent (llm_agent.py lines 1333-1336) and appends the instruction "Do NOT call `finish_task` prematurely. Use your available tools to fully complete every aspect of the delegated task first. If the task is unclear, ask the user for clarification before proceeding. Once the task is fully complete, call `finish_task` by itself with no accompanying text output." (_finish_task_tool.py lines 152-166). The tool validates its arguments against the output schema and returns "Task completed." on success; on a validation error it returns an `error` message ending "You could retry calling this tool, but it is IMPORTANT for you to provide all the mandatory parameters with correct types." and a validation-error response is not terminal, "so the caller keeps iterating and the LLM gets a chance to retry" (_finish_task_tool.py lines 168-222). A code comment says "The LlmAgent wrapper sniffs the finish_task FC's `output` arg directly to set event.output on the task agent's run." (_finish_task_tool.py lines 201-203), and `llm_agent.py` says "Task mode agents deliver their final output via finish_task, not intermediate conversational text turns." (llm_agent.py lines 1100-1101).

### Google Gemini CLI

The parent sees one spawn tool, `invoke_agent`, and each subagent sees the child-side return tool `complete_task`. There is no model-facing wait, status, message, list, or cancel tool for subagents.

#### `invoke_agent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Invoke a subagent to perform a specific task or investigation.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema object literal in the TypeScript source at commit 9b6e026, verbatim):

```ts
      {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          agent_name: {
            type: 'string',
            description: 'Name of the subagent to invoke',
          },
          prompt: {
            type: 'string',
            description:
              'The COMPLETE query to send the subagent. MUST be comprehensive and detailed. Include all context, background, questions, and expected output format. Do NOT send brief or incomplete instructions.',
          },
        },
        required: ['agent_name', 'prompt'],
      },
```

Source (description and parameters): Gemini CLI source at commit 9b6e026, `packages/core/src/agents/agent-tool.ts` (`AgentTool` constructor; file last changed `c4758ba8204a`, 2026-05-19) - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Agent list (system-prompt template from `renderSubAgents`, verbatim):

```text
# Available Sub-Agents

Sub-agents are specialized expert agents. You can invoke them using the ${formatToolName(AGENT_TOOL_NAME)} tool by passing their name to the \`agent_name\` parameter. You MUST delegate tasks to the sub-agent with the most relevant expertise.

### Strategic Orchestration & Delegation
Operate as a **strategic orchestrator**. Your own context window is your most precious resource. Every turn you take adds to the permanent session history. To keep the session fast and efficient, use sub-agents to "compress" complex or repetitive work.

When you delegate, the sub-agent's entire execution is consolidated into a single summary in your history, keeping your main loop lean.

**Concurrency Safety and Mandate:** You should NEVER run multiple subagents in a single turn if their abilities mutate the same files or resources. This is to prevent race conditions and ensure that the workspace is in a consistent state. Only run multiple subagents in parallel when their tasks are independent (e.g., multiple concurrent research or read-only tasks) or if parallel execution is explicitly requested by the user.

**High-Impact Delegation Candidates:**
- **Repetitive Batch Tasks:** Tasks involving more than 3 files or repeated steps (e.g., "Add license headers to all files in src/", "Fix all lint errors in the project").
- **High-Volume Output:** Commands or tools expected to return large amounts of data (e.g., verbose builds, exhaustive file searches).
- **Speculative Research:** Investigations that require many "trial and error" steps before a clear path is found.

**Assertive Action:** Continue to handle "surgical" tasks directly - simple reads, single-file edits, or direct questions that can be resolved in 1-2 turns. Delegation is an efficiency tool, not a way to avoid direct action when it is the fastest path.

<available_subagents>
${subAgentsXml}
</available_subagents>

Remember that the closest relevant sub-agent should still be used even if its expertise is broader than the given task.

For example:
- A license-agent -> Should be used for a range of tasks, including reading, validating, and updating licenses and headers.
- A test-fixing-agent -> Should be used both for fixing tests as well as investigating test failures.
```

Source: Gemini CLI source at commit 9b6e026, `packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts` (`renderSubAgents`, last changed `f5dc904d21da`, 2026-09-29) - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The tool description itself is a fixed string; the agent list reaches the model only through this system-prompt section, where `${formatToolName(AGENT_TOOL_NAME)}` (the `invoke_agent` name) and `${subAgentsXml}` are filled at runtime, each agent rendering as `<subagent>`, `<name>${agent.name}</name>`, `<description>${agent.description}</description>`, `</subagent>` on separate indented lines.

Semantics. `invoke_agent` always blocks and returns the subagent's outcome as its tool result, `Subagent '${this.definition.name}' finished.\nTermination Reason: ${output.terminate_reason}\nResult:\n${output.result}` or `Subagent '${this.definition.name}' failed. Error: ${errorMessage}`, where the termination reason is one of `ERROR`, `TIMEOUT`, `GOAL`, `MAX_TURNS`, `ABORTED`, or `ERROR_NO_COMPLETE_TASK_CALL` (source at commit, `local-invocation.ts`). `prompt` is placed into the target agent's single input key when it has exactly one, otherwise passed as `{ prompt }`, and an unknown name fails with `Subagent '${params.agent_name}' not found.`; the built-in agents are `codebase_investigator` (input `objective`), `cli_help` (input `question`), `generalist` (input `request`), and `browser_agent` when enabled (source at commit, `registry.ts`). There are no subagent ids, and subagents cannot call agents because the executor skips tools of kind `Agent` (source at commit, `local-executor.ts`); background mode exists only for the shell tool `run_shell_command`, not for subagents. Rename history: one tool per agent, named after the agent, on 2025-10-01 (PR #9988); one `delegate_to_agent` tool with an `anyOf` branch per agent on 2025-12-10 (PR #14769); back to one tool per agent on 2026-01-23 (PR #17346, which says `delegate_to_agent` caused "schema squashing" and `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` errors on Gemini 3 Pro and that the per-agent design "leverages knowledge the model already has around how to call functions"); then `invoke_agent` on 2026-04-09 (PR #24489, per-agent wrappers removed in PR #25053). PR #24489's title says "invoke_subagent" while its code and body say `invoke_agent` (defined as `AGENT_TOOL_NAME = 'invoke_agent'`, display name `Invoke Subagent`), and the policy engine treats `agent_name` as a virtual tool name, so `PLAN_MODE_TOOLS` still lists `'codebase_investigator'` and `'cli_help'` (PR #24489; source at commit, `tool-names.ts`).

#### `complete_task` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Call this tool to submit your final findings and complete the task. This is the ONLY way to finish.
```

Parameters (TypeScript function that builds the JSON Schema, source at commit 9b6e026, verbatim):

```ts
  private static buildParameterSchema(
    outputConfig?: OutputConfig<z.ZodTypeAny>,
  ): unknown {
    if (outputConfig) {
      const jsonSchema = zodToJsonSchema(outputConfig.schema);
      const {
        $schema: _$schema,
        definitions: _definitions,
        ...schema
      } = jsonSchema;
      return {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          [outputConfig.outputName]: schema,
        },
        required: [outputConfig.outputName],
      };
    }
    return {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        result: {
          type: 'string',
          description:
            'Your final results or findings to return to the orchestrator. ' +
            'Ensure this is comprehensive and follows any formatting requested in your instructions.',
        },
      },
      required: ['result'],
    };
  }
```

Source (description and parameters): Gemini CLI source at commit 9b6e026, `packages/core/src/tools/complete-task.ts` (file last changed `3b7c17a22c8b`, 2026-04-10) - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. A subagent calls `complete_task` to end its run; a subagent with a structured output configuration instead sees the description "Call this tool to submit your final answer and complete the task. This is the ONLY way to finish." and a single required parameter named after `outputName` (`report` for `codebase_investigator` and `cli_help`), validated against the agent's zod schema. The child's tool result is "Result submitted and task completed." (or "Output submitted and task completed."), the tool's data holds `taskCompleted: true` and the submitted value as `submittedOutput`, and a call with an empty `result` fails with "Missing required "result" argument. You must provide your findings when calling complete_task." Defaults are `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 30` and `DEFAULT_MAX_TIME_MINUTES = 10`; when a subagent hits a limit it gets one grace turn with the text "`${explanation}` You have one final chance to complete the task with a short grace period. You MUST call \`complete_task\` immediately with your best answer and explain that your investigation was interrupted. Do not call any other tools.", and a run that ends without the call terminates with `ERROR_NO_COMPLETE_TASK_CALL` (source at commit, `local-executor.ts` and `types.ts`). The tool was already named `complete_task` in December 2025.

Goose's `summon` platform extension gives the parent `delegate` and `load`; the extension is registered with `unprefixed_tools: true`, so these names have no extension prefix, while other extensions expose `"{key}__{tool}"`. A subagent session gets `load` only, and each subagent finishes by calling `recipe__final_output`. Background mode and the hidden `orchestrator__*` tools were removed on 2026-10-07, so at this commit every delegate runs in the foreground.

#### `delegate` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a task to a subagent that runs independently with its own context.

Modes:
1. Ad-hoc: Provide `instructions` for a custom task
2. Source-based: Provide `source` name to run a subrecipe, recipe, or agent
3. Combined: Pair a source with a task (e.g., source: "deploy", instructions: "deploy to staging")

Effective Delegation:
- Delegates know only instructions + source content
- Delegates cannot coordinate. Same-file work = conflicts.
- You get a delegate's result back once it finishes.

Research (read-only): delegates explore and report back.
Work (writes): partition files strictly - no two delegates touch the same file.
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `serde_json::json!` in Rust, verbatim):

```rust
        let schema = serde_json::json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "instructions": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Task instructions. Required for ad-hoc tasks."
                },
                "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Name of a recipe or agent to run."
                },
                "parameters": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "additionalProperties": true,
                    "description": "Parameters for the source (only valid with source)."
                },
                "extensions": {
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {"type": "string"},
                    "description": "Extensions to enable. Omit to inherit all, empty array for none."
                },
                "provider": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Override LLM provider."
                },
                "model": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Override model."
                },
                "temperature": {
                    "type": "number",
                    "description": "Override temperature."
                },
                "max_turns": {
                    "type": "integer",
                    "minimum": 1,
                    "description": "Maximum turns for this delegate. Overrides recipe settings.max_turns and GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS."
                },
                "context": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Reference context to inject into the delegate's system prompt. Use for background information, file contents, or constraints the delegate needs but that aren't part of the task instructions."
                },
                "working_dir": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Working directory for the delegate. Must be within the parent session's working directory. Defaults to the parent's working directory."
                }
            }
        });
```

Source (description and parameters): Goose source, `crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/summon.rs` lines 449-515 (`create_delegate_tool`), commit 3bd8520 - source at commit, 2026-10-09; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description block is the Rust string literal with its `\n\` line continuations resolved.

Semantics. The schema requires no property, but the handler rejects a call that has neither `instructions` nor `source` ("Must provide 'instructions' or 'source' (or both)") or that passes `parameters` without `source`, and subagent sessions are not offered `delegate` at all ("Delegated tasks cannot spawn further delegations" is the guard error). The call returns at once with "Delegated to foreground subagent {id}"; once every tool call in the parent's turn has a response, the pending subagents run concurrently and each outcome is appended to the parent's conversation as a user message hidden from the user but visible to the model: "Subagent {id} completed: {output}" (where `{output}` is the subagent's final-output JSON, such as `{"summary":"..."}`), "Subagent {id} failed: {reason}", or "Subagent {id} was cancelled before it finished and will not run again." (source at commit, `ops_foreground_subagent.rs`). The turn limit comes from `max_turns`, then the recipe's `settings.max_turns`, then `GOOSE_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS`, then a default of 25. From 2026-02-10 until 2026-10-07 `delegate` also took an `async` boolean ("Run in background (default: false).") whose acknowledgement was `Task {} started in background: "{}"\nContinue with other work. When you need the result, use load(source: "{}").`; commit 8f72d2d3055b (PR #12729) removed it together with the hidden, default-off `orchestrator__list_sessions`, `orchestrator__view_session`, `orchestrator__start_agent`, `orchestrator__send_message`, and `orchestrator__interrupt_agent` tools, which had existed since 2026-03-19 (source at commit, d2fe88f4, 8f72d2d3055b, and 3f8eec3237a7). Earlier spawn tools were `subrecipe__run__<name>` (2025-06-24 to 2025-07-04), `subagent__run_task` (2025-06-25 to 2025-07-18), `subrecipe__create_task_<name>` (2025-07-04 to 2025-12-13), `sub_recipe__execute_task` (2025-07-04 to 2025-07-18), `subagent__execute_task` with `dynamic_task__create_task` (2025-07-18 to 2025-12-13), and `subagent` (2025-12-13 to 2026-02-10), which commit 7ea19f5c83da (PR #6964) replaced with `delegate` and `load` (source at commit, 9e6247d9ed09, d9d7eb06978e, 2e9a2a53be9d, 4771ffbb5bda, a131b08817fa, and 7ea19f5c83da).

#### `load` (list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Load knowledge into your current context or discover available sources.

Call with no arguments to list all available sources (subrecipes, recipes, agents).
Call with a source name to load its content into your context.

Examples:
- load() → Lists available sources
- load(source: "deploy") → Loads the deploy recipe
```

Parameters (JSON Schema built with `serde_json::json!` in Rust, verbatim):

```rust
        let schema = serde_json::json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Name of the source to load. If omitted, lists all available sources."
                }
            }
        });
```

Source (description and parameters): Goose source, `crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/summon.rs` lines 425-447 (`create_load_tool`), commit 3bd8520 - source at commit, 2026-10-09; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description block is the Rust string literal with its `\n\` line continuations resolved.

Semantics. At this commit `load` only lists sources (subrecipes, recipes, and agents) or loads one source's content into the caller's context, and it is the one summon tool a subagent session gets. Agent sources come from `.goose/agents`, `.claude/agents`, and `.agents/agents` in the working directory, and from `.goose/agents`, `.agents/agents`, the Goose config `agents` directory, and `.claude/agents` in the home directory (`summon.rs` lines 274-289). From 2026-02-10 until 2026-10-07 `load` also served background delegates: it took a `cancel` boolean ("For running background tasks: cancel and return output.") and, from 2026-06-18 (PR #9519), a `peek` boolean ("For running background tasks: check progress without blocking. Returns durable assistant-turn count, idle time, and recent tool activity."), and its description included `"For background tasks: load(source: \"task_id\") waits for the task and returns the result.\n To cancel a running task: load(source: \"task_id\", cancel: true) stops and returns output.\n To check progress: load(source: \"task_id\", peek: true) returns status without blocking."` (source at commit, d2fe88f4 and 6d3620d66f4d). Both booleans were removed in commit 8f72d2d3055b (PR #12729) on 2026-10-07 (source at commit, 8f72d2d3055b).

#### `recipe__final_output` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
The final_output tool collects the final output for the user and provides validation for structured JSON final output against a predefined schema.

This final_output tool MUST be called with the final output for the user.

Purpose:
- Collects the final output for the user
- Ensures that final outputs conform to the expected JSON structure
- Provides clear validation feedback when outputs don't match the schema

Usage:
- Call the `final_output` tool with your JSON final output passed as the argument.

The expected JSON schema format is:

{}

When validation fails, you'll receive:
- Specific validation errors
- The expected format
```

Source: Goose source, `crates/goose/src/agents/final_output_tool.rs` lines 173-195 (`FinalOutputTool::tool`, a `formatdoc!` template), commit 3bd8520 - source at commit, 2026-10-09; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. At runtime `{}` is replaced with the pretty-printed response JSON Schema.

Parameters (default response JSON Schema for a delegate whose source defines none, Rust `serde_json::json!`, verbatim):

```rust
        if recipe
            .response
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|response| response.json_schema.as_ref())
            .is_none()
        {
            recipe.response = Some(Response {
                json_schema: Some(serde_json::json!({
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}},
                    "required": ["summary"]
                })),
            });
        }
```

Source: Goose source, `crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/summon.rs` lines 878-891, commit 3bd8520 - source at commit, 2026-10-09; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The tool's input schema is the recipe's `response.json_schema` as is (`final_output_tool.rs` lines 196-206).

Semantics. The input schema is the recipe's `response` JSON Schema, so a delegate with no recipe schema calls this tool with `{"summary": string}`. A valid call returns "Final output successfully collected."; an invalid one returns an error that begins "Validation failed:" and lists the validation errors and the expected format. The collected JSON, serialized on one line, becomes `{output}` in the parent's "Subagent {id} completed: {output}" message (source at commit, `ops_foreground_subagent.rs`). The description and the final-output system prompt call the tool `final_output`, while the registered name is `recipe__final_output` (`FINAL_OUTPUT_TOOL_NAME`), and recipes with a `response` block use the same tool outside delegation.

The README says the project is "community-built, open-source, and **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by xAI Corp.**" and lists "**sub-agents on by default**". The model sees `task` for foreground subagents and, in `agent` mode only, `delegate`, `delegation_read`, and `delegation_list` for background subagents (`src/grok/tools.ts`, which registers each tool only when the matching runner option is present).

#### `task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delegate a focused foreground task to a sub-agent. Prefer this proactively for review, research, investigation, code quality work, verification, and computer-use flows instead of waiting for the user to request a sub-agent. Use `general` for multi-step execution, `explore` for fast read-only investigation, `vision` for image validation, `verify` for sandbox-aware build, test, and smoke validation, `verify-detect` for read-only verification recipe detection, `verify-manifest` to create or update a verification manifest, and `computer` for host desktop screenshot/input workflows.${customHint} Provide a short description plus a detailed prompt for the child agent.
```

Source: Grok CLI source, `src/grok/tools.ts` (a TypeScript template literal shown as its string value; `${customHint}` is empty when no custom sub-agents are configured, and otherwise reads ` You may also use these user-defined sub-agents by exact name: ${customNames.join(", ")}.`), commit `fb97af83` - source at commit, 2026-05-15 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit fb97af83, verbatim):

```ts
    const taskAgentEnum = [
      "general",
      "explore",
      "vision",
      "verify",
      "verify-detect",
      "verify-manifest",
      "computer",
      ...customNames,
    ] as [string, ...string[]];
...
      inputSchema: z.object({
        agent: z
          .enum(taskAgentEnum)
          .default("general")
          .describe(
            customNames.length > 0
              ? "Built-in general, explore, vision, verify, verify-detect, verify-manifest, or computer, or a configured custom sub-agent name from user settings"
              : "Which sub-agent to use",

```

Source: Grok CLI source, `src/grok/tools.ts`, commit `fb97af83` - source at commit, 2026-05-15 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. `task` is a foreground subagent: the call waits for the subagent and returns the `ToolResult` of the `runTask` runner, whose text format is not in the sources. The `agent` enum holds the seven built-in sub-agents plus the names of any custom sub-agents loaded from user settings, and defaults to `general`. Completion is the tool result itself; there is no ID and no companion tool for foreground subagents.

#### `delegate` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a read-only background agent that can keep researching while you continue working. Use this only for `explore` tasks that do not edit files or make shell changes. You will be notified when it completes.
```

Parameters (zod schema from source at commit fb97af83, verbatim):

```ts
        inputSchema: z.object({
          agent: z
            .enum(["explore"])
            .default("explore")
            .describe("Background delegations currently support only the read-only explore agent"),
          description: z.string().describe("A short label for the delegation, such as 'OAuth callback research'"),
          prompt: z.string().describe("Detailed instructions for the background agent to complete"),
        }),
```

Source (description and parameters): Grok CLI source, `src/grok/tools.ts`, commit `fb97af83` - source at commit, 2026-05-15 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. `delegate` starts a detached background process and returns at once with four lines joined by newlines: `Delegation started: ${id}`, `Agent: explore`, `You will be notified when it completes.`, and ``Use `delegation_read("${id}")` to retrieve the full result later.`` (`src/agent/delegations.ts`, source at commit). IDs are built from an adjective, a color, and an animal, such as 'calm-blue-fox' in the `delegation_read` schema. The completion notice is the lines ``Background agent ${statusText}: `${record.id}` ``, `Title: ${title}`, `Summary: ${summary}`, an optional `Error: ${record.error}`, and ``Use `delegation_read("${record.id}")` to retrieve the full result.``, where `statusText` is `complete` or `failed`; how the notice enters the model's context is not in the sources. A background child cannot delegate again ("Nested background delegations are disabled."), and an agent other than `explore` is refused with ``Background delegations are read-only. Use `delegate` with the `explore` agent, or use `task` for foreground work that may edit files.`` (`src/agent/delegations.ts`, source at commit).

```text
Read the saved output of a background delegation by ID. Use this after a completion notice or when revisiting prior research.
```

Semantics. `delegation_read` does not wait: it returns the saved Markdown output file of a finished delegation, or `Delegation "${id}" is still running. Continue working and wait for the completion notice.` while it runs, or ``Delegation "${id}" not found. Use `delegation_list()` to see available results.`` for an unknown ID (`src/agent/delegations.ts`, source at commit). A failed delegation without a readable output file returns `Delegation "${id}" failed.\n\n${record.error}`.

Semantics. `delegation_list` takes no arguments and lists the delegations stored for the current project, newest first by start time (`src/agent/delegations.ts`, source at commit); the text format of its result is not in the sources.

The model sees one subagent tool, `delegate_task` (toolset `delegation`), whose `action` parameter selects `spawn` (the default), `list`, `steer`, or `stop`. The static description and the `tasks` description in the schema are placeholders; every `get_definitions()` call replaces them with text built from the user's delegation settings, and the parts that vary are named under the description block.

#### `delegate_task` (spawn, message, list, cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn subagents in isolated contexts; each gets its own conversation, terminal session, and toolset, and only its final summary returns to you. Pass every task in `tasks` - one entry spawns one subagent, several run in parallel (limit in the tasks description).

Sessions without a later-result consumer (including one-shot CLI and cron) join parallel children and return results in this tool call. Otherwise runs in the background: dispatch returns live transcript paths and results re-enter as a new message when subagents finish (one message per call). Background results are delivered only BETWEEN your turns: finish whatever does not depend on them, then give a one-line status and END YOUR TURN. Never wait or poll on transcripts, artifact files, or CI for a child. While children run, `action` (list/steer/stop) controls them live.

USE FOR: reasoning-heavy subtasks, work that would flood your context, or independent parallel workstreams.
DO NOT USE FOR (use these instead):
- Mechanical multi-step work with no reasoning needed -> execute_code
- A single tool call -> call the tool directly
- Tasks needing user interaction -> subagents cannot ask questions
- Durable work that must survive this session -> cronjob or terminal(background=True, notify=True); /stop, /new, or process exit halts running subagents (whole tree); each returns an 'interrupted' completion with partial output.

RULES:
- Children know nothing of this conversation: pass everything needed via 'context', including any required output language, tone, or style (e.g. "respond in Chinese").
- Child summaries are SELF-REPORTS, not verified facts: a child claiming "uploaded successfully" or "file written" may be wrong. For external side effects (uploads, remote writes, publishing), require a verifiable handle (URL, ID, absolute path) and verify it yourself before telling the user the operation succeeded.
- Children cannot close tracked work: a child asked to close it returns findings instead; the parent applies the transition.
- Children cannot call delegate_task, clarify, memory, or cronjob.
- Children inherit the parent model unless pinned via delegation.provider / delegation.model in config.yaml.
```

Source: Hermes Agent `delegate_task` tool, `tools/delegate_tool.py` lines 589-646 (`_build_top_level_description`, `_DESCRIPTION_HEAD`, `_DESCRIPTION_TAIL`), commit `6a2662a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog.

The block shows the build with default settings. The parenthetical "(one message per call)" becomes "(each ungrouped task / `group` returns on its own)" when `delegation.independent_completions` is true, and when `delegation.max_spawn_depth` is 2 or more with `delegation.orchestrator_enabled` on, the line "- Children cannot call delegate_task, clarify, memory, or cronjob." is replaced by "- Children cannot call clarify, memory, or cronjob." and "- Children can themselves delegate while depth remains (max_spawn_depth={N}); the runtime derives this from depth automatically." with the configured depth in place of `{N}`. The static placeholder description is "Spawn one or more subagents in isolated contexts. Description is rebuilt at every get_definitions() call to reflect the user's current delegation limits."

Parameters (Python dict holding a JSON Schema, from source at commit 6a2662a, verbatim):

```python
def _build_tasks_param_description() -> str:
    """Compose the 'tasks' parameter description with current concurrency limit."""
    try:
        max_children = _get_max_concurrent_children()
    except Exception:
        max_children = _DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN
    return (
        f"The task(s), up to {max_children} in parallel for this user (set "
        "via delegation.max_concurrent_children). Each entry spawns one "
        "subagent with isolated context and terminal session; a single task "
        "is a one-entry array. Required when spawning."
    )

def _build_dynamic_schema_overrides() -> dict:
    """Per-call schema overrides (ToolEntry.dynamic_schema_overrides): every
    get_definitions() pass rewrites the descriptions to the user's actual limits."""
    from tools.delegate_tool_config import _get_independent_completions

    independent_completions = _get_independent_completions()
    overrides_params = {**DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA["parameters"]}
    # Copy properties so the static schema dict is never mutated.
    overrides_params["properties"] = {k: dict(v) for k, v in DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA["parameters"]["properties"].items()}
    overrides_params["properties"]["tasks"]["description"] = _build_tasks_param_description()

    if not independent_completions:
        tasks = overrides_params["properties"]["tasks"]
        tasks["items"] = {**tasks["items"], "properties": {
            k: v for k, v in tasks["items"]["properties"].items() if k != "group"
        }}

    return {
        "description": _build_top_level_description(independent_completions=independent_completions),
        "parameters": overrides_params,
    }

def _p(type_: str, description: str, **extra) -> dict:
    return {"type": type_, **extra, "description": description}

DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA = {
    "name": "delegate_task",
    # description / tasks.description are placeholders: the real text is built per get_definitions() call by
    # _build_dynamic_schema_overrides() so the model sees the user's actual max_concurrent_children / max_spawn_depth.
    # Lazy (not at import) so cli.CLI_CONFIG isn't forced to load before the test conftest redirects HERMES_HOME.
    "description": (
        "Spawn one or more subagents in isolated contexts. "
        "Description is rebuilt at every get_definitions() call to reflect the user's current delegation limits."
    ),
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            # The handler also accepts the legacy single-goal shape (top-level `goal`/`context`/`output_schema`),
            # wrapped into a one-entry batch at dispatch, and a per-task `role` (legacy, ignored: capability is
            # depth-derived). Both unadvertised on purpose (old transcripts only); do not re-add. No maxItems - the
            # runtime limit (delegation.max_concurrent_children) is enforced with a clear error in delegate_task().
            "tasks": {
                "type": "array",
                "minItems": 1,
                "items": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "goal": _p(
                            "string",
                            "What this subagent should accomplish. Be specific and self-contained - it knows "
                            "nothing about your conversation history.",
                        ),
                        "context": _p(
                            "string",
                            "Background THIS child needs: file paths, error messages, constraints. Each child "
                            "sees only its own context - repeat shared background in every task that needs it.",
                        ),
                        "output_schema": _p(
                            "object",
                            "Optional JSON Schema this child's final answer must validate against (told to the "
                            "child up front; parent validates with one bounded correction retry; result gains "
                            "schema_valid, plus schema_errors on failure - the child's raw text is still returned "
                            "as summary, never discarded). Keep it forgiving - require only fields you will read.",
                        ),
                        "images": _p(
                            "array",
                            "Optional images this child must SEE (max 8): local file paths or http(s) URLs - e.g. a "
                            "screenshot the user sent, a design mock, a chart. Vision-capable children receive the "
                            "pixels on their first turn; non-vision children get path hints for vision_analyze. Text "
                            "files do NOT belong here - put paths in 'context' instead.",
                            items={"type": "string"},
                        ),
                        "group": _p(
                            "string",
                            "Optional result-delivery bucket within this call (only when delegation.independent_completions "
                            "is enabled; otherwise the whole call returns as one message). Tasks sharing a group return "
                            "together in ONE message; ungrouped tasks return individually as each finishes. This does not "
                            "order execution; if B needs A's output, dispatch B after A returns.",
                        ),
                    },
                    "required": ["goal"],
                },
                "description": "(rebuilt at get_definitions() time)",
            },
            # `background` (bool) is also accepted - DEPRECATED, ignored: top-level
            # delegations always run in the background. Unadvertised; do not re-add.
            "action": _p(
                "string",
                "Default 'spawn'. Live control of running children: "
                "'list' = ids/goals/status/transcripts; 'steer' = queue "
                "course-correction text into one child (subagent_id + "
                "message) without stopping it; 'stop' = end one child "
                "early (subagent_id; partial result still returns). "
                "Control actions return immediately; goal/tasks are ignored unless spawning.",
                enum=["spawn", "list", "steer", "stop"],
            ),
            "subagent_id": _p("string", "Target for action='steer'/'stop' (ids from the spawn response or action='list')."),
            "message": _p(
                "string",
                "For action='steer': the course correction, appended to "
                "the child's next tool result mid-run. Be directive and specific.",
            ),
        },
        "required": [],
    },
}
```

Source: Hermes Agent `delegate_task` tool, `tools/delegate_tool.py` lines 648-766, commit `6a2662a` - source at commit, 2026-10-10, fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. With default settings the rebuilt `tasks` description reads "The task(s), up to 10 in parallel for this user (set via delegation.max_concurrent_children). Each entry spawns one subagent with isolated context and terminal session; a single task is a one-entry array. Required when spawning." and `group` is removed from the task items, because `delegation.independent_completions` defaults to false (`tools/delegate_tool_config.py`).

Semantics. Top-level delegations always run in the background and the model does not choose (the deprecated `background` flag is accepted and ignored), except that sessions without a later-result consumer, such as one-shot CLI and cron, join the children and return results in the tool call, and orchestrator subagents at depth above 0 also get their workers' results within their own turn (source at commit, `delegate_tool.py` lines 772-778). A background spawn returns at once with `{"status": "dispatched", "mode": "background", "count": n, "delegation_id": ..., "goals": [...], "note": ...}`, plus `subagent_ids` and a `control_hint` when children have ids and `live_transcripts` paths when transcripts were written, and the single-task note reads "Subagent is running in the background; its full result re-enters the conversation as a new message when it finishes. Results are delivered only after you END YOUR TURN: do anything that does not depend on it, then stop with a one-line status. Do not poll its transcript or artifacts to wait for it." (source at commit, `delegate_tool_dispatch.py` lines 324-368). The result arrives between turns as a new message titled "[ASYNC DELEGATION COMPLETE - {deleg_id}]" with the intro "A background subagent you dispatched earlier has finished. You may have moved on since dispatching it; the full task source is below so you can act on the result or re-dispatch if things have changed.", then `Dispatched:`, `Original goal:`, `Role:` and `Model:`, `Status: {status}   API calls: ...   Duration: ...s`, "--- RESULT ---", and the child's summary; multi-task units use "[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE - {deleg_id}]", and a child that fails while its siblings still run produces an early "[ASYNC DELEGATION TASK FAILED - {deleg_id}, task {idx + 1}/{n}]" notice (source at commit, `process_registry_notifications.py` lines 142-299). The `list`, `steer`, and `stop` actions run synchronously over the caller's own spawn tree: `steer` returns `{"action", "subagent_id", "status": "queued", "note"}` and the child sees the text appended to its next tool result, while `stop` returns `"status": "interrupt_requested"` and the child's partial result still arrives as a completion message (source at commit, `delegate_tool_registry.py` lines 264-310). Concurrency is `delegation.max_concurrent_children` (default 10, floor 1, no ceiling; a background dispatch at capacity is rejected and runs synchronously) and depth is `delegation.max_spawn_depth` (default 1, flat) (source at commit, `delegate_tool_config.py`); the tool was added on 2026-02-20 (`90e521112876`), gained background runs on 2026-06-15 (PR #40946), lost model-facing `toolsets` on 2026-07-01 (PR #56386), gained `output_schema` on 2026-08-07 and `action` list/steer/stop on 2026-08-13, and became tasks-only with `background` and top-level `goal`/`context` unadvertised on 2026-08-27 (PR #96424) (source at commit, `delegate_tool.py` history).

An agent built with `managed_agents=[...]` exposes each managed agent to the model as a callable tool named after that agent; the source and prompts call these "managed agents", "team members", and the parent the "manager". `ToolCallingAgent` sends managed agents to the model as native tool definitions next to its ordinary tools (`tools_to_call_from=self.tools_and_managed_agents`, `agents.py:1261-1263`, `:1293-1313`), and `CodeAgent` presents each one as a Python function stub in its system prompt. There is no background mode and no wait, status, or cancel tool.

#### `<agent_name>` (spawn)

Description (verbatim, system-prompt template for `ToolCallingAgent`):

```text
{%- if managed_agents and managed_agents.values() | list %}
You can also give tasks to team members.
Calling a team member works similarly to calling a tool: provide the task description as the 'task' argument. Since this team member is a real human, be as detailed and verbose as necessary in your task description.
You can also include any relevant variables or context using the 'additional_args' argument.
Here is a list of the team members that you can call:
{%- for agent in managed_agents.values() %}
- {{ agent.name }}: {{ agent.description }}
  - Takes inputs: {{agent.inputs}}
  - Returns an output of type: {{agent.output_type}}
{%- endfor %}
{%- endif %}
```

Source: smolagents prompt template at commit 96f33fa, `src/smolagents/prompts/toolcalling_agent.yaml:97-107`, shown without the YAML block indentation - source at commit, 2026-10-06 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The native tool definition's own `description` field is the managed agent's `description` string, which the developer must supply: `get_tool_json_schema` sets `"description": tool.description` (`models.py:318-329`), and `_setup_managed_agents` asserts "All managed agents need both a name and a description!" (`agents.py:373-375`).

Parameters (Python dict that smolagents assigns to every managed agent, from source at commit 96f33fa, verbatim):


Source: smolagents source at commit 96f33fa, `src/smolagents/agents.py:379-387` - source at commit, 2026-10-06 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). For native tool calling, `get_tool_json_schema` wraps these inputs as `{"type": "object", "properties": <inputs>, "required": [...]}` and marks an input required unless it has `"nullable": True`, so only `task` is required (`models.py:288-329`).

```python
{{code_block_closing_tag}}
```

Source: smolagents prompt template at commit 96f33fa, `src/smolagents/prompts/code_agent.yaml:144-154`, shown without the YAML block indentation; the lines before it (`code_agent.yaml:139-143`) repeat the "You can also give tasks to team members." text shown above - source at commit, 2026-10-06 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The tool name is the managed agent's `name`, which must be a valid Python identifier and not a reserved keyword (`agents.py:364-367`) and must not repeat any tool or other managed agent name (`agents.py:404-413`); the inputs schema shown is what smolagents generates for each managed agent. The call is blocking: it runs the subagent's `__call__(task, **kwargs)`, which wraps `task` in the `managed_agent.task` template, runs the subagent, and returns the `managed_agent.report` text "Here is the final answer from your managed agent '{{name}}':\n{{final_answer}}" as the tool result, with a `<summary_of_work>` block appended when `provide_run_summary=True` (`agents.py:868-890`, `toolcalling_agent.yaml:234-236`). The subagent's task wrapper begins "You're a helpful agent named '{{name}}'. You have been submitted this task by your manager." and says its final_answer "WILL HAVE to contain these parts:" "### 1. Task outcome (short version):", "### 2. Task outcome (extremely detailed version):", and "### 3. Additional context (if relevant):"; the subagent returns through its ordinary `final_answer` tool (`toolcalling_agent.yaml:218-233`). A failed call returns "Error executing request to team member '{tool_name}' with arguments {str(arguments)}: {e}\nPlease try again or request to another team member" (`agents.py:1492-1496`).

The Kilo CLI and the Kilo VS Code extension share one tool set from the kilocode repository, whose README says "Kilo CLI is a fork of [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), enhanced to work within the Kilo agentic engineering platform." The model sees `task` in every client, the shared-board tools `board_post` and `board_read` unless the board is turned off, and `agent_manager` only in the VS Code extension.

#### `task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim, default with `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS` on):

```text
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multistep tasks autonomously.

When using the Task tool, you must specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use.

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- If you want to read a specific file path, use the Read or Glob tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the Grep tool instead, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the Read tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- If no available agent is a good fit for the task, use other tools directly


Usage notes:
1. Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses
2. Once you have delegated work to an agent, do not duplicate that work yourself. Continue with non-overlapping tasks, or wait for the result. For background tasks, you will be notified automatically when the result is ready.
3. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result. The output includes a task_id you can reuse later to continue the same subagent session.
4. Each agent invocation starts with a fresh context unless you provide task_id to resume the same subagent session (which continues with its previous messages and tool outputs). When starting fresh, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
5. The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
6. Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent. Tell it how to verify its work if possible (e.g., relevant test commands).
7. If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement.


Subagents launched with this tool are internal to the current session and create no worktrees or interactive sessions. To start visible Agent Manager sessions, use `agent_manager` only when the user explicitly asks.

Background mode: background=true launches the subagent asynchronously and returns immediately. Use foreground when you need the result before proceeding; otherwise use background for non-overlapping work, but do not give the final answer until all required background results have arrived. You will be notified automatically when it finishes.

Subagent model selection is enabled. Omit these fields, or send null, to keep the normal subagent model and reasoning defaults. Only override model, provider, or variant when the user explicitly requests it. Do not choose overrides on your own based on task complexity, cost, or latency. Use agent_manager_models only when an override is requested to find available models, providers, and variants; do not guess names or use model knowledge from training. This does not create Agent Manager sessions. Resumed tasks keep their last model and variant unless overridden. A variant-only override keeps the resolved model. A model override does not inherit the parent's reasoning effort.
Available agent types and the tools they have access to:
- ${item.name}: ${item.description ?? "This subagent should only be called manually by the user."}
```

Source: Kilo Code source at commit fb7e96e, assembled from `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.txt` (byte-identical to opencode v1), `KiloTask.usageDescription` and `KiloTask.modelDescription` in `packages/opencode/src/kilocode/tool/task.ts`, `BACKGROUND_DESCRIPTION` in `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts` (joined with blank lines), and `describeTask` in `packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts` (joined with one newline) - source at commit, 2026-10-09 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The `- ${item.name}: ...` lines are filled at runtime, one per non-primary agent the caller's permissions allow, sorted by name; with the background flag turned off, the "Background mode" paragraph is left out.

```ts
    model: Schema.optional(Schema.NullOr(Schema.String)).annotate({
      description:
        "Optional subagent model name or qualified provider/model ID from agent_manager_models. Only set when the user explicitly requests a different model. Omit or send null to keep the normal subagent model.",
    }),
    provider: Schema.optional(Schema.NullOr(Schema.String)).annotate({
      description:
        "Optional provider ID from agent_manager_models. Only set when the user explicitly requests a provider. Requires model; omit or send null to prefer the current turn's provider, then Kilo Gateway.",
    }),
    variant: Schema.optional(Schema.NullOr(Schema.String)).annotate({
```
