Source (description and parameters): Qwen Code `agent` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/agent/agent.ts` lines 365-416, 811-894, 950-1042, and 1084-1089, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is TypeScript source with code comments omitted; the model sees the `baseDescription` template literal with each `${...}` filled at runtime, where `AGENT_DESCRIPTION_FIRST_LINE` is "Delegate complex, independent work to specialized agents for explicit parallel requests or broad codebase research that clearly needs more than 3 searches." and the `ToolNames` constants resolve to `read_file`, `glob`, `agent`, `grep_search`, `list_agents`, `send_message`, and `ask_user_question`. In the parameters block a line holding only `...` marks skipped lines; `model` is added only when user model grades are configured, and the team properties only when the agent-team feature is on. The text returned by `buildAgentDelegationSection()` for `${delegationSection}` and by `toolSearchBridgeSentence()` for `${rosterDiscovery}` was not captured.

Semantics. Top-level regular subagents run in the background by default (`run_in_background` default `true` since 2026-07-18, PR #7048; nested agents run in the foreground), and the launch result begins "Background agent launched successfully." with a `task_id` and the line "Its result arrives as a <task-notification> for this task_id in a later turn; you will not see it in this turn." (source at commit, `agent.ts`). The result then arrives as a user-role `<task-notification>` message with `<task-id>`, `<status>`, `<summary>Agent "..." completed.</summary>` (or "failed" or "was cancelled"), `<remaining>`, `<all-terminal>`, `<result>`, `<output-file>`, and `<usage>` children, from a queue capped at 20 (source at commit, `background-tasks.ts`). With `run_in_background: false` the call blocks and returns the subagent's final text with no envelope, there is no wait or join tool, `send_message`, `list_agents`, and `task_stop` take the same `task_id`, and the tool result is capped at 32,000 characters with the tail kept (`maxOutputChars`, `truncateKeep: 'tail'`). Built-in types are `general-purpose` (the default), `Explore`, `statusline-setup`, `review-agent`, `claude-code`, and `codex`; forks (`subagent_type: "fork"`) were added on 2026-04-14 (PR #2936) and background subagents on 2026-04-17 (PR #3076) (source at commit, `builtin-agents.ts`; forum or issue). The tool was created as `task` on 2025-09-08, whose schema at commit `d4cfb18f` (2026-02-21) required `description`, `prompt`, and `subagent_type` and whose description began "Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.", and it was renamed `agent` on 2026-03-19 (PR #2489, merged 2026-03-20, "for clearer semantics and better alignment with industry terminology"); `tool-names.ts` keeps `task: ToolNames.AGENT` in `ToolNamesMigration`, which the file says supports legacy names "for backward compatibility with existing user configurations" (source at commit, `task.ts` at d4cfb18f and `tool-names.ts`; forum or issue).

#### `create_sub_session` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn a fresh, independent sub-session (its own clean context and transcript) and run a prompt in it. Use to fan work out into a separate session - e.g. a self-contained sub-task you want isolated from this conversation.

ONLY available when running under `qwen serve` (daemon mode); it is not declared at all in plain interactive or headless sessions.

## Completion modes
- `first-turn` (default): waits for the sub-session's first turn to finish and returns its result to you. Use when you need the answer back.
- `sent`: returns immediately after dispatching the prompt, without waiting. Use for fire-and-forget launches whose output you do not need inline.

The sub-session runs the prompt with full tool access, starting from zero context - brief it completely in `prompt` (it cannot see this conversation).
```

Source (description and parameters): Qwen Code `create_sub_session` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/create-sub-session.ts` lines 229-283, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is a string concatenation in source, shown here joined.

Semantics. The tool is registered only when the session has a sub-session spawner, which the source says happens only under `qwen serve`, and the file describes the result as "a FRESH top-level sub-session (a sibling of the current session, its own transcript)" (source at commit, `config.ts`). With the default `completion: "first-turn"` the call blocks until the sub-session's first turn finishes, up to "the daemon's 5-minute `first-turn` ceiling" per a source comment, and returns "Sub-session <link> first-turn result" followed by the sub-session's text; with `"sent"` it returns at once with "created and the prompt was dispatched. It runs independently - this call did not wait for a result." The link uses a `qwen-session://<sessionId>` URL. Cancelling the caller's turn does not cancel a sub-session that has started ("it runs independently and is not cancelled"), and this file defines no companion tool for reading, messaging, or stopping a sub-session.

#### `workflow` (spawn)

Description (partial, verbatim):

```text
const WORKFLOW_TOOL_DECISION = `Execute a workflow script that orchestrates subagents deterministically.

**Only on an explicit request**

Do not call this tool unless the user has asked for multi-agent orchestration. A run can dispatch up to ${DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS_PER_RUN} subagents and spend tokens accordingly, so that scale has to be requested rather than inferred. It counts as requested when any of these holds:

- The user's message contains the word \`workflow\`; a system reminder confirms it when it does.
- The user asked for orchestration in their own words - run a workflow, fan out agents, orchestrate this with subagents.
- A skill or slash command that ran - invoked by the user, or by you through the Skill tool - instructs you to use this tool.
- The user named a saved workflow to run, reached through \`name\`, \`workflow('<name>')\` or \`scriptPath\`.
- The user asked to resume or continue an earlier run, which is \`resumeFromRunId\`.

Otherwise do not call it, however well the task would parallelize. Do the work in the main loop, or spawn a single subagent for one self-contained piece. When a workflow would genuinely be the better tool, say in one sentence what it would fan out over and roughly how many agents that is, then let the user decide - and mention that including the word \`workflow\` next time skips the ask.

**What a workflow is for**

Reach for one to be comprehensive (cover every part of the work in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before an answer is committed to), or to take on scale a single context cannot hold. Parallelism on its own is not a reason; work that is already one short sequence of edits belongs in the main loop.`;

const WORKFLOW_TOOL_RUNTIME = `**Runtime**

\`phase(title)\`, \`log(msg)\`, \`agent(prompt, opts?)\`, \`parallel(thunks)\`, \`pipeline(items, ...stages)\`, \`workflow(nameOrRef, args?)\`, plus the \`args\` and \`budget\` globals. Saved workflows are \`<name>.js\` files under \`<projectRoot>/.qwen/workflows\` (project scope, also surfaced as \`/<name>\` slash commands) or \`~/.qwen/workflows\` (user scope), plus active extensions' \`<extension>:<name>\`; \`scriptPath\` additionally accepts an active extension's workflow file or a path inside the generated-scripts root (\`$QWEN_CODE_PROJECT_DIR/workflows/generated\` - the per-project runtime dir, not the project tree); any other path is refused. Default \`max(2, min(16, availableParallelism()-2))\` agents in flight per run, which follows CPU affinity and container CPU limits (\`${MAX_WORKFLOW_CONCURRENCY_ENV}\`), up to ${DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS_PER_RUN} agents total (\`${MAX_WORKFLOW_AGENTS_ENV}\`), under a 30-minute wall-clock cap per run (\`QWEN_CODE_MAX_WORKFLOW_SECONDS\`) - a fan-out near the agent cap will not fit inside the default cap. Each subagent attempt is separately capped at ${DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS} turns (\`${WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS_ENV}\`) and ${DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MAX_TIME_MINUTES} minutes (\`${WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MAX_MINUTES_ENV}\`). \`agent()\` resolves to \`null\` when that admitted agent fails on its own - turn/time caps, model or setup errors, missing structured output, exhausted stall retries - for a bare \`await agent()\` exactly as inside \`parallel()\`/\`pipeline()\`, so check for \`null\` wherever you read a result; run-level rejections no later call could survive (the token budget, the ${DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS_PER_RUN}-agent cap, cancellation) throw instead. \`budget.total\` is the turn's output-token target when the user's message sets one with a \`+500k\`-style directive, and \`budget.spent()\` then counts every output token this turn, the main loop included. Every run hands back its runId, the script's path on disk (an inline script is persisted, so a resume edits that file rather than re-sending the source) and its journal path; read it before diagnosing an empty or surprising result. Runs appear in the background-tasks view and the \`/workflows\` dialog (live phase tree, token usage, cooperative pause/resume, cancel); \`run_in_background: true\` returns a run handle immediately in the interactive TUI and delivers completion through the conversation. Scripts run in a node:vm sandbox with no filesystem or shell access - all I/O happens through the spawned agents.`;

const WORKFLOW_AUTHORING_POINTER = `**Writing the script**

Before writing a script, load the \`${WORKFLOW_AUTHORING_SKILL_NAME}\` skill - the authoring reference: the sandbox contract, agent() options, \`pipeline()\` vs \`parallel()\`, verification and convergence patterns, resume, and a worked example.`;
...
```

Source: Qwen Code `workflow` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/workflow/workflow.ts` lines 170-260 and 1678-1691, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). Source comments are omitted and a line holding only `...` marks skipped lines; the schema has no `required` list because exactly one of `script`, `scriptPath`, and `name` is enforced in validation, and a name-only session drops `script` and `scriptPath` and rewrites the `name` and `resumeFromRunId` descriptions.

Semantics. The tool is registered only when workflows are enabled, which is opt-in through settings, `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_WORKFLOWS=1`, or the bundled review skill, with `QWEN_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1` as a kill switch and no workflows under a shell execution sandbox (source at commit, `config.ts`). The model writes a JavaScript script whose `agent(prompt, opts?)`, `parallel()`, and `pipeline()` calls spawn the subagents; the call blocks by default (`run_in_background` default `false`), and `true` returns a run handle at once in the interactive TUI only, with completion "delivered to the conversation when the run settles". Each run returns its runId, the script path, and the journal path, and `resumeFromRunId` replays journaled `agent()` results for the longest unchanged prefix of calls. Limits stated in the description are a 30-minute wall-clock cap per run, a per-run agent cap, and per-subagent turn and minute caps, and an `agent()` whose subagent fails resolves to `null`. A workflow `agent({schema})` call gives that subagent the `structured_output` tool described below (source at commit, `syntheticOutput.ts`).

#### `team_create` (define)

Description (verbatim):

````text
# TeamCreate

## When to Use

Use this tool proactively whenever:
- The user explicitly asks to use a team, swarm, or group of agents
- The user mentions wanting agents to work together, coordinate, or collaborate
- A task is complex enough that it would benefit from parallel work by multiple agents (e.g., building a full-stack feature with frontend and backend work, refactoring a codebase while keeping tests passing, implementing a multi-step project with research, planning, and coding phases)

When in doubt about whether a task warrants a team, prefer spawning a team.

## Choosing Agent Types for Teammates

When spawning teammates via the Agent tool, choose the `subagent_type` based on what tools the agent needs for its task. Each agent type has a different set of available tools - match the agent to the work:

- **Enforced read-only teammates** use the Agent tool's read_only option. This replaces the selected agent's tool surface with inspection and team-coordination tools, so shell and file writes are unavailable. Use them for research, search, review, or planning tasks.
- **Full-capability agents** (e.g., general-purpose) have access to all tools including file editing, writing, and bash. Use these for tasks that require making changes.
- **Custom agents** defined in `.qwen/agents/` may have their own tool restrictions. Check their descriptions to understand what they can and cannot do.

Always review the agent type descriptions and their available tools listed in the Agent tool prompt before selecting a `subagent_type` for a teammate.

Create a new team to coordinate multiple agents working on a project. Teams have a 1:1 correspondence with task lists (Team = TaskList).

```
{
  "team_name": "my-project",
  "description": "Working on feature X"
}
```

This creates:
- A team file at `~/.qwen/teams/{team-name}/config.json`
- A corresponding task list directory at `~/.qwen/tasks/{team-name}/`

## Team Workflow

1. **Create a team** with TeamCreate - this creates both the team and its task list
2. **Create tasks** using the Task tools (TaskCreate, TaskList, etc.) - they automatically use the team's task list
3. **Spawn teammates** using the Agent tool with explicit `name` and `subagent_type` parameters to create teammates that join the active team (max ${config.getAgentsSettings().team?.maxTeammates ?? MAX_TEAMMATES} teammates per team). Set `read_only: true` for investigation workers; pin a single writer to a leader-owned worktree with `working_dir` when code changes are required, then shut it down before removing that worktree.
4. **Assign tasks** using TaskUpdate with `owner` to give tasks to idle teammates
5. **Teammates work on assigned tasks** and mark them completed via TaskUpdate
6. **Teammates go idle between turns** - after each turn, teammates automatically go idle and send a notification. IMPORTANT: Be patient with idle teammates! Don't comment on their idleness until it actually impacts your work.
7. **Shutdown your team** - when the task is completed, gracefully shut down each teammate with ${ToolNames.REQUEST_SHUTDOWN} (`to`: the teammate name). ${ToolNames.SEND_MESSAGE} carries ordinary text only.

## Task Ownership

Tasks are assigned using TaskUpdate with the `owner` parameter. Any agent can set or change task ownership via TaskUpdate.

## Automatic Message Delivery

**IMPORTANT**: Messages from teammates are automatically delivered to you. You do NOT need to manually check your inbox.

When you spawn teammates:
- They will send you messages when they complete tasks or need help
- These messages appear automatically as new conversation turns (like user messages)
- If you're busy (mid-turn), messages are queued and delivered when your turn ends
- The UI shows a brief notification with the sender's name when messages are waiting

Messages will be delivered automatically.

When reporting on teammate messages, you do NOT need to quote the original message - it's already rendered to the user.

## Teammate Idle State

Teammates go idle after every turn - this is completely normal and expected. A teammate going idle immediately after sending you a message does NOT mean they are done or unavailable. Idle simply means they are waiting for input.

- **Idle teammates can receive messages.** Sending a message to an idle teammate wakes them up and they will process it normally.
- **Idle notifications are automatic.** The system sends an idle notification whenever a teammate's turn ends. You do not need to react to idle notifications unless you want to assign new work or send a follow-up message.
- **Do not treat idle as an error.** A teammate sending a message and then going idle is the normal flow - they sent their message and are now waiting for a response. When a teammate's turn ends, the runtime forwards that teammate's final text output of the turn to you automatically; if they also called send_message earlier, that earlier report is delivered too. There is no summary of teammate-to-teammate messages; ask the teammate directly when you need peer-collaboration detail.

## Discovering Team Members

Teammates can read the team config file to discover other team members:
- **Team config location**: `~/.qwen/teams/{team-name}/config.json`

The config file contains a `members` array with each teammate's:
- `name`: Human-readable name (**always use this** for messaging and task assignment)
- `agentId`: Unique identifier (for reference only - do not use for communication)
- `agentType`: Role/type of the agent

**IMPORTANT**: Always refer to teammates by their NAME (e.g., "team-lead", "researcher", "tester"). Names are used for:
- `to` when sending messages
- Identifying task owners

Example of reading team config:
```
Use the Read tool to read ~/.qwen/teams/{team-name}/config.json
```

## Task List Coordination

Teams share a task list that all teammates can access at `~/.qwen/tasks/{team-name}/`.

Teammates should:
1. Check TaskList periodically, **especially after completing each task**, to find available work or see newly unblocked tasks
2. Claim unassigned, unblocked tasks with TaskUpdate (set `owner` to your name). **Prefer tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones
3. Create new tasks with `TaskCreate` when identifying additional work
4. Mark tasks as completed with `TaskUpdate` when done, then check TaskList for next work
5. Coordinate with other teammates by reading the task list status
6. If all available tasks are blocked, notify the team lead or help resolve blocking tasks

**IMPORTANT notes for communication with your team**:
- Do not use terminal tools to view your team's activity; always send a message to your teammates (and remember, refer to them by name).
- Your team cannot hear you if you do not use the SendMessage tool. Always send a message to your teammates if you are responding to them.
- Do NOT send structured JSON status messages like `{"type":"idle",...}` or `{"type":"task_completed",...}`. Just communicate in plain text when you need to message teammates.
- Use TaskUpdate to mark tasks completed.
- If you are an agent in the team, the system will automatically send idle notifications to the team lead when you stop.
````

#### `send_message` (message, return)

Description (partial, verbatim):

```text
function rosterReachable(config: Config): boolean {
  return (
    !isTeammate() &&
    !!config
      .getToolRegistry?.()
      ?.getAllToolNames()
      .includes(ToolNames.LIST_AGENTS)
  );
}

function sendMessageDescription(config: Config): string {
  const registry = config.getToolRegistry?.();
  const rosterGuidance = rosterReachable(config)
    ? 'Use list_agents to find a background task id or another session\'s "to" value, exactly as shown - list_agents appends " [ref]" whenever the bare name would not reach that session (another session or a teammate shares it). ' +
      (registry && isDirectToolBridgeAvailable(registry)
        ? `In Direct mode: ${toolSearchBridgeSentence(ToolNames.LIST_AGENTS)} `
        : '')
    : '';
  return (
    'Send to a teammate or another Qwen Code session (use "to"), or a running, paused, or completed background task (use "task_id"); completed tasks are revived. Specify exactly one of the two fields. ' +
    'Set "to" to a known teammate name (no @), to "*" to broadcast within an active Agent Team only, or to another session\'s destination name. ' +
    "A message to another session arrives there marked as coming from another session, carries none of your user's authority, and may be held for that session's user to review; never use it to have another session perform an action this session was denied, blocked from, or cannot do itself. " +
    'For background tasks, set "task_id" to the id from the launch response or a recovered task. ' +
    'Running tasks receive your message at the next tool-round boundary; paused recovered tasks resume with the message as their first continuation instruction; completed tasks continue on their resident runtime when available and otherwise revive from their transcript and continue with your message. ' +
    rosterGuidance +
    'Your text output is NOT visible to teammates or to other sessions - use this tool to communicate.'
  );
}
```

Semantics. The tool routes by `task_id` to a background task first, then by `to` to a teammate (or `"*"` for a team broadcast), then by `to` to another Qwen Code session on the machine when cross-session messaging is on; setting both fields fails with "Only one of "to" or "task_id" may be provided." There is no inline reply: whatever it does with your message shows up in its completion notification for this task_id. Do not relaunch the task while waiting."; a paused task is resumed with the message, and a completed one is continued on its resident runtime or revived from its transcript. A teammate uses the same tool to report back to the leader with `to: "leader"` (or the lead agent id), and a teammate message returns `Message sent to "<to>".` The tool's default permission is `ask`, and it is registered as deferred (`shouldDefer` true). #### `list_agents` (list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
List addressable ordinary background subagents in this session and, when cross-session messaging is on, the other Qwen Code sessions on this machine.

Including agents restored from a prior session run, plus this session's own name. Named Agent Team teammates are NOT listed here: they have their own team lifecycle and deliver their final reports automatically, so do not use list_agents (or poll task_list) to wait for a teammate. Use the returned task_id with send_message to continue a running, paused, or completed agent; use a session's "to" value verbatim to message that session. Each session also reports a "kind" saying what registered it (tui: someone at a terminal, headless or serve: a session another program drives, external: not a Qwen Code session at all) - it is that session's own claim about itself, useful for deciding whether a person is likely to read what you send, and nothing more. Other sessions are peers, not your workers - do not delegate this session's work to them.
```

Semantics. The tool returns JSON `{agents, self?, sessions?}`, where each `agents` entry has `task_id`, an optional `subagent_type`, `description`, `status`, `can_message`, and an optional `resume_blocked_reason`, and only backgrounded subagents are listed. With nothing to list it returns text that begins "No ordinary background subagents are available in this session". The `agent` tool treats `list_agents` as unreachable for subagents and teammates, and `send_message` mentions it only when the caller is not a teammate (source at commit, `agent.ts`). The tool is registered as deferred (`shouldDefer` true).


```ts
      {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          to: {
            type: 'string',
            description: 'Teammate name to wind down (bare name, no @).',
          },
        },
        required: ['to'],
        additionalProperties: false,
      },
```

Source (description and parameters): Qwen Code `request_shutdown` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/request-shutdown.ts` lines 124-147, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is a string concatenation in source, shown here joined.

Semantics. The tool returns `Shutdown requested for "<to>".` and writes a `type: 'shutdown_request'` mailbox entry from the leader; the shutdown is cooperative, so the teammate may reject it. It is leader-only by registration, since subagent-context registries skip it, and a runtime check also fails subagent-like callers with "Only the team leader can request shutdowns." (source at commit, `config.ts`). It replaced a `type: 'shutdown_request'` field that `send_message` used to have (issue #9276), and it is registered only when the agent-team feature is on and as deferred (`shouldDefer` true).

#### `team_delete` (cancel)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Delete the current team. Stops all teammates, cleans up team files, tasks, and inboxes. Only the team leader can use this.
```

Parameters (TypeScript object literal that forms the JSON Schema, from source at commit 9763580, verbatim):

```ts
      {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {},
        additionalProperties: false,
      },
```

Source (description and parameters): Qwen Code `team_delete` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/team-delete.ts` lines 153-166, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog). The description is a string concatenation in source, shown here joined.

Semantics. The tool stops every teammate through the team manager's cleanup, removes the team and task directories, clears the session's team state, and returns `Team "<name>" deleted.`; if file cleanup fails it still resets the team state and reports that directories may remain on disk. A teammate calling it gets "Only the team leader can delete the team.", and with no team it returns "No active team to delete." It is registered only when the agent-team feature is on (source at commit, `config.ts`).

#### `structured_output` (return)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Submit your final answer as structured JSON that conforms to the provided schema.

CRITICAL: In structured-output mode, this is the ONLY way to deliver the final result. Call this tool to deliver the final result; the first call with valid arguments ends the session. Do not emit the final answer as plain text - it will be discarded. Use other tools (Read, Grep, etc.) to gather the information you need before calling this tool.

The arguments you pass MUST validate against the tool's parameter schema. If validation fails you will receive the error and may retry with corrected fields.
```

Parameters (TypeScript constructor from source at commit 9763580, verbatim; the parameter schema is the caller-supplied JSON Schema):

```ts
  constructor(
    userSchema: Record<string, unknown>,
    private readonly validateParams?: (params: unknown) => string | null,
  ) {
    super(
      SyntheticOutputTool.Name,
      ToolDisplayNames.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT,
      structuredOutputDescription,
      Kind.Think,
      userSchema,
      false, // isOutputMarkdown
      false, // canUpdateOutput
      false, // shouldDefer - must be visible so the model knows to call it
      true, // alwaysLoad - never hidden behind the deferred-tool bridge
      'structured output json schema final result submit',
    );
  }
```

Source (description and parameters): Qwen Code `structured_output` tool, `packages/core/src/tools/syntheticOutput.ts` lines 11-15 and 68-84, commit 9763580 - source at commit, 2026-10-10 (fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog).

Semantics. The tool's parameter schema is whatever JSON Schema the run supplies, so it has no fixed fields; a source comment says it is registered when the user passes `--json-schema` and that a workflow `agent({schema})` call passes a validator compiled for that one call. The first valid call ends the session and returns "Structured output accepted. The session will end now - do not send further content.", and the arguments become the structured result. The `workflow` description says `agent()` resolves to `null` when a subagent ends with "missing structured output" (source at commit, `workflow.ts`). It is always loaded (`alwaysLoad` true) rather than deferred.

The model sees one subagent tool, `new_task`, which runs a subtask in a chosen mode and returns the subtask's result to the parent. The README names Cline as the project "from where Roo Code originated".

#### `new_task` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Create a new task instance in the chosen mode using your provided message and initial todo list (if required).

CRITICAL: This tool MUST be called alone. Do NOT call this tool alongside other tools in the same message turn. If you need to gather information before delegating, use other tools in a separate turn first, then call new_task by itself in the next turn.
```

Parameters (OpenAI `ChatCompletionTool` object in TypeScript from source at commit b867ec91, verbatim):

```ts
const MODE_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION = `Slug of the mode to begin the new task in (e.g., code, debug, architect)`

const MESSAGE_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION = `Initial user instructions or context for the new task`

const TODOS_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION = `Optional initial todo list written as a markdown checklist; required when the workspace mandates todos`

export default {
	type: "function",
	function: {
		name: "new_task",
		description: NEW_TASK_DESCRIPTION,
		strict: true,
		parameters: {
			type: "object",
			properties: {
				mode: {
					type: "string",
					description: MODE_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION,
				},
				message: {
					type: "string",
					description: MESSAGE_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION,
				},
				todos: {
					type: ["string", "null"],
					description: TODOS_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION,
				},
			},
			required: ["mode", "message", "todos"],
			additionalProperties: false,
		},
	},
} satisfies OpenAI.Chat.ChatCompletionTool
```

Source (description and parameters): Roo Code source, `src/core/prompts/tools/native-tools/new_task.ts`, commit `b867ec91` - source at commit, 2026-05-15.

Semantics. Subtasks run strictly one at a time: the parent task is closed with the interim tool result `Delegated to child task ${child.taskId}`, the child starts with `<user_message>\n${task}\n</user_message>`, and there is no background mode and no wait, list, or cancel tool for subtasks (Roo Code `NewTaskTool.ts`, source at commit). The child finishes with `attempt_completion {result}`, and Roo then rewrites the parent's tool result to `Subtask ${childTaskId} completed.\n\nResult:\n${completionResultSummary}` and resumes the parent with no new user text (Roo Code `ClineProvider.ts`, source at commit). Tool calls after `new_task` in the same message are dropped with "This tool was not executed because new_task was called in the same message turn. The new_task tool must be the last tool in a message." (Roo Code `src/core/task/Task.ts`, source at commit); `todos` is listed as required for OpenAI strict mode but accepts null and is enforced only when the `newTaskRequireTodos` setting is on (default false). The built-in Orchestrator mode (slug `orchestrator`, renamed from "Boomerang Orchestrator" in v3.21.2 on 2025-06-20) has no tool groups, so it has only always-available tools such as `new_task` and `attempt_completion`, and its instructions say "For each subtask, use the `new_task` tool to delegate." (Roo Code `mode.ts`, source at commit; Roo Code `CHANGELOG.md`, official changelog). History: the XML tool `new_task {mode, message}` arrived on 2025-01-29, results returned to the parent from v3.8.0 (2025-03-07), optional `todos` on 2025-08-21, the XML protocol was removed on 2026-01-21, and "MUST be called alone" was added on 2026-01-27; no model-call alias for `new_task` is in the sources (Roo Code `new-task.ts` at `13de490c3b3c`, commits `466495512795`, `8de9337e63cb`, and `dc5e765e9cc2`, source at commit; Roo Code `CHANGELOG.md`, official changelog).

VS Code core registers `runSubagent` (tool id and `toolReferenceName` both `runSubagent`, no `copilot_` prefix), and the Copilot extension, which moved into `microsoft/vscode/extensions/copilot/` when microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat was archived on 2026-05-20, contributes three specialized subagent tools whose model-facing names are the `ToolName` values `search_subagent`, `explore_subagent`, and `execution_subagent`. The three extension tools are off by default: `github.copilot.chat.searchSubagent.enabled` and `github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.enabled` default to `false` (tags `advanced`, `experimental`, `onExp`), and `search_subagent` and `explore_subagent` exclude each other through `when` clauses on `github.copilot.chat.exploreAgent.enabled` (default `true`).

#### `runSubagent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.
```

Parameters (TypeScript object building the JSON Schema, verbatim):

```ts
		const properties: IJSONSchemaMap = {
			prompt: {
				type: 'string',
				description: 'A detailed description of the task for the agent to perform'
			},
			description: {
				type: 'string',
				description: 'A short (3-5 word) description of the task'
			}
		};
		properties.agentName = {
			type: 'string',
			description: 'Optional name of a specific agent to invoke. If not provided, uses the current agent.'
		};
		properties.model = {
			type: 'string',
			description: 'Optional model for the subagent. Format: "Model Name (Vendor)", vendor is usually "copilot". Only use to enforce a specific model.',
		};

		const inputSchema: IJSONSchema & { properties: IJSONSchemaMap } = {
			type: 'object',
			properties,
			required: ['prompt', 'description']
		};
```

Source (description and parameters): VS Code source, `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/builtinTools/runSubagentTool.ts` lines 52-59 (`BaseModelDescription`) and 131-157 (`getToolData`), commit cc3fec8 - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. `getToolData` sets `modelDescription` to `BaseModelDescription` with nothing appended; the description block is the template literal with its `\'` escapes resolved.

Semantics. The call blocks, as the description says, and several `runSubagent` calls in one turn run in parallel (source at commit, 32cdd274e832); there is no wait, cancel, list, or steer tool. The tool result is the subagent's final markdown as plain text, or "Agent completed with no output" when it is empty, "Agent error: " followed by the error message, or "Error invoking subagent: " followed by the message. A subagent can call `runSubagent` only when `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents` is on, up to `RUN_SUBAGENT_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` (5); otherwise the maximum depth is 0. Without `model`, the subagent uses the first available model in the custom agent's `model` list, then Copilot "Auto" when the `ChatConfiguration.SubagentsDefaultToAuto` setting is true, then the parent's model, and a resolved model other than Auto that exceeds the main model's cost tier fails with an error. The tool began in vscode-copilot-chat as `execute_task` with `prompt` and `description` on 2025-09-01, was renamed `execute_prompt` on 2025-09-27 and `runSubagent` on 2025-10-19 (when the line "Agents do not run async or in the background" was added), moved to VS Code core as `runSubagent2` with an optional `subagentId` on 2025-11-03, and took the `runSubagent` name there on 2025-11-06 when the extension's version was deleted; `subagentId` was renamed `agentName` on 2025-11-24 and `model` was added on 2026-04-09 (source at commit, 018376ae5a73, 733cb4be8c2b, 3d6a87160a9c, 13330e1420d4, cb7163e5ffaf, 11ac626791ef, 21ca4eb7b3fa, and 394d71b13c95).

```text
Launch a fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?").
Returns: A list of relevant files/snippet locations in the workspace.

Input fields:
- query: Natural language description of what to search for.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message. 
- details: 2-3 sentences detailing the objective of the search agent.
```

#### `execution_subagent` (spawn)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Launch an iterative execution-focused subagent that performs an execution-based task.
USE THIS INSTEAD OF RUNNING INDIVIDUAL COMMANDS WITH run_in_terminal EXCEPT IN THE RARE CASES THAT YOU NEED THE FULL OUTPUT OF A COMMAND.
Here are some examples of how it can be used:
- Run tests and filter the output to summarize which tests failed and why.
- Install all dependencies of a project.
Returns: A list of commands that were run, along with relevant excerpts of each command's output.
Input fields:
- query: What to execute, and what to look for in the output. Can include exact commands to run, or a description of an execution task.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message.
NOTE: In the subagent query, make sure to specify any restrictions or guidelines on running commands provided by the user earlier in the conversation.
For example, if the user instructs the agent to not edit files in a particular directory, make sure to include that instruction in the subagent query when relevant.
```

Zed's native agent shows the model `spawn_agent` and `list_agents_and_models`; neither has a feature flag at this commit, and `spawn_agent` exists only on root threads. Each tool's description is its input struct's Rust doc comment: `AgentTool::description()` reads the `description` field of `schemars::schema_for!(Self::Input)`, and schemars 1.0.4 joins the doc lines with newlines after removing one leading space from each. A third tool, `create_thread`, behind `CreateThreadToolFeatureFlag`, starts an independent sibling thread rather than a subagent; its description says "you will NOT receive its output and you cannot interact with it afterwards. Use `spawn_agent` instead if you need the results back."

#### `spawn_agent` (spawn, message)

Description (verbatim):

```text
Spawn a sub-agent for a well-scoped task.

### Designing delegated subtasks
- An agent does not see your conversation history. Include all relevant context (file paths, requirements, constraints) in the message.
- Subtasks must be concrete, well-defined, and self-contained.
- Delegated subtasks must materially advance the main task.
- Do not duplicate work between your work and delegated subtasks.
- Do not use this tool for tasks you could accomplish directly with one or two tool calls. For example, don't ask the agent to read a single file and return the contents, you can do this yourself.
- When you delegate work, focus on coordinating and synthesizing results instead of duplicating the same work yourself.
- Avoid issuing multiple delegate calls for the same unresolved subproblem unless the new delegated task is genuinely different and necessary.
- Narrow the delegated ask to the concrete output you need next.
- For code-edit subtasks, decompose work so each delegated task has a disjoint write set.
- When sending a follow-up using an existing agent session_id, the agent already has the context from the previous turn. Send only a short, direct message. Do NOT repeat the original task or context.

### Parallel delegation patterns
- Run multiple independent information-seeking subtasks in parallel when you have distinct questions that can be answered independently.
- Split implementation into disjoint codebase slices and spawn multiple agents for them in parallel when the write scopes do not overlap.
- When a plan has multiple independent steps, prefer delegating those steps in parallel rather than serializing them unnecessarily.
- Reuse the returned session_id when you want to follow up on the same delegated subproblem instead of creating a duplicate session.

### Model selection
- When the user requests a particular model or asks you to choose based on cost or capability, call `list_agents_and_models` first, then pass the exact `models[].id` from the native Zed agent entry (`is_native: true`) in `model`.
- Omit `model` to use the user's configured subagent model, or the parent model when no subagent model is configured.
- Do not silently choose a different model when an explicit model is unavailable unless the user allowed fallback.
- A resumed session keeps its existing model, so `model` cannot be combined with `session_id`.

### Output
- You will receive only the agent's final message as output.
- Successful calls return a session_id that you can use for follow-up messages.
- Error results may also include a session_id if a session was already created.
```

Parameters (Rust struct deriving `schemars::JsonSchema`, field doc comments become property descriptions, verbatim):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub struct SpawnAgentToolInput {
    /// Short label displayed in the UI while the agent runs (e.g., "Researching alternatives")
    pub label: String,
    /// The prompt for the agent. For new sessions, include full context needed for the task. For follow-ups (with session_id), you can rely on the agent already having the previous message.
    pub message: String,
    /// Session ID of an existing agent session to continue instead of creating a new one. Omit to create a new agent.
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "deserialize_session_id")]
    pub session_id: Option<acp_v2::SessionId>,
    /// Optional model override. Pass the exact `models[].id` returned for the
    /// native Zed agent (`is_native: true`) by `list_agents_and_models`.
    /// Omit to preserve default behavior.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub model: Option<String>,
}
```

Source (description and parameters): Zed source, `crates/agent/src/tools/spawn_agent_tool.rs` lines 15-60, commit 93d7456 - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description block is the struct's doc comment with the `/// ` prefixes removed, which is the string schemars 1.0.4 produces (source at commit, schemars v1.0.4). `label` and `message` are required; the rendered JSON Schema for `acp_v2::SessionId` is not in the sources.

Semantics. The call blocks until the subagent finishes; there is no background mode and no wait, list, or cancel tool, and a follow-up message goes through `spawn_agent` again with the returned `session_id` (combining it with `model` fails with "model cannot be changed when resuming a subagent session"). The tool result is the JSON `{"session_id": ..., "output": ...}`, where `output` is the subagent's final message, or `{"session_id": ..., "error": ...}`; errors include "User canceled" and a message that begins "The agent is nearing the end of its context window and has been stopped.", and can end with "\n\nPartial subagent output (last 3 messages, up to 4096 characters each):\n\n" followed by those messages (source at commit, `agent.rs`). `spawn_agent` is added only while the thread depth is below `MAX_SUBAGENT_DEPTH` (1), so subagents do not get it, and `label` becomes the tool call's title in the UI (source at commit, `thread.rs`). The tool began as `subagent` behind a staff flag on 2026-01-09 with parameters `label`, `task_prompt`, `summary_prompt`, `context_low_prompt`, `timeout_ms`, and `allowed_tools`; its instruction parameter was `prompt` from 2026-02-19, `task` from 2026-02-20, and `message` from 2026-02-21, `session_id` was added and the tool was renamed `spawn_agent` on 2026-02-20, the timeout parameter was removed on 2026-02-23, the flag on 2026-03-02, the description was rewritten on 2026-03-19, and `model` was added on 2026-09-22 (source at commit, acbb32d19fd2, 85c23d0d0bb5, e42dae588a93, 9304e02b9a2e, 66bdb116d002, 76c878ddc43e, 304951a18f3f, 12b786dffc39, 5089b3e147f1, and e5221fa2956c). PR #49741 gives the rename reason as "we both agreed spawn_agent was a better name for what this tool is doing. It still calls the right tool if you ask for a subagent, but especially if we move these to be running in the background, spawn will be a better name anyway." (forum or issue, 2026-02-20).

#### `list_agents_and_models` (list)

Description (verbatim):

```text
List the agents and models available for use with the `create_thread` and
`spawn_agent` tools.

The result may include external agents. The `spawn_agent` tool creates a
native Zed subagent, so its `model` must be an exact `models[].id` from the
agent entry where `is_native` is `true`.

Call this before either tool if you need to pick a specific agent or a
non-default model (for example, to use a cheaper model for bulk work). If
you're happy with the user's current defaults, you don't need to call this.
```

Parameters (Rust struct deriving `schemars::JsonSchema`, verbatim):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub struct ListAgentsAndModelsToolInput {}
```

Source (description and parameters): Zed source, `crates/agent/src/tools/list_agents_and_models_tool.rs` lines 12-24, commit 93d7456 - source at commit, 2026-10-10; fetched 2026-10-10 for this catalog. The description block is the struct's doc comment with the `/// ` prefixes removed; the line breaks are the source's own.

Semantics. The tool takes no arguments and returns the JSON serialization of `AvailableAgents`, or `{"error": ...}` on failure; the shape of `AvailableAgents` is not in the sources. It is added at every thread depth, so subagents also get it, and it has no feature flag (source at commit, `thread.rs` and `tools.rs`). The `spawn_agent` description tells the parent to call it first when the user asks for a particular model or for a choice based on cost or capability.

## 53 harnesses and features have no captured subagent tool

These products appear in the survey but get no full entry, because no model-facing subagent tool was found for them or because their delegation feature's tool was not captured. Each bullet gives one sentence of fact and its source, except that the 25 products checked only in shared collections of extracted prompts share one source statement.

**No model-facing subagent tool found (35).** These 10 each cite their own sources:

- **Aider** (open source) - Aider has no model-facing subagent, delegation, or background-task tool at commit 5dc9490b, and its architect mode is a code-driven handoff in which the architect model's reply becomes the editor model's user message (`editor_coder.run(with_message=content, preproc=False)`) rather than a tool call. ## Protocols define methods, not model-facing tools

A2A (Agent2Agent) is a wire protocol between agents, not a set of model-facing tools: version 1.0 (2026-03-12, with v1.0.1 on 2026-05-26) defines the methods `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`, `CancelTask`, `SubscribeToTask`, and `ListTasks`, plus push-notification configuration methods and `GetExtendedAgentCard`, and these replaced the v0.2 and v0.3 names `message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/cancel`, and `tasks/resubscribe` (source: a2aproject/A2A `docs/specification.md` and `specification/a2a.proto` at commit `12e9d2fbb9badfe98f8ab4f660697870eeb1940b`, 2026-10-07). MCP Tasks are protocol-level async handles for `tools/call` between an MCP client and server: spec `2025-11-25` defines `tasks/get`, `tasks/result`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/list`, and the notification `notifications/tasks/status`, and the final SEP-2663 Tasks Extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`) moves tasks out of the core protocol with the methods `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, and `tasks/cancel` (source: modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol `schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts` and `seps/2663-tasks-extension.md` at commit `c518f7a927cff918bce35d3522fcdb046d264d7c`, 2026-10-08). The model does not see these method names; a harness that uses either protocol maps them to its own model-facing tools.
